Founder Lab is a weekly build day for early-stage founders. Bring what you're stuck on — check in on what you're testing and what you learned, then get to work: office hours with investors and operators, and open build time with founders at your stage. Same day, every week.

​Who is this for?

​Anchor the Roadmap: Align on near-term technical unlocks and business milestones.

events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "How to Turn Trains Into Music" 🎤 Lecturer: Joshua Wolk 📆 Date: Friday, September 4th  ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Tribeca, Manhattan
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
Every dot is a real subway train. Eight hundred of them, give or take, form a small jazz combo (walking bass, piano, sax, vibes, brushes) that has been playing without pause for over a hundred years. On the platforms they are hot, screaming, full of complaint. This is the music inside the noise.  The harmony moves through a slow chorus. A note is placed precisely where the train happens to be along its route. Rush hour fills the band with held tones; at 3 a.m. the silences grow longer. Whatever is playing now has not played before and will not play again.  Share your location and the trains nearest you grow louder. The piece rearranges itself around your body. You are listening to a portrait of where you stand, played by the city you are standing in.
Joshua Wolk is a designer and engineer who leverages data to make art.
We'll explore:
* The music all around us in every day life.
* The science of sound design.
* Basic music theory as applied to locomotives.
This might be for you if you...
* Are a music enthusiast or have interest in sound design
* Are curious about music theory in a bite sized setting
* Are intrigued by the idea of finding the art in the ordinary
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "Freedom, Justice, and Democracy: History of the Reconstruction and Thaddeus Stevens" 🎤 Lecturer: Stephanie Townrow 📆 Date: Friday, September 9th ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Dumbo, Brooklyn
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
When the Civil War ended, the United States faced an enormous question: What kind of country would it become? Congressman Thaddeus Stevens believed the nation could not simply rebuild what had existed before the war. Instead, he called for radical changes to dismantle the South's old social and economic system, protect the rights of formerly enslaved people, and create a country built on a foundation of legal equality. This talk explores Stevens' bold vision for Reconstruction, the fierce opposition he faced, and why the questions he raised about freedom, justice, and democracy remain just as relevant today.

Stephanie Townrow is the Director of Interpretation and Exhibitions at the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy, a new museum she has had the privilege to build from the ground-up. A Ph.D. candidate in American history at the University of Delaware, she specializes in bringing the past to life through storytelling, artifacts, and the occasional deep dive down a historical rabbit hole. She has spent the last several years immersed in the world of Thaddeus Stevens and Lydia Hamilton Smith—and promises that Stevens was far more interesting (and important) than most history textbooks let on. She's excited to share some of the surprising stories behind one of America's most fascinating and fearless politicians.
We'll explore:
* The reconstruction of the United States post Civil War
* The radical changes that occured during this period which have led to the state of the country we live in today
* The role that Thaddeus Stevens played in shaping our nation
This might be for you if you...
* Are curious about unknown figures in our shared history
* Are intrigued by the steps taken by the government during the Reconstruction era that have directly impacted where the US is today
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

Session 3: Sales

This session walks participants through building a complete sales funnel, from attracting a stranger to booking a meeting and ultimately closing a deal. You’ll create lead magnets, landing pages, qualification questions, automated lead scoring, scheduling flows, and follow-up sequences using tools like Claude, HubSpot, and Calendly or Cal.com. You’ll also build systems for reminders, no-shows, rescheduling, and personalized post-meeting follow-ups so promising leads do not fall through the cracks. A major focus is measurement, including cost per lead, cost per booked meeting, customer acquisition cost, conversion rates, lifetime value, and payback period. By the end, you’ll have a live funnel that captures, qualifies, books, nurtures, and tracks leads, plus a dashboard showing where money is being spent or lost. Because the material is especially dense, the session may work best split into two evenings: one for lead generation and capture, and one for qualification, booking, follow-up, and measurement.

A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

Learn more at www.DanielStillman.com

A portion of the proceeds from ticket sales will go to the Ever Forward Club, which provides support programs and workshops to disadvantaged young men and boys in the Bay Area.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

A practical workshop on cold email, DMs, and writing messages people actually answer — from the coach who broke into the NFL with 450 handwritten letters.

In this workshop, you’ll learn how to:
- Identify the right people to reach out to — and find a legitimate reason to contact them.

Evan Burk is a former NFL and college football coach, author, and leadership advisor who built his career by learning how to open doors that weren’t supposed to be open.

Over the past two decades, he’s continued studying how relationships are built, opportunities are created, and a thoughtful message can turn a stranger into a mentor, colleague, client, or friend.

Evan is the author of Finding Intangibles and has worked with athletes, coaches, executives, and organizations across professional sports and business. In this workshop, he’ll share the practical strategies he’s used throughout his own career to reach people he didn’t know, and build relationships that changed where his career could go.

Stop the week from leaking. Build the system that runs everything that isn’t the product.

What’s covered

Create the operating system for a one-person company.

This session covers how to plan your work, use AI throughout the day, connect the tools you already rely on, automate repetitive tasks, and establish a rhythm that keeps the business moving.

What you’ll do

Map your operation

Identify where your time, attention, and money are leaking across your inbox, calendar, notes, follow-ups, and administrative work.

Build your hub

Set up one central workspace for your tasks, documents, projects, and roadmap.

Wire in Claude

Turn meeting notes into actionable tasks.
Draft updates and replies.
Plan your week with AI support.

Automate the busywork

Build two or three automations connecting the tools you already use.
Examples might include sending a new lead into your CRM with a follow-up task, or transforming meeting notes into assigned action items.

Add guardrails and rhythm

Establish approvals and limits so automations remain safe and predictable.
Create a daily and weekly operating routine supported by a simple dashboard.

Recommended stack: Claude as the central intelligence layer, Notion as the workspace, and Make for automations. The proposal recommends Notion for its flexibility and accessible free plan, and Make for affordable, multi-step workflows.

Other tools considered: Linear for product and engineering teams, ClickUp for businesses trying to consolidate multiple tools, Zapier for ease of use and a large integration library, n8n for technical users who want a self-hosted option, and AI-agent tools such as Lindy or Relay for inbox and meeting workflows.

You’ll leave with: A working operating system for your business and two or three automations already running.

About Sixfactors AI

Sixfactors AI is building a workforce-upskilling platform and learning-and-development brand for founders who want to build, not just talk about building.

Its sessions are hands-on and practice-first, with participants creating real working software, marketing systems, funnels, and automations during the session itself. ​Who is this for?

​The System

events.name: UGLY TALK X GOOD TALK: WHAT NO ONE TELLS YOU ABOUT BEING A MIDDLE AGED FOUNDER
events.description:
A small, facilitated roundtable for founders who aren't hustle-culture kids.
Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with real perspective on it, and a handful of founders who know what you're actually dealing with.
No stage. No audience. No pitching. 
Facilitated by executive leadership coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. 
Who is this for?
Being a founder takes commitment, sacrifice, and sometimes hustle. But the hustle-culture narrative doesn't match the life you want as you get older. You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You want a proper vacation. Maybe you have aging parents to care for. And a mission you still want to bring into the world. 

Why a Roundtable?
You don’t need another big networking event, or a poorly moderated panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x.

You need an intimate, high-trust, off-the-record room where you can get real with other founders, builders and entrepreneurs. 

A roundtable is one where everyone shares, everyone is heard, and everyone gets more than they imagined.

The Conversation
Conversations are the atomic unit of change. Our lives are built by the conversations we have, and defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off but never resolve. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot you keep putting off.
The ones we avoid most are with ourselves. The bargains we never renegotiated. The anxiety we can't politely ask to leave. The question we keep not answering.
The un-had conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground and gets more expensive. This roundtable is designed to create the space for the most important questions and conversations you’re facing right now.

Application and Curation
Admission is by invitation only - please complete all application questions so we can curate the group, optimizing for:

People actively building
Openness, Curiosity and Generosity
Commitment - people who don’t show up won’t be invited to come again
The Prework: 
This is a small room, on purpose, so we’re only selecting a handful of folks who are willing to do some thinking before they get in the room. Apply with your thoughtful answers to the registration questions.
The Format: 
Five rounds of conversation: 
Connection and Learning - so we know who we are and why we’re building what we are each building
Exploration: Sharing your avoided conversation with the group
Stories Vs Advice: Sharing stories to help each other through shared empathy, not problem solving
Asks and Offers: What’s something you need from the group? What’s something you can offer in generosity?
Closing Round - What you’re taking away from the conversation - what you’re committed to
The Follow Up:
Join a continuing conversation with the attendees, where you can share the resource you mentioned, ask that follow-up question, and get the support you need from a generous, growing community.
Your Co-Hosts
Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, and insists that you do too. He's an executive coach and facilitator who works with founders and founding teams on how they lead, communicate, and navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) and wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers and innovators.
Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, and lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, and came up as a designer and agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups.
About Ugly Talk
Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough “aha!” moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons and insights.
With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami, we’ve built a vibrant community of thousands of founders and industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.
Official Website: UglyTalk.com

events.name: Grave Misconduct: What is the History of Body Snatching?
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
💡 A smarter night out in NYC—fascinating speakers, craft beer, and real conversation. 💡
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
Join us as we unearth the dark underbelly of medical history and the 100 plus year reign of the body snatchers. Driven by a severe shortage of legal cadavers for medical training, professional "ghouls" built a lucrative seasonal industry by secretly exhuming fresh corpses from local burial sites.
 This illicit trade disproportionately targeted marginalized communities, igniting public fury and violent “anatomy riots,” including New York City’s infamous 1788 uprising. While families fought back with creative defensive measures to protect their dead, the grim business of body snatching persisted for generations, until modern anatomy laws and shifting medical practices claimed to shut it down. Or did they? Join us for a thrilling evening of true crime as we find out where all the bodies aren't buried.
James Henry is a NYC tour guide, a nine-year veteran guide at Green-Wood Cemetery, and a specialist in NYC cemeteries and burial grounds. He is currently working on a graphic novel about the global history of body snatching. He is also featured as a guide on Bowery Boys Walks & a guest on The Gilded Gentleman podcast.

We'll explore:
* How the history of modern medicine is built on the stolen bodies of the poor and disenfranchised.
* How for over a century in America, illicit grave robbing supplied anatomical demand until state institutions quietly took over the trade through early 20th-century 'unclaimed body' laws.
* How today, a new "Golden Age" of body exploitation has arrived, as unregulated for-profit body brokers capitalize on dismantled oversight and put a price tag on vulnerable remains once again.
This might be for you if you...
* Are intrigued by medical history or NYC history
* Are a true-crime fan or cemetery enthusiast
* Are curious about our shared, unknown, dark history
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

events.name: Spirits of Photography:Photographing the Dead Brings Peace
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
💡A smarter night out in NYC—fascinating speakers, craft beer, and real conversation. 💡
🍻 Craft beer included with ticket!
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
If a photographer told you he could capture an image of your deceased loved one, would you believe him? In the 1860s, many people did. Hundreds believed photographers such as William Mumler could photograph ghosts, offering what seemed to be proof that communication with the spirit world was possible. However, spirit photography also had its critics. The famous showman P.T. Barnum was one of its most outspoken opponents and even testified at a trial to expose the practice as a fraud. Despite these accusations, many Victorians continued to believe in Mumler’s mysterious “ghosts.”  During the Victorian era, society had a deep fascination with death, and photography became a way to preserve the memory of those who had passed away. Families often commissioned and collected postmortem photographs of their deceased loved ones. At the same time, photographers like William Mumler and, later, William Hope claimed they could capture the spirits of the dead alongside the living. For people grieving their loved ones, these photographs seemed to offer not only a lasting image, but also the possibility of proof that the dead were still present in the spirit world.
JR Pepper is a photographer, lecturer, author, and cemetery tour guide whose work explores the intersections of art, history, death, and the macabre. She holds a BA and MA in Art History, specializing in Surrealism and the history of photography. Pepper has spent more than 20 years working in photography, image restoration, and digital imaging, and has lectured extensively on topics including spirit photography and Victorian mourning traditions. She is also an adjunct professor of art history at Brooklyn College and a tour guide at Green-Wood Cemetery in Brooklyn. Her books include Buried Boston: America’s Revolutionary Necropolis and Buried New Orleans: The Resilient Cemeteries of the Crescent City.
We'll explore:
* How early photographers convinced people of the possibility of the supernatural
* How people responded to such allegations
* Current examples of 'spirit' photography
This might be for you if you...
* Are curious about the supernatural fascination during the Victorian Era
* Are intrigued by examples of the art form of photography being used in unique ways across history

events.name: Building Slack's Simplified Layout Mode
events.description: This event will be online on YouTube & in-person (New York City). The speaker & live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page & someone will come down ASAP. DescriptionSlack is a powerful hub for work & communication, but its dense & complex interface can be a barrier for users with motor, vision, & cognitive disabilities. To help more people use Slack effectively, we introduced Simplified Layout Mode on desktop & web. This preference transforms Slack into a single-column layout that is easier to navigate & has fewer distractions. In this session, we will demo Simplified Layout Mode & discuss its evolution from an accommodation request by an ALS advocacy group to a feature that benefits multiple audiences. Along the way, we'll share specific examples of how its design was shaped by our partnerships with disabled & neurodivergent users. Attendees will learn ... How to collect & synthesize feedback from different groups of users with disabilities over the course of a feature's developmentHow to collaborate with internal employee disability groups to get feedback & build momentum around a featurePresenter biosChris Xu is a director of product management of Slack looking after accessibility & design systems. Outside of product management, they have had a wide-ranging career focused on how technology & communities shape each other. They live in Brooklyn, NY & hold strong opinions about fruit. Lena Wang is a frontend software engineer at Slack working on accessibility & design systems. Outside of engineering, she's usually mid-side-quest - whether that's walking the entire length of Manhattan on a whim, running a Taco Bell 5k, or competing in a city-wide scavenger hunt. She lives in Manhattan, NY. Kaili Liang is a Software Engineer at Slack, working on accessibility & design systems. In her free time, she loves chasing new eats, diving into books, trying various arts & crafts, & traveling. AccessibilityThe presentation will have human captions [CC], not automatic captions. For ASL preferred speakers, learn about the Aira ASL App, & download it before the event. For the Blind & Low Vision community, learn about the Aira Explorer App & download it before the event. To access the online webinar for audio description, use the A11yNYC Access Offer to call, or simply inform your Visual Interpreter that you'd like that offer applied when you connect. For additional accessibility requirements, please email meryl@equalentry.com two weeks before the event. LivestreamYouTube Provided by Internet Society Accessibility SIG. Location detailsThe event is at 72 Spring street on the 4th floor. Everyone must be accompanied to the event on the 4th floor. Because everyone needs to be escorted, please arrive early or on time. When you enter the ground floor, a representative from A11yNYC will be there to provide elevator access. TransitThe building 72 Spring street is near several transit stops: 6 train Spring Street (non-accessible stop): 100 feetCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.4 milesB/D/F/M trains Broadway-Lafayette Street (accessible stop), 0.2 milesN/Q/R/W trains Prince Street (non-accessible stop): 0.2 milesCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.3 milesM1 / M55 Bus lines Broadway/Spring Street stop: 500 feetCabs & rideshares can let passengers out right near the building entrance. Finding the buildingIn Google Maps, find 72 Spring street. It shows the correct location of the entrance: on Spring Street, halfway between Crosby & Lafayette.It's also between the Glossier store & the Krewe Eyewear store.Inside & over the reception desk in our building 72 Spring st, it says Marc Jacobs. Traveling to the event?We recommend Hotel on Rivington or Crosby Street Hotel. AccreditationAll A11yNYC meetups are pre-approved for IAAP Continuing Accessibility Education Credits (CAEC). SponsorsThanks to Aira, AKQA, Deque, Evinced, Equal Entry, & Fable for sponsoring. Want to be a sponsor? Contact meryl@equalentry.com

events.name: Builders & Brews
events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). backed by Gates, Bezos, Bloomberg) Combined estimated private market exposure represented at Atlas Coaliton's events: $2.5T+ USD  Sponsors & Partners: Get full access to our alumni directory of 280+ verified past family offices guests - including family offices, institutional LPs, & hardware / frontier tech founders - through our WeTheAtlas Family Office & Investors Matching System. Search by investor type, AUM range, sector focus, & geography. Request warm introductions to any previous guest directly through the platform. Reach out to us at : team@wetheatlas.com WHAT HAPPENED AFTER OUR LAST SUMMITS This is not a talking shop. Capital moves in this room. $15M Raised - Twelve (SAF Carbon Transformation). An introduction made through our summit network connected Twelve - the company turning CO into jet fuel & chemicals for Mercedes-Benz, P&G, & British Airways - with the CMA CGM Saad family office. Result: $15M raised to scale the technology that's replacing fossil fuels with air & water. $37M+ in Funds LPs Investments Value Facilitated in 2025. Across our summits & coalition network, Atlas team facilitated more than $37M in transaction value between LPs & GPs of frontier & climate tech funds in a single year. 500+ Investor-Innovators Connections Made. Our events don't end when the panels do. Through structured 1:1 matching, post-event introductions, & the WeTheAtlas platform, our summits have generated over 500 qualified LP-GPs connections since 2024. Every number on this page is real. We don't count badge scans. We count capital deployed. THE FORMAT: BUILT FOR DEALS, NOT PANELS This is not a 3,000-person conference with a lanyard & a prayer. Here's exactly how the day works: 150 attendees. That's it. We cap attendance & curate every seat. Ratio target: 50% LPs & family offices, 30% GPs & fund managers, 20% frontier tech founders. Everyone in the room is either writing checks or building companies worth funding. Structured 1:1 Investor-Founder Matching. Every sponsors is matched with up to 10 relevant connections before the event through our WeTheAtlas matching system. You'll arrive knowing exactly who to meet, what time & which table number - no cold intros, no wasted conversations. 3 Deep-Dive Panels (Not TED Talks) Moderated discussions with founders & investors who are in the trenches - not keynotes from people selling you a vision. Topics this year:  Energy Abundance: Nuclear Power, SAF & the New Economics of the Energy Renaissance  From Bits to Atoms: Physical AI, Robotics & the Climate Resilient Infrastructure Revolution  LP & GP Perspectives: Deploying Capital in Vital, Frontier Tech, Resilience & the Rise of Secondaries  Old Money, New Frontiers: Foundations, Endowments & Corporates Are Funding Existential Resilience  The 2026 Portfolio: How Family Offices Are Navigating War, Tariffs, Reshoring & the New World Order About WeTheAtlas WeTheAtlas is the capital mobilization platform for frontier & climate tech. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. With $22B committed across 1,200 members (70% investors, 30% founders), the coalition hosted events in 8+ cities, share a monthly newsletter, conduct media interviews, & connect active frontier & climate investors through deal flow. Learn more: https://www.atlascoalition.com/ By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with the organizers of Climate Week NYC.

events.name: Leaders In Fintech - Evolution Of Agentic Commerce
events.description: Join leading AI & product executives as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. Drawing on experience scaling complex transactional infrastructure, the panel will unpack practical models for deploying autonomous agents, securing machine-to-machine payments, & capturing enterprise value in agent-driven markets. Andr Kerr is the Director, Applied AI Lab at American Express, leading the strategy & execution of AI-driven product development. With a strong engineering background, he focuses on integrating generative AI technologies to enhance customer experiences & drive innovation within the financial services sector. Sailaja is a Director, Product Management - Agent Pay at Mastercard, where she launches innovative payment products across North America. She partners with major tech platforms & issuers to scale tokenized solutions that secure & simplify transactions, & brings 10+ years of experience across fintech, banking, & regulation driving innovation in complex, highly regulated environments. Join our panel of fintech leaders as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. They will unpack practical models for scaling autonomous execution across complex financial ecosystems while prioritizing security & customer trust. 01From Recommendations to Transactions Explore how AI systems are evolving from advisory roles to autonomous decision-makers capable of completing complex financial transactions. Learn how teams are designing products that seamlessly bridge conversational interactions with real-world execution. 02Trust, Security, & Payment Infrastructure Discover how leading institutions build secure, scalable payment rails designed specifically for autonomous agents. We'll examine how leaders manage risk, balance authorization with autonomy, & ensure ironclad trust across machine-driven financial interactions. 03The Machine-to-Machine Product Playbook Examine the strategies & frameworks product leaders use to build, launch, & scale machine-to-machine financial products. Learn how to adapt traditional product management playbooks to meet the demands of an increasingly agentic commerce ecosystem. What's IncludedGourmet Light Refreshments - Enjoy a curated selection of artisanal bites & small plates, perfect for connecting with colleagues.Settle in for easy conversation & good company in a warm, welcoming space. With a thoughtful selection of beer & wine on hand, it's the perfect backdrop for winding down or catching up.Have dietary restrictions? To ensure we can accommodate your dietary needs, please inform us at least 48 hours before the workshop start date.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: a16z's new 'Machine Age' fund & AI hardware a16z just launched a $1.1 billion "Machine Age" fund, betting that AI's next bottleneck isn't models - it's the physical stuff underneath them: chips, memory, data centers, robotics. We're decoding whether this is a smart contrarian shift for a software-focused firm, or a sign the AI hardware trade is getting crowded & late. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: Rethinking Compensation - Smarter Ways To Invest In Talent, Not Just Cut Costs
events.description: Compensation is one of the most powerful levers CFOs have to attract & retain top talent & drive profitability. Excessive cuts force turnover & hurt performance, while overly generous pay strains budgets & planning. In this session, CFOs will explore how to redesign salary, incentives, equity, & benefits by weighing the tradeoffs that matter most. You'll leave with a framework for deciding when to invest in talent versus tighten costs, how to structure incentives that reward both short- & long-term results, & practical tactics for effective offers without overpaying. Schedule:6:00-6:20 PM: Welcome networking 6:20-7:00 PM: Panel conversation featuring prepared questions followed by audience Q&A 7:00-8:00 PM Continued networking around topics Refreshments & light food will be available. Sponsors:CTI, founded by former tax auditors & Big 4 tax professionals, helps businesses maximize tax incentives. Our expert team of CPAs, attorneys, & engineers have secured over $52B in credits, including R&D, employment, sales & use, & property incentives using advanced technology & deep expertise to drive measurable financial results. Libra Value Partners is a boutique valuation firm that provides independent, defensible valuations for tax/409A, financial reporting, & transaction purposes. We help business owners, CFOs, attorneys, & CPAs make informed decisions with confidence. Build Scale Grow provides fractional leadership that helps you grow faster, spend less, & avoid costly mistakes. We turn goals into priorities, solve problems proactively, & establish systems so you can stay focused on growth. Founded in 2016, the New York Tech CFO Group is a free community where high-growth finance leaders share practical strategies for planning, operations, & technology. We host regular in-person gatherings from casual happy hours & breakfasts to educational & networking events.

events.name: Superplane & Elastic - AI Agents That Build & Ship Code
events.description: Software factories are here. AI agents write code, open PRs, run tests, deploy to production, & respond to incidents - all without waiting for a human to click a button. Join SuperPlane & Elastic for an evening where engineering leaders, platform teams, & SREs explore what it actually takes to run a software factory: how agents ship code, how Elastic monitors what happens in production, & how SuperPlane orchestrates the full loop from commit  deploy to incident to fix. SuperPlane is the agent orchestrator that turns your tools into a software factory. Elastic is the observability engine that tells you what's happening inside it. This is an unconference, you bring the topics, we bring the structure (and drinks). Come with opinions about how far you'd let agents go.  Date: Thursday, September 17th from 6:00-9:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001 Some topics we would discuss: How much autonomy should agents have in production?Building the feedback loop: deploy  observe  respond  learnAgents that fix what agents broke - is that a loop or a spiral?What does "human in the loop" actually mean when agents ship 10x faster?Observability as the control plane for your software factoryFrom Kibana alert to automated rollback - what's your threshold?The trust problem: when do you stop reviewing agent PRs?Format: Topics proposed by attendees at the beginningSessions run in small groups (~5-7 people)30 minutes of facilitated discussion per sessionOpen participation & movement between sessions encouraged Schedule: 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Arrival, food & drinks, networking6:30 - 6:50 PM  Welcome + software factories w/ Elastic & Superplane6:50 - 7:00 PM  Topic proposals & voting7:00 - 7:30 PM  Session 17:30 - 7:40 PM  Short break7:40 - 8:10 PM  Session 28:10 - 8:20 PM  Short break8:20 - 8:50 PM  Session 38:50 - 9:00 PM  Wrap-up & key takeaways9:00 PM  ClosingAbout SuperPlaneSuperPlane Software Factory platform that transforms software delivery from a collection of manual tasks into an orchestrated, AI-powered production system. It coordinates AI agents, developers, infrastructure, & operational tools to build, test, deploy, & maintain software with speed, consistency, & governance. About ElasticElastic is the observability stack behind high-velocity engineering teams. With Elasticsearch, Kibana, & the rest of Elastic Stack, engineers, SREs & platform engineers get real-time visibility into logs, metrics, traces, & security events correlated in one place, not scattered across tools. As release cadence increases with the adoption of software factories, Elastic keeps you in control of what's running & why.

events.name: SOSV's HAX Deep Tech Showcase
events.description: Deep tech has always mattered, but right now, the tailwinds are stronger & more urgent than at any point in the last 40 years. Global demand & national security priorities are converging, making this area critical to the next decade of industrial & economic growth. As part of Climate Week NYC, meet 20+ deep tech companies driving that transformation - all graduates of HAX, SOSV's hard-tech program & the world's most active pre-seed investor for deep tech founders. You will meet Seed & Series A companies building critical solutions with commercial traction across energy systems, industrial automation, robotics, plasma, critical minerals, & advanced chemistry. SOSV's HAX provides hard-tech founders a 6-month collaborative residency, hands-on engineering support, & an initial investment package of up to $550,000. HAX has a flagship 35,000 square foot facility in Newark, with additional offices in Shenzhen, Pune & Tokyo, & expansion planned for a new facility focused on applications of plasma physics called HAX Plasma Forge in Princeton. This event is for investors only. events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Hugging Face - the hack, Microduck & acquisition by Nvidia Hugging Face's busy months - hacked by an OpenAI model, launching a $399 robot duck, & reportedly being bought by Nvidia for $12.9B. We're decoding what it all means for the future of AI. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. About Farzad, the host Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C.   About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Grids In Transition - A New Global Conference Series
events.description: The US power sector is entering a complex new phase driven by rapidly expanding electricity demand. While generation capacity is growing, the critical challenge is delivering clean, reliable, & affordable power to homes, businesses, & industry. This transformation is uniquely defined by surging electrification, the rise of AI & large data centers, the growth of distributed energy resources, & expanding heavy industry loads-creating unprecedented stress on the power grid.  America's goals for energy security, economic growth, & industrial competitiveness rely as much on grid modernization as they do on expanding generation. Grid capacity now often dictates where new generation projects & data centers are located, & how quickly electrification can scale across transportation, buildings, & manufacturing. If the grids are not strengthened faster, progress will slow down, costs will rise, congestion & reliability problems will increase, & economic opportunities could be lost.  Originally built for a different era, the US transmission & distribution networks are now operating near their limits, facing challenges including integration of renewables, bidirectional power flows, rising peak demand, declining system inertia, & increasing climate & cybersecurity risks. Grids must evolve from passive infrastructure into an intelligent, dynamic system that manages flexibility, resilience, & reliability in real time.  Meeting this moment requires urgent expansion & modernization of the power grids-a priority reinforced by the U.S. Department of Energy's Speed to Power initiative to accelerate critical grid infrastructure. With record investments underway, electricity grids must transform to support growing demand, manage emerging risks, & integrate varied generation resources more effectively.  However, grid transformation is complex, requiring close coordination among federal & state regulators, regional transmission organizations, utilities, technology providers, investors, & communities. No single policy, market mechanism, or technology can deliver this transition alone.  In this context, Global Transmission is organizing a conference on Grids in Transition - US on September 24, 2026, in New York City. This conference will place grids at the center of the conversation about the future of the US electricity industry, bringing together policymakers, regulators, system operators, utilities, technology leaders, & investors to examine how the grid must evolve to support the nation's rapidly changing power system.  Building on the success of our past grid & electrification events, this conference will provide a timely opportunity to discuss the challenges, trade-offs, & solutions needed for developing the electricity networks of the future. This event will offer vital insights & collaboration opportunities on the transformative role of grids in the American energy landscape.

events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.name: Co-Founder Matching - Find A Partner By Solving Real Problems
events.description: You don't find a co-founder by reading a profile. You find one by working: two hours, real problems, mutual matches only. You don't find a co-founder by reading a profile. You find one by working.   Two hours next to someone shows you how they think, argue & cut scope. A profile shows you nothing. So we don't do matching - we do work, & the partnership question answers itself.    YOUR PROBLEM IS ON THE BOARD BEFORE YOU WALK IN   After you book, you send us one line: the problem you're bringing. By the time you arrive it's already on the board with everyone else's. The room votes, the top problems get the tables - five people, twenty-five minutes each, one problem at a time.   Two minutes to explain it. Three minutes of questions only. Eight minutes while the table works on it out loud & you turn your chair around & take notes - you don't defend, you don't explain, you write. Two minutes for what you're taking away.   Halfway through there's a second vote, so the problems that didn't make the first round get their turn. By the end you've worked shoulder-to-shoulder with eight to ten people. That's a filter no profile gives you.    NOBODY LEAVES WITH NOTHING   Before we scatter, the host asks one question out loud: who still doesn't have an answer? Every hand gets the room's attention - & someone in it has the contact you need.    MUTUAL MATCHES ONLY   You mark the people you'd build something with. We connect you only when both sides say yes, within 48 hours. No cold intros, no lists, no awkward follow-ups to people who weren't interested.    ONE THING IS REQUIRED BEFORE YOU COME   A three-minute form in our Mini App: your problem in one line, some context, how long it's been unresolved. Only submitted problems make the board & the vote.    WHO'S IN THE ROOM   Solo founders looking for a technical or commercial partner  engineers & builders who want to co-found, not take a job  product & GTM operators ready for zero-to-one  founders with a team who came to unstick something.   Hosted by Andrey Krylow. He greets every guest at the door, seats you at the right table, & makes the introductions - nobody stands alone at this event.   WHAT'S GUARANTEED: a curated room, two working sessions, mutual matches within 48 hours. WHAT WE DON'T PROMISE: a co-founder by the end of the evening, or a room full of investors. What we promise is the working session that tells you who's worth a second conversation.   Three rules, said out loud in sixty seconds: what's said here stays here  we share experience, not advice  moving to another table mid-session is normal.   Registration required. Check-in through the Ascent Valley Mini App inside Telegram: everyone you meet stays saved, matched & reachable after tonight.   Ascent Valley - a founder & investor ecosystem across 21 cities. IDEA  PROCESS  RESULT.

Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

events.name: Convening The Next-Generation Materials Transition
events.description: The future of fashion depends on bringing next-generation materials to scale. While innovation continues to accelerate, turning breakthrough solutions into industry-wide adoption requires collaboration across the entire value chain. This Climate Week NYC, Eco-Age is convening the organisations, brands, & initiatives helping to shape that future. The Forum creates a platform where leaders can share knowledge, build partnerships, & explore practical pathways to adoption, connecting the people who each play a vital role in scaling next-generation materials. While global brands play an important role in leading the transition, commercial scale will ultimately depend on adoption across the wider fashion market, emerging brands to suppliers, material innovators, manufacturers, investors, NGOs, & solution providers. The Forum is designed to move that conversation forward & focus on commercial adoption, supply chain readiness, investment, sourcing, & the partnerships that can accelerate progress across the industry. Climate Week NYC is where global leaders come together to turn ambition into action. As one of the world's largest platforms for climate collaboration, it creates the ideal environment to build the relationships & shared understanding needed to move promising innovations beyond pilots & into practice. The Forum contributes to that momentum by connecting the people who can help shape the future of next-generation materials. Forum Partners Developed with & featuring voices from: Eco-Age - a purpose-led media & communications agency accelerating the fashion industry's transition to sustainability. Canopy - an award-winning environmental non-profit driving the shift to next-generation, forest-free fibres. Fashion for Good - the global platform for sustainable fashion innovation, connecting brands & innovators to scale breakthrough solutions. Material ConneXion - the world's leading materials insights company, connecting industries to the most innovative & sustainable materials available. Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) - New York's internationally renowned college for fashion, design, business & technology, fostering innovation, education & industry collaboration across the global fashion & textile sector. The Programme The Forum combines a keynote, structured workshops, & a networking reception. Through an invitation-based format & curated audience, participants will explore the opportunities & challenges shaping the next chapter of material innovation. The programme, speakers, & venue are currently being developed with our partners & will be announced in the coming weeks. Who Should Attend The Forum is designed for senior leaders in sustainability, sourcing, supply chain, & procurement across the fashion, apparel, & textile industry. It is built for the people inside the industry who are responsible for what gets made, how it is sourced, & what it is made from. Event Details 22 September 20263:30 PM - 7:30 PMFashion Institute of Technology (FIT), New York City Pre-register now for priority access & programme updates. Registration is open but subject to review. We reserve the right to cancel registrations from organisations outside this scope. We look forward to seeing you there.

Please complete this application form Submission Deadline: September 3, 2026 Finalists Announced: September 8, 2026 AWARDSCash prize of $10,000, plus packages filled with perks like coworking space, VC advising, financial advising, bookkeeping, & more! Additional prize & partner benefits will be announced soon. THE EVENTPart of a national series, the Women in AI Pitch Competition brings together trailblazing founders, leading investors, technologists, & community champions to showcase transformative ideas & support the next generation of AI leadership. 6 pre-seed to seed stage AI startups with founding teams that are at least 50% women will be selected through a competitive application process to pitch live & receive feedback from top investors & industry experts.   WHAT TO EXPECTAn Elevated Experience. This is not your average pitch competition - we believe in thoughtful, exceptional curation that honors & reflects our finalists & guests. That's why we take extra care - from opening to closing receptions, with elegant bites & drinks, to ensure your evening is both enriching & beautiful. Startup Pitches - 6 rigorously vetted founders will pitch their startups for 5 minutes, followed by 3-5 minutes live Q&A from our panel of judges. Curated Networking - Network with founders, VCs, & industry leaders in the room before & after the pitches. Insights - Get a front-row view into what makes a pitch land, how investors evaluate early-stage companies, & what separates an idea from a fundable business. Full schedule TBA soon.   JUDGES (more TBA soon!)Dennis ThankachanCo-Founder & CEO of Lightyear; former public-equity investor at PointState Capital & former investment banker at Goldman Sachs. Eduardo YnatyHead of GTM Eng @ Genspark, former Head of Solutions at Ramp & former AVP of Sales & Head of Global Solutions at monday.com. Mirit LugassiEarly-Stage Investor at Laconia Capital; Venture Capital Fellow at Included VC, former B2B Fintech Growth Operator at DueDil, & former VP of Customer Operations at an early-stage Edtech startup. Joy MarcusCo-Founder & General Partner at The 98; Lecturer in Entrepreneurship at Princeton University, former Managing Director at Gotham Ventures, & former executive at Cond Nast Entertainment & Dailymotion. Past judges in our series have included partners & leadership from a16z, McKinsey, Canvas Ventures, & Microsoft Healthcare AI  See What Happened Last TimeOur NY Tech Week edition sold out & brought together an exceptional room of founders, investors, & AI leaders View the event gallery. Hosted by:Oasis Collective is a San Francisco-based national 501(c)(3) nonprofit advancing women's leadership in AI & closing the funding gap for female founders. events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Brunch & Learn
events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. Her experience is specialized in the digital health space, & she enjoys building community & connecting people in the space. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.
