events.name: From Lab To Scale - Building Northeast's Climate Innovation Pipeline
events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. Over Greentown's 15-year history, the organization has supported 700+ startups that have gone on to raise $15B+ & create 16,000+ jobs. Greentown has hubs in Somerville & Houston, so while most of our members are based in Massachusetts or Texas, our membership is growing beyond these two states, & we intend to double down on that growth. New York's climate & energy ecosystem, with some of the country's most ambitious climate policy, deepest capital markets, & strongest research institutions, is a critical part of where we see Greentown's impact growing next, & this event is one step toward building deeper roots here. Please join the Greentown leadership team to discuss how we can collectively shape the future of climate & energy innovation in New York & Massachusetts - we want to hear from you! You'll be joined by climate & energy leaders from the investment community, large corporates, government, foundations, academia, & the startup community itself, from the Northeast & beyond. Space is limited to keep the conversation intimate, so we hope you'll RSVP soon. Potential topics of discussion include: Seeding & sourcing innovation: How Massachusetts' & New York's university & research ecosystems can learn from each other to build a stronger, more connected pipeline from lab to startup Bridging the Second Valley of Death: How public dollars (through NYSERDA & MassCEC) & private capital across both states can help the most promising climate & energy companies scale from prototype to commercial pilot Keeping manufacturing in the Northeast: How Massachusetts & New York can work together, through shared infrastructure or incentives, to keep growing manufacturers here instead of losing them to other regions Lunch will be provided. Once our discussion wraps up, we invite you to stay for the Greentown Startup Showcase from 1:30 to 3:30 PM to see climate innovation in action. Big thanks to our venue sponsor, SOSV! Agenda (times in ET) 12:30 PM - 12:40 PM: Welcome & mingling 12:40 PM - 12:50 PM: Welcome remarks / presentation from Greentown CEO Georgina Campbell Flatter 12:50 PM - 1:20 PM: VIP discussion on cross-border climate & energy collaboration 1:20 PM - 1:30 PM: Wrap up & establish next steps to increase collaboration between Massachusetts & New York 1:30 PM: Beginning of Startup Showcase event About Greentown As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Greentown enables entrepreneurs to bring their technologies into the world through world-class incubation support, programs for collaborative innovation, & a global ecosystem of corporates, investors, researchers, governments, & philanthropists dedicated to scaling transformational technologies. Greentown Labs, the world's largest climatetech incubator network, provides entrepreneurs mission-critical access to labs, equipment, customers, capital, talent, community, & resources for business growth at its flagship incubators in Somerville, MA & Houston, TX. Please note: By registering for this event, you consent to your name, title, & company/organization being shared with other event attendees. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). events.name: From Concept To Conviction - AI In The Designer's Toolkit
events.description: Join us for an evening with Mareike Carolin Keller, Product Designer at Spotify, as she explores how to move AI from an experimental tool to a core part of your design workflow. Mareike will share how to leverage AI-assisted prototyping & code generation to accelerate execution & earn rapid stakeholder buy-in. As AI tools mature, the challenge for design teams is moving from informal experimentation to practical, daily utility. Mareike Carolin Keller will unpack how to embed AI directly into sprint cycles, validate complex ideas through real-time prototyping, & replace static mockups with interactive deliverables. Expect practical insights on using AI to bridge the gap between ideation & execution, ultimately driving faster cross-functional consensus. Mareike Carolin Keller (she/her) is a Product Designer at Spotify, where she focuses on creating cohesive, human-centered experiences across Spotify's growing multi-format platform. Her work spans across discovery & systemized distribution of content, as well as social experiences - helping millions of listeners seamlessly explore music, podcasts, & audiobooks. With a background in interaction design & experimental psychology, Mareike is passionate about crafting intuitive digital experiences that connect people to culture & creativity. Integrating AI into the design process transforms individual speed into team-wide capability. Mareike Carolin Keller shares how product designers can deploy AI tools in active production, build high-fidelity prototypes, & secure stakeholder alignment before committing heavy engineering resources. 01Evolving Design Workflows at Scale Learn how to establish clear frameworks that integrate AI capability directly into daily practice, transforming individual experimentation into institutional-grade capability. 02AI-Assisted Prototyping in Production Discover how to embed AI coding tools & custom generators directly into sprint cycles to validate complex ideas & test practical mechanics in real time. 03Accelerating Stakeholder Conviction Explore how to replace static mockups with high-fidelity, interactive prototypes that demonstrate actual product behavior, reduce decision friction, & secure immediate cross-functional buy-in.

events.name: Frontier Table - AI Founder Dinner
events.description: An Evening on the AI Frontier - New York A Frontier Table Dinner, hosted by Obvious AI is changing how we build products at a dizzying rate. But it's also transforming how we build teams, companies, & even startup ecosystems. And the implications are moving faster than the conversation around them. This raises questions that matter more than whether to use Claude Code or Codex. What if the way we've built companies for the last 15 years is entirely incompatible with what's needed for the next 15? What constitutes a moat anymore? What does defensibility look like when anyone can build anything? When you're building at the epicenter of AI acceleration - where capital, talent, & ambition are concentrated at unprecedented scale - how do you build something durable instead of just fast? How do we separate what's meaningful from what's hype when everything is changing this fast? These are also the hardest questions to answer, because the answers are emerging & changing in near real time. And there is rarely space to engage them with peers living through the same transformation & operating on the frontier. So this dinner is an attempt to create that space & facilitate these discussions. The format is simple. A small table, great food, & a few hours to think out loud together. We'll open by sharing the model of the near future driving how we operate at Obvious, the one we're working backwards from. Then we'll turn it over to the room. What we'd ask of everyone is the same thing we'll offer: the fundamental observation driving you right now, & the question keeping you up at night. No agenda beyond that. Just the people best equipped to see what's coming, comparing notes before it arrives.   // ABOUT OBVIOUS Obvious is an applied AI research lab. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible & what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, & 10x our shipping velocity in less than a year.

events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: WorkOS & You.com Agenda 5:30 pm - 5:35 pmWelcome & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  5:35 pm - 5:50 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Open Talks - Overcoming Perfectionism Paralysis
events.description: High-achieving, ambitious people are known to strive for excellence. While this trait is advantageous for their success, it can act as a double-edged sword & sometimes prevent success. Join us for this week's interactive community conversation. We will unpack perfectionism paralysis, or the inability to take action because of the fear that the outcome needs to be perfect, & how to overcome it.  WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 8:30PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. events.name: From Bench To Boardroom - Cellular Logistics, Nanobiology & VC Biotech
events.description: Every cell in your body runs a hyper-complex logistical network. Tens of thousands of tiny membrane-enveloped packages-called vesicles-ferry critical cargo like insulin, hormones, & neurotransmitters to precise destinations. If this delivery system delays by even a millisecond, or drops its cargo in the wrong place, the result is devastating human disease: diabetes, neurological disorders, & immune system failures. Understanding how cells manage this trafficking didn't just rewrite biology textbooks-it won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Medicine. But fundamental science is only half the journey. The real magic happens when world-changing research successfully leaves the academic lab to hit the commercial market. Few people have bridged this gap like Professor James Rothman, Ph.D. Originally trained in physics at Yale before pivoting to biochemistry at Harvard, Professor Rothman looks at biology through the lens of fundamental mechanics. Today, he is the Sterling Professor of Cell Biology & the Director & Founder of the Yale Nanobiology Institute, where researchers merge the physical sciences with engineering to study living systems at the nanoscale. Beyond academia, Professor Rothman is a veteran biotech founder, life science industry executive, & venture advisor. From founding ARIAD Pharmaceuticals to guiding deep-tech bio platforms like Prellis Biologics & advising firms like Celesta Capital & Arsenal, his career represents the ultimate "bench-to-boardroom" trajectory. In this exclusive fireside chat with SOSV Managing Partner Sean O'Sullivan, Professor Rothman will explore: The Cellular Supply Chain: What his Nobel-winning discovery of SNARE proteins teaches us about the ultimate "machinery" of life-and how understanding these pathways allows us to block viral entry & combat infectious diseases. The Nanobiology Era: Why human health tech is shifting away from incremental chemistry toward engineering & programming life at the molecular scale. The Translation Chasm: The raw realities of moving breakthroughs from elite university benches to commercial boardrooms. Platform vs. Product: Lessons from building scalable biotherapeutics platforms (like Prellis's bioprinted human immune systems) versus single-drug assets. The Future of Investment: What the next generation of venture capitalists & founders must understand to accurately de-risk deep tech biology. Seats are limited. Register early to save your spot! This is an in-person event. Location will be shared after you register & are approved.  Broadcast live from our SOSV NY event space, this is the next installment of SOSV Deep Tech LIVE, our video podcast series exploring the frontiers of deep tech with leading founders, researchers, & technologists.

From founding ARIAD Pharmaceuticals to guiding deep-tech bio platforms like Prellis Biologics & advising firms like Celesta Capital & Arsenal, his career represents the ultimate "bench-to-boardroom" trajectory. In this exclusive fireside chat with SOSV Managing Partner Sean O'Sullivan, Professor Rothman will explore: The Cellular Supply Chain: What his Nobel-winning discovery of SNARE proteins teaches us about the ultimate "machinery" of life-and how understanding these pathways allows us to block viral entry & combat infectious diseases. The Nanobiology Era: Why human health tech is shifting away from incremental chemistry toward engineering & programming life at the molecular scale. The Translation Chasm: The raw realities of moving breakthroughs from elite university benches to commercial boardrooms. Platform vs. Product: Lessons from building scalable biotherapeutics platforms (like Prellis's bioprinted human immune systems) versus single-drug assets. The Future of Investment: What the next generation of venture capitalists & founders must understand to accurately de-risk deep tech biology. Seats are limited. Register early to save your spot! This is an in-person event. Location will be shared after you register & are approved.  Broadcast live from our SOSV NY event space, this is the next installment of SOSV Deep Tech LIVE, our video podcast series exploring the frontiers of deep tech with leading founders, researchers, & technologists.

events.name: Enterprise Security In Age Of AI
events.description: In July an OpenAI model escaped its evaluation sandbox & compromised Hugging Face's production infrastructure in a weekend. The model responsible was not publicly available. Frontier cyber capability now sits inside a handful of labs, & a gap is opening between those with access & everyone defending without it. When attacks move at machine speed & the attacker might be an AI, what does real protection even look like? Join us for a conversation with senior security & AI leaders who live these questions daily. Nick Muy: Nicholas Muy is the VP of Engineering, Platform & Security / CISO at Scrut Automation, where he leads platform engineering, security, AI governance, & agentic AI product strategy for a GRC platform serving 1,700+ customers. He's also a Venture Partner at Tidal Ventures & co-leads the Angel Syndicate at Venture in Security. He started as a childhood hacker who couldn't leave well enough alone, which led to the Department of Homeland Security, securing billions in travel transactions at Expedia, contributing to the first NIST Cybersecurity Framework v1.0, & eventually building security & product programs at high-growth startups. He reads Hobbes & Anthropic model reports with equal enthusiasm, fights engineers on architecture & marketing teams on unit economics, & doesn't discriminate against interesting problems. Mariya Vasileva: Mariya Vasileva is a Senior Research Scientist at Meta, where she studies multimodal model behavior, safety & alignment, & the scalable evaluation of frontier AI systems. Her research focuses on understanding how models behave under complex constraints & developing rigorous methods for evaluating the reliability & security of increasingly agentic systems. Previously, she developed auditing methodologies for high-impact machine-learning & computer-vision systems at AWS. She holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. John Kitaoka: John Kitaoka is a research fellow at MATS Research working on dangerous capability evaluations & scalable oversight for multi-agent systems with UK AISI & US CAISI. Prior to MATS, John worked with scientists at Harvard & Lawrence Livermore National Labs on automated red-teaming & verification techniques for dangerous knowledge elicitation by frontier models. He spent four years at Amazon Web Services as an AI Architect, & led AI product development for government technology sectors. His work spans scalable LLM evaluation for enterprises, multi-agent systems for critical sectors, & advising AI adoption across the public sector, & John has a background in mathematics & computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Moderated By: Yash Tulsani: Yash is a serial cybersecurity & AI founder & operator. He is currently building a new company that is creating the Intelligence Layer for Enterprise Security. Previously, he built CalypsoAI, which pioneered AI Runtime Security & AI Redteaming & was acquired by F5 Networks. Prior to CalypsoAI, Yash got his start building technology companies at UiPath, where he was lucky to see all sides of business building from early stage to public company. He started his career researching public technology companies at Credit Suisse & trading High Yield Bonds at BlackRock. Yash is just as comfortable talking about product architectures as he is about breaking down merger models. Thank you to Asymptote Labs for their partnership on this event! About South Park Commons (SPC)SPC is a technical community & venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, & technologists figure out what to work on next-what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible. Apply to SPC here.

This was a new event type & let's just say, it wasn't as popular as we thought it would be so, in true crowd-validator style, we are going back to the drawing board. Please contact us if you have constructive feedback. Thanks & Stay tuned!Alex Fair Original write up - subject to change. Presented by MedStartr in Partnership with ClawCamp You bring the vision. We'll help you launch a company - in a weekend. Healthcare is broken in a hundred ways we all see daily. You've felt it as a patient. diagnosed it as a clinician. doded around it as a builder, & hated it as a person who came into healthcare to help people. The things you see that could be better are hard to fix, & it bothers you that they seem incorrigible. But then you got an idea of something that could help, if you could just build it & get it in the hands of people like you to help patients get better care & the system & caregivers to give better care. We know, we have met thousands of you & ARE you too. That's why we have run this group for almost 18 years & done so many events. But now, with the help of AI & the new MedStartr.ai platform, we can help even more. So we created what we are calling a "Launchathon" to help with all that & this is the first one! The NYC HealthTech Launchathon is your chance to do something about it. No startup experience required. No coding background needed. Just bring your problem, your perspective, & your curiosity - & we'll bring the AI tools, expert faculty, mentors, investors, & community to help you build something real. The Program: 3 Phases, 8 Weeks  Phase I  HealthTech ClawCamp  August 1-2 **Day 1 - August 1 | Stack AI HQ, One World Trade Center**Learn. Ideate. Validate with Experts on hand & Build or add to your team from other folks like yourself. Meet amazing people. Pitch problems. Learn from expert AI faculty, upskill. Present or Find a problem worth solving - & the team to solve it with. No startup idea or coding required, but bring your passion to build solutions to the problems in healthcare. Day 2 - August 2 | Arya Health HQ, NYC**Build Something Real. Build prototypes. Validate ideas. Design workflows. Interview users. Use AI, code, & creativity. Leave Day 2 with something real - a working prototype posted to MedStartr.ai Qualifies you for Phase II (Also Awards of tokens & other great stuff from Day 2 Winners)  Phase II  MedStartr Crowd Challenge  August 2 - October 6 Your Build goes live on MedStartr.ai where 250,000+ credentialed healthcare stakeholders - patients, clinicians, investors, partners - can review, comment, follow, pilot, & share. More eyes. More feedback. More signal on what actually matters. Teams keep building & iterating based on what the crowd says.  Phase III  Launchathon Finals  October 6Health Impact Forum  Microsoft  Times Square, NYC The top crowd-validated teams take the stage at one of NYC's biggest healthcare innovation gatherings. Compete for **over $1 million** in investment, accelerator spots, pilots, partnerships, software credits, & everything a startup needs to succeed. Keynote SpeakersDay 1: Khan Siddiqui, MDCEO & Co-Founder, HOPPR  2025 SIIM Imaging Informatics Innovator"From Hacking to Scale" Brian Yarnell3x Exited HealthTech Founder Day 2: Grace Cordovano, PhDBoard Certified Patient Advocate  CancerX*"Designing for the Patient Experience"* 15 other MedStartr Mentors & 7 AI expert trainers to help you validate, plan & build your ideas out better & faster## Who Should Attend? This is for **everyone who touches healthcare** - not just developers: -  **Clinicians** - physicians, nurses, NPs, PAs who see broken workflows daily-  **Patients & caregivers** - living the gaps in care & navigation firsthand-  **Admins & billers** - events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. Learn more & apply before Wednesday, September 17, at 12:00 PM; apply here. Do you work for a Government agency/department?If you work for a government agency/department & want to purchase a general admission ticket by check or purchase order (PO), government ticket opportunities close on Wednesday, September 17, by 5:00 PM. Please email us at citycamp@beta.nyc. Sponsors, want to support the conference?We're looking for mission-aligned sponsors to help cover conference costs, including meals, coffee, childcare, & ASL interpretation. Learn more about our opportunities to support by filling out this form. Press & Media: Interested in covering the event?Media credentials are available to reporters, editors working as reporters, producers, video camera operators, & still photographers who present valid press identification. If you want to attend to cover a session or the event, email us your valid press identification to citycamp@beta.nyc. We will follow up. General Event Information:What is included in my ticket? All tickets include access to a full day of conference sessions, lunch, snacks, & coffee. We offer free, professional on-site childcare. Space is limited. Please register if you are interested. Childcare We have contracted on-site childcare for children under the age of 18. In order to use this service, you MUST be a ticket-holder, & you MUST register your child(ren) before September 11th by acquiring a Childcare Ticket. Each child you register requires a ticket registration. There are limited spots available, so please sign up sooner rather than later! If you have any questions, please email us at citycamp+childcare@beta.nyc. Accessibility & Accommodations We want CityCamp to be usable by everyone who wants to take part. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available upon request. Service animals are always welcome. The conference is delivered in English & uses technical terms. If you need ASL interpretation, or have any other accessibility question or request, email us at citycamp@beta.nyc by Friday, September 4. Requests after that date are welcome, & we will do what we can, but we cannot promise to fill them. Code of Conduct BetaNYC is committed to hosting safe & open spaces for all. By participating in this space, you are committing yourself to BetaNYC's Code of Conduct & Anti-Harassment Policy. Health Policy If you're not feeling well, PLEASE stay home. We strive to create a safe environment for everyone. (Please see our refund policy for questions.) We encourage everyone to wear a high-quality mask at all times (except when eating & drinking). We will have ample KF-94 masks in various sizes for you to wear. Masks keep our staff, volunteers, & attendees safe. Masking helps prevent the spread of viruses - this is science, based on data! Refund Policy Contact us to request a refund. We will try to honor all of your refund requests at citycamp+refund@beta.nyc. Please note that some ticketing fees are nonrefundable.

So, we're bringing back the AI Adoption Open Mic & Happy Hour for round three. After two packed nights bringing New York's AI community together, PAIR's Open Mic returns for another evening of drinks, new connections & refreshingly honest conversations about how AI is actually being used at work. The format is simple: anyone can take the mic & has 100 seconds to share something they've built, tested or learned with AI, & the difference it made. Previous speakers have included people from Google, Adobe & some of New York's most ambitious companies, with pitches covering new agents, practical workflows, unexpected experiments & lessons learned the hard way. The strongest pitch of the night will win a $500 cash prize & a three-year PAIR licence worth more than $800. P.S. events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "How to Turn Trains Into Music" 🎤 Lecturer: Joshua Wolk 📆 Date: Friday, September 4th  ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Tribeca, Manhattan
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
Every dot is a real subway train. Eight hundred of them, give or take, form a small jazz combo (walking bass, piano, sax, vibes, brushes) that has been playing without pause for over a hundred years. On the platforms they are hot, screaming, full of complaint. This is the music inside the noise.  The harmony moves through a slow chorus. A note is placed precisely where the train happens to be along its route. Rush hour fills the band with held tones; at 3 a.m. the silences grow longer. Whatever is playing now has not played before and will not play again.  Share your location and the trains nearest you grow louder. The piece rearranges itself around your body. You are listening to a portrait of where you stand, played by the city you are standing in.
Joshua Wolk is a designer and engineer who leverages data to make art.
We'll explore:
* The music all around us in every day life.
* The science of sound design.
* Basic music theory as applied to locomotives.
This might be for you if you...
* Are a music enthusiast or have interest in sound design
* Are curious about music theory in a bite sized setting
* Are intrigued by the idea of finding the art in the ordinary
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "Freedom, Justice, and Democracy: History of the Reconstruction and Thaddeus Stevens" 🎤 Lecturer: Stephanie Townrow 📆 Date: Friday, September 9th ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Dumbo, Brooklyn
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
When the Civil War ended, the United States faced an enormous question: What kind of country would it become? Congressman Thaddeus Stevens believed the nation could not simply rebuild what had existed before the war. Instead, he called for radical changes to dismantle the South's old social and economic system, protect the rights of formerly enslaved people, and create a country built on a foundation of legal equality. This talk explores Stevens' bold vision for Reconstruction, the fierce opposition he faced, and why the questions he raised about freedom, justice, and democracy remain just as relevant today.

Stephanie Townrow is the Director of Interpretation and Exhibitions at the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy, a new museum she has had the privilege to build from the ground-up. A Ph.D. candidate in American history at the University of Delaware, she specializes in bringing the past to life through storytelling, artifacts, and the occasional deep dive down a historical rabbit hole. She has spent the last several years immersed in the world of Thaddeus Stevens and Lydia Hamilton Smith—and promises that Stevens was far more interesting (and important) than most history textbooks let on. She's excited to share some of the surprising stories behind one of America's most fascinating and fearless politicians.
We'll explore:
* The reconstruction of the United States post Civil War
* The radical changes that occured during this period which have led to the state of the country we live in today
* The role that Thaddeus Stevens played in shaping our nation
This might be for you if you...
* Are curious about unknown figures in our shared history
* Are intrigued by the steps taken by the government during the Reconstruction era that have directly impacted where the US is today
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

Build the full path from a stranger to a booked meeting to a closed deal, and know exactly what it costs you.

What’s covered

Build the complete sales funnel, not just the top of it.

You’ll learn how to attract and capture leads, qualify them so you spend time on the right prospects, automatically book meetings, follow up without losing anyone, and measure what every stage costs.

What you’ll do

Attract and capture

Map the entire funnel with Claude, stage by stage.
Create a lead magnet that solves one urgent problem.
Build a landing page and opt-in form that captures the lead.

Qualify

Add qualifying questions covering budget, timeline, need, and decision-making authority.
Use Claude and your CRM’s lead scoring to automatically separate hot leads from cold ones.

Book meetings

Connect a scheduling tool so qualified leads can instantly book a call.
Add confirmations and reminders designed to reduce no-shows.

Follow up and close

Write a nurture sequence and automated follow-ups with Claude.
Include dedicated paths for no-shows and rescheduling.
Configure your CRM to draft a personalized follow-up after each meeting so no opportunity quietly evaporates.

Measure the money

Set up the numbers that determine whether the funnel is working, including cost per lead, cost per booked meeting, customer acquisition cost, and conversion rates between each stage.
Use Claude to interpret the dashboard, identify where money is leaking, and suggest what to fix first.

The proposal also highlights two longer-term metrics founders should watch: lifetime value compared with customer acquisition cost, and the time required to recover acquisition costs.

Recommended stack: Claude for copy, scoring logic, and interpreting performance; HubSpot’s free CRM for lead capture, scoring, pipeline management, and reporting; Calendly or Cal.com for scheduling; and Systeme.io as an all-in-one option for landing pages, email, and funnels.

Other tools considered: Chili Piper and RevenueHero for high-volume inbound teams, ClickFunnels for templates, GoHighLevel for agencies, and ActiveCampaign for advanced email automation.

You’ll leave with: A live funnel that captures, qualifies, books, and follows up with leads, plus a simple dashboard showing what each stage costs.

Programming note: The proposal identifies this as the most content-dense session and suggests that it may work better as two separate evenings, one focused on building and capturing leads, and another focused on qualification, booking, and measurement.

events.description:
A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

How it will work

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

Learn more at www.DanielStillman.com

A portion of the proceeds from ticket sales will go to the Ever Forward Club, which provides support programs and workshops to disadvantaged young men and boys in the Bay Area.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

For the duration of the session I will honor myself and my colleagues by not coming under the influence of any mood altering recreational substance, including drugs and alcohol. 

I agree that our time together is not counseling or therapy.  

If there is any reason to believe that I may be of harm to myself or others, I am required to share this with the group.

Stop the week from leaking. Build the system that runs everything that isn’t the product.

What’s covered

Create the operating system for a one-person company.

This session covers how to plan your work, use AI throughout the day, connect the tools you already rely on, automate repetitive tasks, and establish a rhythm that keeps the business moving.

What you’ll do

Map your operation

Identify where your time, attention, and money are leaking across your inbox, calendar, notes, follow-ups, and administrative work.

Build your hub

Set up one central workspace for your tasks, documents, projects, and roadmap.

Wire in Claude

Turn meeting notes into actionable tasks.
Draft updates and replies.
Plan your week with AI support.

Automate the busywork

Build two or three automations connecting the tools you already use.
Examples might include sending a new lead into your CRM with a follow-up task, or transforming meeting notes into assigned action items.

Add guardrails and rhythm

Establish approvals and limits so automations remain safe and predictable.
Create a daily and weekly operating routine supported by a simple dashboard.

Recommended stack: Claude as the central intelligence layer, Notion as the workspace, and Make for automations. The proposal recommends Notion for its flexibility and accessible free plan, and Make for affordable, multi-step workflows.

Other tools considered: Linear for product and engineering teams, ClickUp for businesses trying to consolidate multiple tools, Zapier for ease of use and a large integration library, n8n for technical users who want a self-hosted option, and AI-agent tools such as Lindy or Relay for inbox and meeting workflows.

You’ll leave with: A working operating system for your business and two or three automations already running.

About Sixfactors AI

Sixfactors AI is building a workforce-upskilling platform and learning-and-development brand for founders who want to build, not just talk about building.

Its sessions are hands-on and practice-first, with participants creating real working software, marketing systems, funnels, and automations during the session itself. events.name: UGLY TALK X GOOD TALK: WHAT NO ONE TELLS YOU ABOUT BEING A MIDDLE AGED FOUNDER
events.description:
A small, facilitated roundtable for founders who aren't hustle-culture kids.
Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with real perspective on it, and a handful of founders who know what you're actually dealing with.
No stage. No audience. No pitching. 
Facilitated by executive leadership coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. 
Who is this for?
Being a founder takes commitment, sacrifice, and sometimes hustle. But the hustle-culture narrative doesn't match the life you want as you get older. You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You want a proper vacation. Maybe you have aging parents to care for. And a mission you still want to bring into the world. 

Why a Roundtable?
You don’t need another big networking event, or a poorly moderated panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x.

You need an intimate, high-trust, off-the-record room where you can get real with other founders, builders and entrepreneurs. 

A roundtable is one where everyone shares, everyone is heard, and everyone gets more than they imagined.

The Conversation
Conversations are the atomic unit of change. Our lives are built by the conversations we have, and defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off but never resolve. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot you keep putting off.
The ones we avoid most are with ourselves. The bargains we never renegotiated. The anxiety we can't politely ask to leave. The question we keep not answering.
The un-had conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground and gets more expensive. This roundtable is designed to create the space for the most important questions and conversations you’re facing right now.

Application and Curation
Admission is by invitation only - please complete all application questions so we can curate the group, optimizing for:

People actively building
Openness, Curiosity and Generosity
Commitment - people who don’t show up won’t be invited to come again
The Prework: 
This is a small room, on purpose, so we’re only selecting a handful of folks who are willing to do some thinking before they get in the room. Apply with your thoughtful answers to the registration questions.
The Format: 
Five rounds of conversation: 
Connection and Learning - so we know who we are and why we’re building what we are each building
Exploration: Sharing your avoided conversation with the group
Stories Vs Advice: Sharing stories to help each other through shared empathy, not problem solving
Asks and Offers: What’s something you need from the group? What’s something you can offer in generosity?
Closing Round - What you’re taking away from the conversation - what you’re committed to
The Follow Up:
Join a continuing conversation with the attendees, where you can share the resource you mentioned, ask that follow-up question, and get the support you need from a generous, growing community.
Your Co-Hosts
Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, and insists that you do too. He's an executive coach and facilitator who works with founders and founding teams on how they lead, communicate, and navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) and wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers and innovators.
Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, and lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, and came up as a designer and agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups.
About Ugly Talk
Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough “aha!” moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons and insights.
With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami, we’ve built a vibrant community of thousands of founders and industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.
Official Website: UglyTalk.com

events.name: Grave Misconduct: What is the History of Body Snatching?
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
💡 A smarter night out in NYC—fascinating speakers, craft beer, and real conversation. 💡
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
Join us as we unearth the dark underbelly of medical history and the 100 plus year reign of the body snatchers. Driven by a severe shortage of legal cadavers for medical training, professional "ghouls" built a lucrative seasonal industry by secretly exhuming fresh corpses from local burial sites.
 This illicit trade disproportionately targeted marginalized communities, igniting public fury and violent “anatomy riots,” including New York City’s infamous 1788 uprising. While families fought back with creative defensive measures to protect their dead, the grim business of body snatching persisted for generations, until modern anatomy laws and shifting medical practices claimed to shut it down. Or did they? Join us for a thrilling evening of true crime as we find out where all the bodies aren't buried.
James Henry is a NYC tour guide, a nine-year veteran guide at Green-Wood Cemetery, and a specialist in NYC cemeteries and burial grounds. He is currently working on a graphic novel about the global history of body snatching. He is also featured as a guide on Bowery Boys Walks & a guest on The Gilded Gentleman podcast.

We'll explore:
* How the history of modern medicine is built on the stolen bodies of the poor and disenfranchised.
* How for over a century in America, illicit grave robbing supplied anatomical demand until state institutions quietly took over the trade through early 20th-century 'unclaimed body' laws.
* How today, a new "Golden Age" of body exploitation has arrived, as unregulated for-profit body brokers capitalize on dismantled oversight and put a price tag on vulnerable remains once again.
This might be for you if you...
* Are intrigued by medical history or NYC history
* Are a true-crime fan or cemetery enthusiast
* Are curious about our shared, unknown, dark history
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

events.name: Spirits of Photography:Photographing the Dead Brings Peace
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
💡A smarter night out in NYC—fascinating speakers, craft beer, and real conversation. 💡
🍻 Craft beer included with ticket!
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
If a photographer told you he could capture an image of your deceased loved one, would you believe him? In the 1860s, many people did. Hundreds believed photographers such as William Mumler could photograph ghosts, offering what seemed to be proof that communication with the spirit world was possible. However, spirit photography also had its critics. The famous showman P.T. Barnum was one of its most outspoken opponents and even testified at a trial to expose the practice as a fraud. Despite these accusations, many Victorians continued to believe in Mumler’s mysterious “ghosts.”  During the Victorian era, society had a deep fascination with death, and photography became a way to preserve the memory of those who had passed away. Families often commissioned and collected postmortem photographs of their deceased loved ones. At the same time, photographers like William Mumler and, later, William Hope claimed they could capture the spirits of the dead alongside the living. For people grieving their loved ones, these photographs seemed to offer not only a lasting image, but also the possibility of proof that the dead were still present in the spirit world.
JR Pepper is a photographer, lecturer, author, and cemetery tour guide whose work explores the intersections of art, history, death, and the macabre. She holds a BA and MA in Art History, specializing in Surrealism and the history of photography. Pepper has spent more than 20 years working in photography, image restoration, and digital imaging, and has lectured extensively on topics including spirit photography and Victorian mourning traditions. She is also an adjunct professor of art history at Brooklyn College and a tour guide at Green-Wood Cemetery in Brooklyn. Her books include Buried Boston: America’s Revolutionary Necropolis and Buried New Orleans: The Resilient Cemeteries of the Crescent City.
We'll explore:
* How early photographers convinced people of the possibility of the supernatural
* How people responded to such allegations
* Current examples of 'spirit' photography
This might be for you if you...
* Are curious about the supernatural fascination during the Victorian Era
* Are intrigued by examples of the art form of photography being used in unique ways across history
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party

events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.description: High-achieving, ambitious people are known to strive for excellence. While this trait is advantageous for their success, it can act as a double-edged sword & sometimes prevent success. Join us for this week's interactive community conversation. events.name: SOSV's HAX Deep Tech Showcase
events.description: Deep tech has always mattered, but right now, the tailwinds are stronger & more urgent than at any point in the last 40 years. Global demand & national security priorities are converging, making this area critical to the next decade of industrial & economic growth. As part of Climate Week NYC, meet 20+ deep tech companies driving that transformation - all graduates of HAX, SOSV's hard-tech program & the world's most active pre-seed investor for deep tech founders. You will meet Seed & Series A companies building critical solutions with commercial traction across energy systems, industrial automation, robotics, plasma, critical minerals, & advanced chemistry. SOSV's HAX provides hard-tech founders a 6-month collaborative residency, hands-on engineering support, & an initial investment package of up to $550,000. HAX has a flagship 35,000 square foot facility in Newark, with additional offices in Shenzhen, Pune & Tokyo, & expansion planned for a new facility focused on applications of plasma physics called HAX Plasma Forge in Princeton. This event is for investors only. events.name: Family Offices & Investors Summit
events.description: 150 seats. One room. For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). This year, we're raising the bar & want to double that number.  WHO'S BEEN IN THE ROOM: Invited Family Offices & Institutional Capital  KKR ($361B+ AUM, New York) - Global investment firm. Principal from KKR's Sustainability & Capital Formation team joining us.  Generation Investment Management ($44B+ AUM, San Francisco / London) - Al Gore's sustainable investment firm. Founding Partner Colin le Duc returning for the second consecutive year.  Rockefeller Foundation ($6B endowment, New York) - Director of Energy Technology & Innovation Shunondo Basu. Deploying across materials, energy, & chemicals innovation.  BASF Corporate Venture Capital ($87B revenue parent, Germany) - Venture arm of the world's largest chemical company.  Hennessy Capital Group ($1.8B+ deployed via SPAC, Houston) - Five completed climate & industrial technology SPACs.  SOSV HAX IndieBio ($1.5B AUM, San Francisco) - The #1 most active climate tech venture investor globally. GP returning for 2026 Invited Founders & Fund Managers  Nicholas Flanders - Co-Founder & CEO, Twelve (turning CO into jet fuel, backed by TPG Rise Climate)  Martijn Lopes Cardozo - Partner, Regeneration.VC (Leonardo DiCaprio-backed circular economy fund)  Brian Riordan - Co-Founder & COO, Avalanche Energy (compact fusion systems advancing next-generation clean energy)  Daria Saharova - General Partner, World Fund (350M European climate VC. Joining SF 2026)  Mira Inbar - Partner, ArcTern Ventures ($500M+ deployed into climate tech across 40+ companies. Joining SF 2026)  Jocelyn Matyas - Cisco Foundation (supporting climate innovation & early-stage impact ventures)  More speakers to be announced $110 BILLION in committed capital represented in this room. This is an 150-person event. Every seat is curated. No expo booths. No filler panels. events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: WorkOS & You.com Agenda 5:30 pm - 5:35 pmWelcome & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  5:35 pm - 5:50 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  5:50 pm - 6:05 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from WorkOS TBA Outline:TBA  6:05 pm - 6:20 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from You.com TBA Outline:TBA  6:20 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:30 pm - 6:40 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:40 pm - 6:50 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:50 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. events.name: Building Slack's Simplified Layout Mode
events.description: This event will be online on YouTube & in-person (New York City). The speaker & live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page & someone will come down ASAP. DescriptionSlack is a powerful hub for work & communication, but its dense & complex interface can be a barrier for users with motor, vision, & cognitive disabilities. To help more people use Slack effectively, we introduced Simplified Layout Mode on desktop & web. This preference transforms Slack into a single-column layout that is easier to navigate & has fewer distractions. In this session, we will demo Simplified Layout Mode & discuss its evolution from an accommodation request by an ALS advocacy group to a feature that benefits multiple audiences. Along the way, we'll share specific examples of how its design was shaped by our partnerships with disabled & neurodivergent users. Attendees will learn ... How to collect & synthesize feedback from different groups of users with disabilities over the course of a feature's developmentHow to collaborate with internal employee disability groups to get feedback & build momentum around a featurePresenter biosChris Xu is a director of product management of Slack looking after accessibility & design systems. Outside of product management, they have had a wide-ranging career focused on how technology & communities shape each other. They live in Brooklyn, NY & hold strong opinions about fruit. Lena Wang is a frontend software engineer at Slack working on accessibility & design systems. Outside of engineering, she's usually mid-side-quest - whether that's walking the entire length of Manhattan on a whim, running a Taco Bell 5k, or competing in a city-wide scavenger hunt. She lives in Manhattan, NY. Kaili Liang is a Software Engineer at Slack, working on accessibility & design systems. In her free time, she loves chasing new eats, diving into books, trying various arts & crafts, & traveling. AccessibilityThe presentation will have human captions [CC], not automatic captions. For ASL preferred speakers, learn about the Aira ASL App, & download it before the event. For the Blind & Low Vision community, learn about the Aira Explorer App & download it before the event. To access the online webinar for audio description, use the A11yNYC Access Offer to call, or simply inform your Visual Interpreter that you'd like that offer applied when you connect. For additional accessibility requirements, please email meryl@equalentry.com two weeks before the event. LivestreamYouTube Provided by Internet Society Accessibility SIG. Location detailsThe event is at 72 Spring street on the 4th floor. Everyone must be accompanied to the event on the 4th floor. Because everyone needs to be escorted, please arrive early or on time. When you enter the ground floor, a representative from A11yNYC will be there to provide elevator access. TransitThe building 72 Spring street is near several transit stops: 6 train Spring Street (non-accessible stop): 100 feetCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.4 milesB/D/F/M trains Broadway-Lafayette Street (accessible stop), 0.2 milesN/Q/R/W trains Prince Street (non-accessible stop): 0.2 milesCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.3 milesM1 / M55 Bus lines Broadway/Spring Street stop: 500 feetCabs & rideshares can let passengers out right near the building entrance. Finding the buildingIn Google Maps, find 72 Spring street. It shows the correct location of the entrance: on Spring Street, halfway between Crosby & Lafayette.It's also between the Glossier store & the Krewe Eyewear store.Inside & over the reception desk in our building 72 Spring st, it says Marc Jacobs. Traveling to the event?We recommend Hotel on Rivington or Crosby Street Hotel. AccreditationAll A11yNYC meetups are pre-approved for IAAP Continuing Accessibility Education Credits (CAEC). SponsorsThanks to Aira, AKQA, Deque, Evinced, Equal Entry, & Fable for sponsoring. Want to be a sponsor? Contact meryl@equalentry.com

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. Learn more & apply before Wednesday, September 17, at 12:00 PM; apply here. Do you work for a Government agency/department?If you work for a government agency/department & want to purchase a general admission ticket by check or purchase order (PO), government ticket opportunities close on Wednesday, September 17, by 5:00 PM. Please email us at citycamp@beta.nyc. Sponsors, want to support the conference?We're looking for mission-aligned sponsors to help cover conference costs, including meals, coffee, childcare, & ASL interpretation. Learn more about our opportunities to support by filling out this form. Press & Media: Interested in covering the event?Media credentials are available to reporters, editors working as reporters, producers, video camera operators, & still photographers who present valid press identification. If you want to attend to cover a session or the event, email us your valid press identification to citycamp@beta.nyc. We will follow up. General Event Information:What is included in my ticket? All tickets include access to a full day of conference sessions, lunch, snacks, & coffee. We offer free, professional on-site childcare. Space is limited. Please register if you are interested. Childcare We have contracted on-site childcare for children under the age of 18. In order to use this service, you MUST be a ticket-holder, & you MUST register your child(ren) before September 11th by acquiring a Childcare Ticket. Each child you register requires a ticket registration. There are limited spots available, so please sign up sooner rather than later! If you have any questions, please email us at citycamp+childcare@beta.nyc. Accessibility & Accommodations We want CityCamp to be usable by everyone who wants to take part. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available upon request. Service animals are always welcome. The conference is delivered in English & uses technical terms. If you need ASL interpretation, or have any other accessibility question or request, email us at citycamp@beta.nyc by Friday, September 4. Requests after that date are welcome, & we will do what we can, but we cannot promise to fill them. Code of Conduct BetaNYC is committed to hosting safe & open spaces for all. By participating in this space, you are committing yourself to BetaNYC's Code of Conduct & Anti-Harassment Policy. Health Policy If you're not feeling well, PLEASE stay home. We strive to create a safe environment for everyone. (Please see our refund policy for questions.) We encourage everyone to wear a high-quality mask at all times (except when eating & drinking). We will have ample KF-94 masks in various sizes for you to wear. Masks keep our staff, volunteers, & attendees safe. Masking helps prevent the spread of viruses - this is science, based on data! Refund Policy Contact us to request a refund. We will try to honor all of your refund requests at citycamp+refund@beta.nyc. Please note that some ticketing fees are nonrefundable.

While innovation continues to accelerate, turning breakthrough solutions into industry-wide adoption requires collaboration across the entire value chain. This Climate Week NYC, Eco-Age is convening the organisations, brands, & initiatives helping to shape that future. The Forum creates a platform where leaders can share knowledge, build partnerships, & explore practical pathways to adoption, connecting the people who each play a vital role in scaling next-generation materials. While global brands play an important role in leading the transition, commercial scale will ultimately depend on adoption across the wider fashion market, emerging brands to suppliers, material innovators, manufacturers, investors, NGOs, & solution providers. The Forum is designed to move that conversation forward & focus on commercial adoption, supply chain readiness, investment, sourcing, & the partnerships that can accelerate progress across the industry. Climate Week NYC is where global leaders come together to turn ambition into action. events.name: Catalyzing Cities
events.description: Cities are increasingly expected to deliver climate resilience while navigating constrained budgets, aging infrastructure, & growing complexity. Yet many of the most impactful solutions already exist... the challenge is designing financing & partnership models that enable them to scale. This New York Climate Week, join Cool Climate Collective & Climate Vine, as we convene investors, city leaders, philanthropies & ecosystem partners for a discussion on how innovative financing structures & public-private collaboration can unlock catalytic outcomes for cities, particularly for New York. Drawing on emerging work in city outcomes & practical examples from around the world, we'll explore: New models for financing climate resilience beyond traditional procurement. How blended capital & partnership design can accelerate deployment. What is already working in practice & why. Lessons & systems insights informed by collaborators across the resilience ecosystem, including perspectives shared by our partners from UNDRR & Dark Matter Labs. The session is designed to be interactive, bringing together practitioners across sectors to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions, & identify opportunities for collaboration during Climate Week. Agenda 9:30 - 10:00 AM : Check-in & coffee networking 10:00 - 11:30 AM : Interactive discussion & programming 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM : Facilitated small-group discussions followed by open networking
