events.name: From Lab To Scale - Building Northeast's Climate Innovation Pipeline
events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. Over Greentown's 15-year history, the organization has supported 700+ startups that have gone on to raise $15B+ & create 16,000+ jobs. Greentown has hubs in Somerville & Houston, so while most of our members are based in Massachusetts or Texas, our membership is growing beyond these two states, & we intend to double down on that growth. New York's climate & energy ecosystem, with some of the country's most ambitious climate policy, deepest capital markets, & strongest research institutions, is a critical part of where we see Greentown's impact growing next, & this event is one step toward building deeper roots here. Please join the Greentown leadership team to discuss how we can collectively shape the future of climate & energy innovation in New York & Massachusetts - we want to hear from you! You'll be joined by climate & energy leaders from the investment community, large corporates, government, foundations, academia, & the startup community itself, from the Northeast & beyond. Space is limited to keep the conversation intimate, so we hope you'll RSVP soon. Potential topics of discussion include: Seeding & sourcing innovation: How Massachusetts' & New York's university & research ecosystems can learn from each other to build a stronger, more connected pipeline from lab to startup Bridging the Second Valley of Death: How public dollars (through NYSERDA & MassCEC) & private capital across both states can help the most promising climate & energy companies scale from prototype to commercial pilot Keeping manufacturing in the Northeast: How Massachusetts & New York can work together, through shared infrastructure or incentives, to keep growing manufacturers here instead of losing them to other regions Lunch will be provided. Once our discussion wraps up, we invite you to stay for the Greentown Startup Showcase from 1:30 to 3:30 PM to see climate innovation in action. Big thanks to our venue sponsor, SOSV! Agenda (times in ET) 12:30 PM - 12:40 PM: Welcome & mingling 12:40 PM - 12:50 PM: Welcome remarks / presentation from Greentown CEO Georgina Campbell Flatter 12:50 PM - 1:20 PM: VIP discussion on cross-border climate & energy collaboration 1:20 PM - 1:30 PM: Wrap up & establish next steps to increase collaboration between Massachusetts & New York 1:30 PM: Beginning of Startup Showcase event About Greentown As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Greentown enables entrepreneurs to bring their technologies into the world through world-class incubation support, programs for collaborative innovation, & a global ecosystem of corporates, investors, researchers, governments, & philanthropists dedicated to scaling transformational technologies. Greentown Labs, the world's largest climatetech incubator network, provides entrepreneurs mission-critical access to labs, equipment, customers, capital, talent, community, & resources for business growth at its flagship incubators in Somerville, MA & Houston, TX. Please note: By registering for this event, you consent to your name, title, & company/organization being shared with other event attendees. You consent to your image or likeness being used in content associated with the event. You release Greentown Labs & all partners from any & all liability stemming from any event-related incident.

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: Builders & Brews
events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. Come learn, experiment, meet other builders, or work on something of your own. No pressure & no pitches,just agents, coffee, building, & good company. About the Global AI HackathonThe hackathon invites AI builders, ML engineers, founders, & developers to create practical AI systems using NVIDIA open-source models & Nebius infrastructure. The complete brief- including challenges, timeline, rules, prizes, & submission details-will be announced in late August. Until then, join us to explore ideas, get familiar with the tools, & start building. What's happeningNebius provides scalable AI cloud infrastructure that helps teams build, deploy, & scale AI applications efficiently. Tavily is the real-time search engine for AI agents & RAG workflows, offering fast, secure APIs for web search & content extraction. What to expect Welcome & an introduction to the upcoming hackathon  Nebius, Tavily & LangChain platform onboarding & technical setup  Team formation & project ideation  Technical workshops  Mentoring & troubleshooting  Several hours of focused building  Informal progress demos  Clear next steps for continuing your project  Opportunities to share product feedback directly with the teams What you'll get Free coffee & non-caffeinated drinks  Tavily credits  Nebius Token Factory credits  Time & space to brainstorm, start building, or improve an existing project  A chance to meet potential teammates  Access to technical experts for guidance & support  A head start on the upcoming hackathon and some very cool merch Who should comeAI builders & ML engineers Developers curious about agents & open-source AI Hackathon participants looking for ideas or teammates Founders building practical AI products Anyone interested in experimenting with Nebius, NVIDIA models, or Tavily Coffee & music lovers All experience levels are welcome. You don't need a team, a finished idea, or previous hackathon experience. How it worksMeet other builders, join the workshops, brainstorm ideas, & spend a few focused hours building. You won't be required to submit a project, but the experience is designed to help you make meaningful progress toward building-and, if you choose, submitting-something for the hackathon. Full details are coming soon. RSVP to join us in NYC & stay in the loop. Come curious. Leave caffeinated-and a few steps closer to shipping.   Location: NYC, shared after RSVP Time: 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Cost: Free

events.name: Enterprise Security In Age Of AI
events.description: In July an OpenAI model escaped its evaluation sandbox & compromised Hugging Face's production infrastructure in a weekend. The model responsible was not publicly available. Frontier cyber capability now sits inside a handful of labs, & a gap is opening between those with access & everyone defending without it. When attacks move at machine speed & the attacker might be an AI, what does real protection even look like? Join us for a conversation with senior security & AI leaders who live these questions daily. Nick Muy: Nicholas Muy is the VP of Engineering, Platform & Security / CISO at Scrut Automation, where he leads platform engineering, security, AI governance, & agentic AI product strategy for a GRC platform serving 1,700+ customers. He's also a Venture Partner at Tidal Ventures & co-leads the Angel Syndicate at Venture in Security. He started as a childhood hacker who couldn't leave well enough alone, which led to the Department of Homeland Security, securing billions in travel transactions at Expedia, contributing to the first NIST Cybersecurity Framework v1.0, & eventually building security & product programs at high-growth startups. He reads Hobbes & Anthropic model reports with equal enthusiasm, fights engineers on architecture & marketing teams on unit economics, & doesn't discriminate against interesting problems. Mariya Vasileva: Mariya Vasileva is a Senior Research Scientist at Meta, where she studies multimodal model behavior, safety & alignment, & the scalable evaluation of frontier AI systems. Her research focuses on understanding how models behave under complex constraints & developing rigorous methods for evaluating the reliability & security of increasingly agentic systems. Previously, she developed auditing methodologies for high-impact machine-learning & computer-vision systems at AWS. She holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. John Kitaoka: John Kitaoka is a research fellow at MATS Research working on dangerous capability evaluations & scalable oversight for multi-agent systems with UK AISI & US CAISI. Prior to MATS, John worked with scientists at Harvard & Lawrence Livermore National Labs on automated red-teaming & verification techniques for dangerous knowledge elicitation by frontier models. He spent four years at Amazon Web Services as an AI Architect, & led AI product development for government technology sectors. His work spans scalable LLM evaluation for enterprises, multi-agent systems for critical sectors, & advising AI adoption across the public sector, & John has a background in mathematics & computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Moderated By: Yash Tulsani: Yash is a serial cybersecurity & AI founder & operator. He is currently building a new company that is creating the Intelligence Layer for Enterprise Security. Previously, he built CalypsoAI, which pioneered AI Runtime Security & AI Redteaming & was acquired by F5 Networks. Prior to CalypsoAI, Yash got his start building technology companies at UiPath, where he was lucky to see all sides of business building from early stage to public company. He started his career researching public technology companies at Credit Suisse & trading High Yield Bonds at BlackRock. Yash is just as comfortable talking about product architectures as he is about breaking down merger models. Thank you to Asymptote Labs for their partnership on this event! About South Park Commons (SPC)SPC is a technical community & venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, & technologists figure out what to work on next-what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible. Apply to SPC here.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business To 7-Figures Without Raising Venture Capital
events.description: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business to 7-Figures Without Raising Venture CapitalI built Fibe to millions of dollars in profit without raising a dollar of venture capital, without a co-founder, & without a board. I still own the whole thing. Since then I've started The Shortlist, which has just begun to hit profitability, & cofounded Outliers Summit, which runs independently as a profitable events & media company that will cross seven figures soon. I spent years building an audience before I had a business idea, & it is the single biggest reason bootstrapping worked How to find customers who will write a $50,000 check without blinking instead of ones who argue over $20 a month Then live Q&A for the rest of the session. Come with the specific question about your business, not the general one. That is where these earn their keep. Who this is for: anyone building something they would rather own outright than raise against. If you're going after a winner-take-all market & need capital to reach escape velocity, raising is the right call & this isn't for you.at. Mine wasn't.

events.name: Superplane & Elastic - AI Agents That Build & Ship Code
events.description: Software factories are here. AI agents write code, open PRs, run tests, deploy to production, & respond to incidents - all without waiting for a human to click a button. Join SuperPlane & Elastic for an evening where engineering leaders, platform teams, & SREs explore what it actually takes to run a software factory: how agents ship code, how Elastic monitors what happens in production, & how SuperPlane orchestrates the full loop from commit  deploy to incident to fix. SuperPlane is the agent orchestrator that turns your tools into a software factory. Elastic is the observability engine that tells you what's happening inside it. This is an unconference, you bring the topics, we bring the structure (and drinks). Come with opinions about how far you'd let agents go.  Date: Thursday, September 17th from 6:00-9:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001 Some topics we would discuss: How much autonomy should agents have in production?Building the feedback loop: deploy  observe  respond  learnAgents that fix what agents broke - is that a loop or a spiral?What does "human in the loop" actually mean when agents ship 10x faster?Observability as the control plane for your software factoryFrom Kibana alert to automated rollback - what's your threshold?The trust problem: when do you stop reviewing agent PRs?Format: Topics proposed by attendees at the beginningSessions run in small groups (~5-7 people)30 minutes of facilitated discussion per sessionOpen participation & movement between sessions encouraged Schedule: 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Arrival, food & drinks, networking6:30 - 6:50 PM  Welcome + software factories w/ Elastic & Superplane6:50 - 7:00 PM  Topic proposals & voting7:00 - 7:30 PM  Session 17:30 - 7:40 PM  Short break7:40 - 8:10 PM  Session 28:10 - 8:20 PM  Short break8:20 - 8:50 PM  Session 38:50 - 9:00 PM  Wrap-up & key takeaways9:00 PM  ClosingAbout SuperPlaneSuperPlane Software Factory platform that transforms software delivery from a collection of manual tasks into an orchestrated, AI-powered production system. It coordinates AI agents, developers, infrastructure, & operational tools to build, test, deploy, & maintain software with speed, consistency, & governance. About ElasticElastic is the observability stack behind high-velocity engineering teams. With Elasticsearch, Kibana, & the rest of Elastic Stack, engineers, SREs & platform engineers get real-time visibility into logs, metrics, traces, & security events correlated in one place, not scattered across tools. As release cadence increases with the adoption of software factories, Elastic keeps you in control of what's running & why.

events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. Her experience is specialized in the digital health space, & she enjoys building community & connecting people in the space. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: Brunch & Learn
events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.description: Is the SaaS Pricing Model Dead?For twenty years, SaaS companies built their businesses around recurring subscriptions. AI is breaking that model. Seat licenses are turning into token pricing. Some customers want to pay for outcomes, not users. And inference costs are quietly becoming one of the biggest line items on the P&L. If you run a dev shop building AI products, or you're a funded founder trying to scale one, you're probably already feeling this. Even if you haven't figured out what to do about it yet. Join York Effect for a live panel with a Head of Product & a CFO, digging into pricing, unit economics, & what happens when the cost of delivering software starts moving faster than your pricing model can keep up. Who should attend: Software development firms & AI product builders. Series A+ founders scaling SaaS. Also relevant for product leaders, CFOs, finance execs, & investors watching this space. Who's behind this: Tova Feldheim & Caroline Jerome are co-founders of York Effect. events.name: Buildings & Materials Conference
events.description: WHERE BUILDING TECH & MATERIALS COME TOGETHERThe annual Buildings + Materials Conference explores innovation & emerging technology in the development, design, materials, & systems of buildings. The event examines the current state & trajectory of building planning & operational solutions, strategies, & processes, providing insights & guidance on implementation, use cases, opportunities, & challenges. Connect. Inform. Advance.The premier network for advancing innovation & catalyzing collaboration throughout the built environment ecosystem. It Began As a Digital Community Connecting, Sharing, & LearningIn the fall of 2013, BuiltWorlds analysts began harnessing the power of digital media, crowd sourcing, & open innovation, sharing what they were learning & who they were meeting via social media & drawing in ever more passionate, open, experts who shared even more insights & data. The resulting network effect produced a global community of thousands of people actively providing data & contacts, curated by our analyst team, who then shared with back with the community in the form of actionable insights & deeper understanding. From the Community, A Powerful Research Network EmergedBuiltWorlds emerged as a free community, fueled by subscribers & supported by a small groups of sponsors. However, as the community grew, more members of the community wanted to access more of BuiltWorlds' research & collaborate more actively with others in the community.  Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 8.30 am - check-in. We kick off at 8.45 am. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: NVIDIA's recent results, strategies & future Nvidia's earnings just landed with the whole AI trade riding on them. We're decoding the strategy behind the numbers, the competitive moat, & whether the growth story still justifies the valuation Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time.

events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: From Bench To Boardroom - Cellular Logistics, Nanobiology & VC Biotech
events.description: Every cell in your body runs a hyper-complex logistical network. Tens of thousands of tiny membrane-enveloped packages-called vesicles-ferry critical cargo like insulin, hormones, & neurotransmitters to precise destinations. If this delivery system delays by even a millisecond, or drops its cargo in the wrong place, the result is devastating human disease: diabetes, neurological disorders, & immune system failures. Understanding how cells manage this trafficking didn't just rewrite biology textbooks-it won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Medicine. But fundamental science is only half the journey. The real magic happens when world-changing research successfully leaves the academic lab to hit the commercial market. Few people have bridged this gap like Professor James Rothman, Ph.D. Originally trained in physics at Yale before pivoting to biochemistry at Harvard, Professor Rothman looks at biology through the lens of fundamental mechanics. Today, he is the Sterling Professor of Cell Biology & the Director & Founder of the Yale Nanobiology Institute, where researchers merge the physical sciences with engineering to study living systems at the nanoscale. Beyond academia, Professor Rothman is a veteran biotech founder, life science industry executive, & venture advisor. From founding ARIAD Pharmaceuticals to guiding deep-tech bio platforms like Prellis Biologics & advising firms like Celesta Capital & Arsenal, his career represents the ultimate "bench-to-boardroom" trajectory. In this exclusive fireside chat with SOSV Managing Partner Sean O'Sullivan, Professor Rothman will explore: The Cellular Supply Chain: What his Nobel-winning discovery of SNARE proteins teaches us about the ultimate "machinery" of life-and how understanding these pathways allows us to block viral entry & combat infectious diseases. The Nanobiology Era: Why human health tech is shifting away from incremental chemistry toward engineering & programming life at the molecular scale. The Translation Chasm: The raw realities of moving breakthroughs from elite university benches to commercial boardrooms. Platform vs. Product: Lessons from building scalable biotherapeutics platforms (like Prellis's bioprinted human immune systems) versus single-drug assets. The Future of Investment: What the next generation of venture capitalists & founders must understand to accurately de-risk deep tech biology. Seats are limited. Register early to save your spot! This is an in-person event. Location will be shared after you register & are approved.  Broadcast live from our SOSV NY event space, this is the next installment of SOSV Deep Tech LIVE, our video podcast series exploring the frontiers of deep tech with leading founders, researchers, & technologists.

events.name: Frontier Table - AI Founder Dinner
events.description: An Evening on the AI Frontier - New York A Frontier Table Dinner, hosted by Obvious AI is changing how we build products at a dizzying rate. But it's also transforming how we build teams, companies, & even startup ecosystems. And the implications are moving faster than the conversation around them. This raises questions that matter more than whether to use Claude Code or Codex. What if the way we've built companies for the last 15 years is entirely incompatible with what's needed for the next 15? What constitutes a moat anymore? What does defensibility look like when anyone can build anything? When you're building at the epicenter of AI acceleration - where capital, talent, & ambition are concentrated at unprecedented scale - how do you build something durable instead of just fast? How do we separate what's meaningful from what's hype when everything is changing this fast? These are also the hardest questions to answer, because the answers are emerging & changing in near real time. And there is rarely space to engage them with peers living through the same transformation & operating on the frontier. So this dinner is an attempt to create that space & facilitate these discussions. The format is simple. A small table, great food, & a few hours to think out loud together. We'll open by sharing the model of the near future driving how we operate at Obvious, the one we're working backwards from. Then we'll turn it over to the room. What we'd ask of everyone is the same thing we'll offer: the fundamental observation driving you right now, & the question keeping you up at night. No agenda beyond that. Just the people best equipped to see what's coming, comparing notes before it arrives.   // ABOUT OBVIOUS Obvious is an applied AI research lab. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible & what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, & 10x our shipping velocity in less than a year.

events.name: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. events.description: Join Andrew Yeung & Ankur Nagpal, for a live conversation on how outlier founders actually think, & where that thinking breaks from the advice everyone repeats. Ankur built Teachable from an idea to $60M ARR & sold it for $250M. He has seen the pattern from all three seats: building it, selling it, & writing the checks. Andrew is the founder of Fibe, the media & events platform behind Outliers Summit, Junto & Tech Breakfast Club. A former Google & Meta PM, he now convenes founders, operators & investors across eight cities a year. Few people sit across from more founders annually, or hear more of what actually happens behind the announcements. Between them they have built, sold, backed & interviewed the people behind some of the largest companies in tech. events.name: Rethinking Compensation - Smarter Ways To Invest In Talent, Not Just Cut Costs
events.description: Compensation is one of the most powerful levers CFOs have to attract & retain top talent & drive profitability. Excessive cuts force turnover & hurt performance, while overly generous pay strains budgets & planning. In this session, CFOs will explore how to redesign salary, incentives, equity, & benefits by weighing the tradeoffs that matter most. You'll leave with a framework for deciding when to invest in talent versus tighten costs, how to structure incentives that reward both short- & long-term results, & practical tactics for effective offers without overpaying. Schedule:6:00-6:20 PM: Welcome networking 6:20-7:00 PM: Panel conversation featuring prepared questions followed by audience Q&A 7:00-8:00 PM Continued networking around topics Refreshments & light food will be available. Sponsors:CTI, founded by former tax auditors & Big 4 tax professionals, helps businesses maximize tax incentives. Our expert team of CPAs, attorneys, & engineers have secured over $52B in credits, including R&D, employment, sales & use, & property incentives using advanced technology & deep expertise to drive measurable financial results. Libra Value Partners is a boutique valuation firm that provides independent, defensible valuations for tax/409A, financial reporting, & transaction purposes. We help business owners, CFOs, attorneys, & CPAs make informed decisions with confidence. Build Scale Grow provides fractional leadership that helps you grow faster, spend less, & avoid costly mistakes. We turn goals into priorities, solve problems proactively, & establish systems so you can stay focused on growth. Founded in 2016, the New York Tech CFO Group is a free community where high-growth finance leaders share practical strategies for planning, operations, & technology. We host regular in-person gatherings from casual happy hours & breakfasts to educational & networking events.

events.name: From Concept To Conviction - AI In The Designer's Toolkit
events.description: Join us for an evening with Mareike Carolin Keller, Product Designer at Spotify, as she explores how to move AI from an experimental tool to a core part of your design workflow. Mareike will share how to leverage AI-assisted prototyping & code generation to accelerate execution & earn rapid stakeholder buy-in. As AI tools mature, the challenge for design teams is moving from informal experimentation to practical, daily utility. Mareike Carolin Keller will unpack how to embed AI directly into sprint cycles, validate complex ideas through real-time prototyping, & replace static mockups with interactive deliverables. Expect practical insights on using AI to bridge the gap between ideation & execution, ultimately driving faster cross-functional consensus. Mareike Carolin Keller (she/her) is a Product Designer at Spotify, where she focuses on creating cohesive, human-centered experiences across Spotify's growing multi-format platform. Her work spans across discovery & systemized distribution of content, as well as social experiences - helping millions of listeners seamlessly explore music, podcasts, & audiobooks. With a background in interaction design & experimental psychology, Mareike is passionate about crafting intuitive digital experiences that connect people to culture & creativity. Integrating AI into the design process transforms individual speed into team-wide capability. Mareike Carolin Keller shares how product designers can deploy AI tools in active production, build high-fidelity prototypes, & secure stakeholder alignment before committing heavy engineering resources. 01Evolving Design Workflows at Scale Learn how to establish clear frameworks that integrate AI capability directly into daily practice, transforming individual experimentation into institutional-grade capability. 02AI-Assisted Prototyping in Production Discover how to embed AI coding tools & custom generators directly into sprint cycles to validate complex ideas & test practical mechanics in real time. 03Accelerating Stakeholder Conviction Explore how to replace static mockups with high-fidelity, interactive prototypes that demonstrate actual product behavior, reduce decision friction, & secure immediate cross-functional buy-in.

events.description: Note: we are postponing & redesigning this event for September. This was a new event type & let's just say, it wasn't as popular as we thought it would be so, in true crowd-validator style, we are going back to the drawing board. Please contact us if you have constructive feedback. Thanks & Stay tuned!Alex Fair Original write up - subject to change. Presented by MedStartr in Partnership with ClawCamp You bring the vision. We'll help you launch a company - in a weekend. Healthcare is broken in a hundred ways we all see daily. You've felt it as a patient. diagnosed it as a clinician. doded around it as a builder, & hated it as a person who came into healthcare to help people. The things you see that could be better are hard to fix, & it bothers you that they seem incorrigible. But then you got an idea of something that could help, if you could just build it & get it in the hands of people like you to help patients get better care & the system & caregivers to give better care. We know, we have met thousands of you & ARE you too. That's why we have run this group for almost 18 years & done so many events. But now, with the help of AI & the new MedStartr.ai platform, we can help even more. So we created what we are calling a "Launchathon" to help with all that & this is the first one! The NYC HealthTech Launchathon is your chance to do something about it. No startup experience required. No coding background needed. Just bring your problem, your perspective, & your curiosity - & we'll bring the AI tools, expert faculty, mentors, investors, & community to help you build something real. The Program: 3 Phases, 8 Weeks  Phase I  HealthTech ClawCamp  August 1-2 **Day 1 - August 1 | Stack AI HQ, One World Trade Center**Learn. Ideate. Validate with Experts on hand & Build or add to your team from other folks like yourself. Meet amazing people. Pitch problems. Learn from expert AI faculty, upskill. Present or Find a problem worth solving - & the team to solve it with. No startup idea or coding required, but bring your passion to build solutions to the problems in healthcare. Day 2 - August 2 | Arya Health HQ, NYC**Build Something Real. Build prototypes. Validate ideas. Design workflows. Interview users. Use AI, code, & creativity. Leave Day 2 with something real - a working prototype posted to MedStartr.ai Qualifies you for Phase II (Also Awards of tokens & other great stuff from Day 2 Winners)  Phase II  MedStartr Crowd Challenge  August 2 - October 6 Your Build goes live on MedStartr.ai where 250,000+ credentialed healthcare stakeholders - patients, clinicians, investors, partners - can review, comment, follow, pilot, & share. More eyes. More feedback. More signal on what actually matters. Teams keep building & iterating based on what the crowd says.  Phase III  Launchathon Finals  October 6Health Impact Forum  Microsoft  Times Square, NYC The top crowd-validated teams take the stage at one of NYC's biggest healthcare innovation gatherings. Compete for **over $1 million** in investment, accelerator spots, pilots, partnerships, software credits, & everything a startup needs to succeed. Keynote SpeakersDay 1: Khan Siddiqui, MDCEO & Co-Founder, HOPPR  2025 SIIM Imaging Informatics Innovator"From Hacking to Scale" Brian Yarnell3x Exited HealthTech Founder Day 2: Grace Cordovano, PhDBoard Certified Patient Advocate  CancerX*"Designing for the Patient Experience"* 15 other MedStartr Mentors & 7 AI expert trainers to help you validate, plan & build your ideas out better & faster## Who Should Attend? This is for **everyone who touches healthcare** - not just developers: -  **Clinicians** - physicians, nurses, NPs, PAs who see broken workflows daily-  **Patients & caregivers** - living the gaps in care & navigation firsthand-  **Admins & billers** - revenue cycle, coding, & operations insiders-  **Researchers** - with data, insights, & unmet needs to solve-  **Tech co-founders** - developers & AI builders seeking high-impact problems (apply for discounted tickets)-  **Early founders** - ideas at any stage, ready to validate fast MedStartr Challenge Winners are 22 more likely to succeed. --- There are many more ticket Types available on MedStartr.ai/launchathon: | Type | Price | Details ||------|-------|---------|| General Admission | $50| Open enrollment || Two Pack | $80| Everything is better with friends || VIP | $100 | Dedicated mentor time + Health Impact Forum ticket || Early Bird | $0-25 | Apply to attend - going fast || Tech Co-Founder | $50 | Apply - discounted for technical builders || Mentor | Free | Apply via MedStartr.ai || Volunteer | Free | Help us run the event || Demo Table | $1,000 | Table for laptop, monitor + 1 rollup banner | Register & buy tickets here or for more options [visit the MedStartr.ai Healthcare Innovation platform with more details!](http://medstartr.ai/launchathon) Confirmed Sponsors Arya Health  Stack.ai  Health Impact Forum Interested in sponsoring?Five tiers from $2,500 Community to $50,000 Title. About MedStartr 17 years building the global healthcare innovation community. 9,000+ innovations reviewed. 250,000+ credentialed stakeholders. 1,200+ events in 41 cities. The team behind over 120 contests & crowdchallenges for over 200 sponsors since 2010. We also run the investment funds & accelerators, also named MedStartr where we invest in & accelerate the teams that win challenges like this one. Check out the new [MedStartr.ai](http://medstartr.ai) alpha Just Launched 7/14/2026! About ClawCamp ClawCamp is a global community advancing mastery of AI agents - from first personal agent to advanced multi-agent workflows. 1,400+ events  120+ cities  100,000+ attendees trained. The AI training backbone of the Launchathon build weekend. Visit them at clawcamp.us Khan Siddiqui, MDDr. Khan Siddiqui is a physician-entrepreneur, technologist, & radiologist at the forefront of the medical AI revolution. As CEO & Co-Founder of HOPPR, he leads the development of advanced multimodal foundation models designed to democratize AI training & accelerate medical imaging development for healthcare systems worldwide.He previously served as Chief Medical Officer & Chief Strategy Officer of Hyperfine, where he helped take the company public & deploy Swoop - the world's first FDA-cleared, portable bedside MRI system. In 2012 he founded higi, a consumer health network of thousands of biometric screening kiosks across North American pharmacies, culminating in a multi-billion-dollar acquisition. Earlier, as a principal program manager & AI architect at Microsoft, he designed the deep-learning image infrastructure used to train the Xbox Kinect. A recognized pioneer in imaging informatics, Dr. Siddiqui received the 2025 Imaging Informatics Innovator Award from the Society for Imaging Informatics in Medicine (SIIM) & holds dozens of patents across medical image processing, machine learning, & healthcare analytics.

events.name: Co-Founder Matching - Find A Partner By Solving Real Problems
events.description: You don't find a co-founder by reading a profile. You find one by working: two hours, real problems, mutual matches only. You don't find a co-founder by reading a profile. You find one by working.   Two hours next to someone shows you how they think, argue & cut scope. A profile shows you nothing. So we don't do matching - we do work, & the partnership question answers itself.    YOUR PROBLEM IS ON THE BOARD BEFORE YOU WALK IN   After you book, you send us one line: the problem you're bringing. By the time you arrive it's already on the board with everyone else's. The room votes, the top problems get the tables - five people, twenty-five minutes each, one problem at a time.   Two minutes to explain it. Three minutes of questions only. Eight minutes while the table works on it out loud & you turn your chair around & take notes - you don't defend, you don't explain, you write. Two minutes for what you're taking away.   Halfway through there's a second vote, so the problems that didn't make the first round get their turn. By the end you've worked shoulder-to-shoulder with eight to ten people. That's a filter no profile gives you.    NOBODY LEAVES WITH NOTHING   Before we scatter, the host asks one question out loud: who still doesn't have an answer? Every hand gets the room's attention - & someone in it has the contact you need.    MUTUAL MATCHES ONLY   You mark the people you'd build something with. We connect you only when both sides say yes, within 48 hours. No cold intros, no lists, no awkward follow-ups to people who weren't interested.    ONE THING IS REQUIRED BEFORE YOU COME   A three-minute form in our Mini App: your problem in one line, some context, how long it's been unresolved. Only submitted problems make the board & the vote.    WHO'S IN THE ROOM   Solo founders looking for a technical or commercial partner  engineers & builders who want to co-found, not take a job  product & GTM operators ready for zero-to-one  founders with a team who came to unstick something.   Hosted by Andrey Krylow. He greets every guest at the door, seats you at the right table, & makes the introductions - nobody stands alone at this event.   WHAT'S GUARANTEED: a curated room, two working sessions, mutual matches within 48 hours. WHAT WE DON'T PROMISE: a co-founder by the end of the evening, or a room full of investors. What we promise is the working session that tells you who's worth a second conversation.   Three rules, said out loud in sixty seconds: what's said here stays here  we share experience, not advice  moving to another table mid-session is normal.   Registration required. Check-in through the Ascent Valley Mini App inside Telegram: everyone you meet stays saved, matched & reachable after tonight.   Ascent Valley - a founder & investor ecosystem across 21 cities. IDEA  PROCESS  RESULT.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.name: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. About Farzad, the host Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C.   About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 8.30 am - check-in. We kick off at 8.45 am. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: NVIDIA's recent results, strategies & future Nvidia's earnings just landed with the whole AI trade riding on them. We're decoding the strategy behind the numbers, the competitive moat, & whether the growth story still justifies the valuation Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. Her experience is specialized in the digital health space, & she enjoys building community & connecting people in the space. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.
