events.name: Superplane & Elastic - AI Agents That Build & Ship Code
events.description: Software factories are here. AI agents write code, open PRs, run tests, deploy to production, & respond to incidents - all without waiting for a human to click a button. Join SuperPlane & Elastic for an evening where engineering leaders, platform teams, & SREs explore what it actually takes to run a software factory: how agents ship code, how Elastic monitors what happens in production, & how SuperPlane orchestrates the full loop from commit  deploy to incident to fix. SuperPlane is the agent orchestrator that turns your tools into a software factory. Elastic is the observability engine that tells you what's happening inside it. This is an unconference, you bring the topics, we bring the structure (and drinks). Come with opinions about how far you'd let agents go.  Date: Thursday, September 17th from 6:00-9:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001 Some topics we would discuss: How much autonomy should agents have in production?Building the feedback loop: deploy  observe  respond  learnAgents that fix what agents broke - is that a loop or a spiral?What does "human in the loop" actually mean when agents ship 10x faster?Observability as the control plane for your software factoryFrom Kibana alert to automated rollback - what's your threshold?The trust problem: when do you stop reviewing agent PRs?Format: Topics proposed by attendees at the beginningSessions run in small groups (~5-7 people)30 minutes of facilitated discussion per sessionOpen participation & movement between sessions encouraged Schedule: 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Arrival, food & drinks, networking6:30 - 6:50 PM  Welcome + software factories w/ Elastic & Superplane6:50 - 7:00 PM  Topic proposals & voting7:00 - 7:30 PM  Session 17:30 - 7:40 PM  Short break7:40 - 8:10 PM  Session 28:10 - 8:20 PM  Short break8:20 - 8:50 PM  Session 38:50 - 9:00 PM  Wrap-up & key takeaways9:00 PM  ClosingAbout SuperPlaneSuperPlane Software Factory platform that transforms software delivery from a collection of manual tasks into an orchestrated, AI-powered production system. It coordinates AI agents, developers, infrastructure, & operational tools to build, test, deploy, & maintain software with speed, consistency, & governance. About ElasticElastic is the observability stack behind high-velocity engineering teams. With Elasticsearch, Kibana, & the rest of Elastic Stack, engineers, SREs & platform engineers get real-time visibility into logs, metrics, traces, & security events correlated in one place, not scattered across tools. As release cadence increases with the adoption of software factories, Elastic keeps you in control of what's running & why.

events.description: Note: we are postponing & redesigning this event for September. This was a new event type & let's just say, it wasn't as popular as we thought it would be so, in true crowd-validator style, we are going back to the drawing board. Please contact us if you have constructive feedback. Thanks & Stay tuned!Alex Fair Original write up - subject to change. Presented by MedStartr in Partnership with ClawCamp You bring the vision. We'll help you launch a company - in a weekend. Healthcare is broken in a hundred ways we all see daily. You've felt it as a patient. diagnosed it as a clinician. doded around it as a builder, & hated it as a person who came into healthcare to help people. The things you see that could be better are hard to fix, & it bothers you that they seem incorrigible. But then you got an idea of something that could help, if you could just build it & get it in the hands of people like you to help patients get better care & the system & caregivers to give better care. We know, we have met thousands of you & ARE you too. That's why we have run this group for almost 18 years & done so many events. But now, with the help of AI & the new MedStartr.ai platform, we can help even more. So we created what we are calling a "Launchathon" to help with all that & this is the first one! The NYC HealthTech Launchathon is your chance to do something about it. No startup experience required. No coding background needed. Just bring your problem, your perspective, & your curiosity - & we'll bring the AI tools, expert faculty, mentors, investors, & community to help you build something real. The Program: 3 Phases, 8 Weeks  Phase I  HealthTech ClawCamp  August 1-2 **Day 1 - August 1 | Stack AI HQ, One World Trade Center**Learn. Ideate. Validate with Experts on hand & Build or add to your team from other folks like yourself. Meet amazing people. Pitch problems. Learn from expert AI faculty, upskill. Present or Find a problem worth solving - & the team to solve it with. No startup idea or coding required, but bring your passion to build solutions to the problems in healthcare. Day 2 - August 2 | Arya Health HQ, NYC**Build Something Real. Build prototypes. Validate ideas. Design workflows. Interview users. Use AI, code, & creativity. Leave Day 2 with something real - a working prototype posted to MedStartr.ai Qualifies you for Phase II (Also Awards of tokens & other great stuff from Day 2 Winners)  Phase II  MedStartr Crowd Challenge  August 2 - October 6 Your Build goes live on MedStartr.ai where 250,000+ credentialed healthcare stakeholders - patients, clinicians, investors, partners - can review, comment, follow, pilot, & share. More eyes. More feedback. More signal on what actually matters. Teams keep building & iterating based on what the crowd says.  Phase III  Launchathon Finals  October 6Health Impact Forum  Microsoft  Times Square, NYC The top crowd-validated teams take the stage at one of NYC's biggest healthcare innovation gatherings. Compete for **over $1 million** in investment, accelerator spots, pilots, partnerships, software credits, & everything a startup needs to succeed. Keynote SpeakersDay 1: Khan Siddiqui, MDCEO & Co-Founder, HOPPR  2025 SIIM Imaging Informatics Innovator"From Hacking to Scale" Brian Yarnell3x Exited HealthTech Founder Day 2: Grace Cordovano, PhDBoard Certified Patient Advocate  CancerX*"Designing for the Patient Experience"* 15 other MedStartr Mentors & 7 AI expert trainers to help you validate, plan & build your ideas out better & faster## Who Should Attend? This is for **everyone who touches healthcare** - not just developers: -  **Clinicians** - physicians, nurses, NPs, PAs who see broken workflows daily-  **Patients & caregivers** - living the gaps in care & navigation firsthand-  **Admins & billers** - revenue cycle, coding, & operations insiders-  **Researchers** - with data, insights, & unmet needs to solve-  **Tech co-founders** - developers & AI builders seeking high-impact problems (apply for discounted tickets)-  **Early founders** - ideas at any stage, ready to validate fast MedStartr Challenge Winners are 22 more likely to succeed. --- There are many more ticket Types available on MedStartr.ai/launchathon: | Type | Price | Details ||------|-------|---------|| General Admission | $50| Open enrollment || Two Pack | $80| Everything is better with friends || VIP | $100 | Dedicated mentor time + Health Impact Forum ticket || Early Bird | $0-25 | Apply to attend - going fast || Tech Co-Founder | $50 | Apply - discounted for technical builders || Mentor | Free | Apply via MedStartr.ai || Volunteer | Free | Help us run the event || Demo Table | $1,000 | Table for laptop, monitor + 1 rollup banner | Register & buy tickets here or for more options [visit the MedStartr.ai Healthcare Innovation platform with more details!](http://medstartr.ai/launchathon) Confirmed Sponsors Arya Health  Stack.ai  Health Impact Forum Interested in sponsoring?Five tiers from $2,500 Community to $50,000 Title. About MedStartr 17 years building the global healthcare innovation community. 9,000+ innovations reviewed. 250,000+ credentialed stakeholders. 1,200+ events in 41 cities. The team behind over 120 contests & crowdchallenges for over 200 sponsors since 2010. We also run the investment funds & accelerators, also named MedStartr where we invest in & accelerate the teams that win challenges like this one. Check out the new [MedStartr.ai](http://medstartr.ai) alpha Just Launched 7/14/2026! About ClawCamp ClawCamp is a global community advancing mastery of AI agents - from first personal agent to advanced multi-agent workflows. 1,400+ events  120+ cities  100,000+ attendees trained. The AI training backbone of the Launchathon build weekend. Visit them at clawcamp.us Khan Siddiqui, MDDr. Khan Siddiqui is a physician-entrepreneur, technologist, & radiologist at the forefront of the medical AI revolution. As CEO & Co-Founder of HOPPR, he leads the development of advanced multimodal foundation models designed to democratize AI training & accelerate medical imaging development for healthcare systems worldwide.He previously served as Chief Medical Officer & Chief Strategy Officer of Hyperfine, where he helped take the company public & deploy Swoop - the world's first FDA-cleared, portable bedside MRI system. In 2012 he founded higi, a consumer health network of thousands of biometric screening kiosks across North American pharmacies, culminating in a multi-billion-dollar acquisition. Earlier, as a principal program manager & AI architect at Microsoft, he designed the deep-learning image infrastructure used to train the Xbox Kinect. A recognized pioneer in imaging informatics, Dr. Siddiqui received the 2025 Imaging Informatics Innovator Award from the Society for Imaging Informatics in Medicine (SIIM) & holds dozens of patents across medical image processing, machine learning, & healthcare analytics.

events.name: Race To Recover America's Critical Minerals - When Startups & Industry Team Up
events.description: The US imports the vast majority of the critical minerals that power its defense, aerospace, & semiconductor industries - but a meaningful share of what it needs may already be sitting in waste piles at the industrial sites that exist today. Join KOMPAS VC, SOSV, & At One Ventures for a breakfast conversation on what it actually takes to turn that waste into supply - & why the answer increasingly runs through a corporate partnership between a deep-tech innovator & an industrial incumbent, scaling proven technology beyond the pilot stage, not one company going it alone. We'll hear directly from Helios & Atalco, a live example of how corporate partnerships move promising technology from pilot to commercial scale, on infrastructure that already exists. Expect a short, focused fireside chat, brief perspectives from our venture partners, & plenty of time to connect over breakfast with others working at the intersection of hard tech, industrial partnerships, & the circular economy

events.name: Frontier Table - AI Founder Dinner
events.description: An Evening on the AI Frontier - New York A Frontier Table Dinner, hosted by Obvious AI is changing how we build products at a dizzying rate. But it's also transforming how we build teams, companies, & even startup ecosystems. And the implications are moving faster than the conversation around them. This raises questions that matter more than whether to use Claude Code or Codex. What if the way we've built companies for the last 15 years is entirely incompatible with what's needed for the next 15? What constitutes a moat anymore? What does defensibility look like when anyone can build anything? When you're building at the epicenter of AI acceleration - where capital, talent, & ambition are concentrated at unprecedented scale - how do you build something durable instead of just fast? How do we separate what's meaningful from what's hype when everything is changing this fast? These are also the hardest questions to answer, because the answers are emerging & changing in near real time. And there is rarely space to engage them with peers living through the same transformation & operating on the frontier. So this dinner is an attempt to create that space & facilitate these discussions. The format is simple. A small table, great food, & a few hours to think out loud together. We'll open by sharing the model of the near future driving how we operate at Obvious, the one we're working backwards from. Then we'll turn it over to the room. What we'd ask of everyone is the same thing we'll offer: the fundamental observation driving you right now, & the question keeping you up at night. No agenda beyond that. Just the people best equipped to see what's coming, comparing notes before it arrives.   // ABOUT OBVIOUS Obvious is an applied AI research lab. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible & what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, & 10x our shipping velocity in less than a year.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Co-Founder Matching - Find A Partner By Solving Real Problems
events.description: You don't find a co-founder by reading a profile. You find one by working: two hours, real problems, mutual matches only. You don't find a co-founder by reading a profile. You find one by working.   Two hours next to someone shows you how they think, argue & cut scope. A profile shows you nothing. So we don't do matching - we do work, & the partnership question answers itself.    YOUR PROBLEM IS ON THE BOARD BEFORE YOU WALK IN   After you book, you send us one line: the problem you're bringing. By the time you arrive it's already on the board with everyone else's. The room votes, the top problems get the tables - five people, twenty-five minutes each, one problem at a time.   Two minutes to explain it. Three minutes of questions only. Eight minutes while the table works on it out loud & you turn your chair around & take notes - you don't defend, you don't explain, you write. Two minutes for what you're taking away.   Halfway through there's a second vote, so the problems that didn't make the first round get their turn. By the end you've worked shoulder-to-shoulder with eight to ten people. That's a filter no profile gives you.    NOBODY LEAVES WITH NOTHING   Before we scatter, the host asks one question out loud: who still doesn't have an answer? Every hand gets the room's attention - & someone in it has the contact you need.    MUTUAL MATCHES ONLY   You mark the people you'd build something with. We connect you only when both sides say yes, within 48 hours. No cold intros, no lists, no awkward follow-ups to people who weren't interested.    ONE THING IS REQUIRED BEFORE YOU COME   A three-minute form in our Mini App: your problem in one line, some context, how long it's been unresolved. Only submitted problems make the board & the vote.    WHO'S IN THE ROOM   Solo founders looking for a technical or commercial partner  engineers & builders who want to co-found, not take a job  product & GTM operators ready for zero-to-one  founders with a team who came to unstick something.   Hosted by Andrey Krylow. He greets every guest at the door, seats you at the right table, & makes the introductions - nobody stands alone at this event.   WHAT'S GUARANTEED: a curated room, two working sessions, mutual matches within 48 hours. WHAT WE DON'T PROMISE: a co-founder by the end of the evening, or a room full of investors. What we promise is the working session that tells you who's worth a second conversation.   Three rules, said out loud in sixty seconds: what's said here stays here  we share experience, not advice  moving to another table mid-session is normal.   Registration required. Check-in through the Ascent Valley Mini App inside Telegram: everyone you meet stays saved, matched & reachable after tonight.   Ascent Valley - a founder & investor ecosystem across 21 cities. IDEA  PROCESS  RESULT.

events.name: From Bench To Boardroom - Cellular Logistics, Nanobiology & VC Biotech
events.description: Every cell in your body runs a hyper-complex logistical network. Tens of thousands of tiny membrane-enveloped packages-called vesicles-ferry critical cargo like insulin, hormones, & neurotransmitters to precise destinations. If this delivery system delays by even a millisecond, or drops its cargo in the wrong place, the result is devastating human disease: diabetes, neurological disorders, & immune system failures. Understanding how cells manage this trafficking didn't just rewrite biology textbooks-it won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Medicine. But fundamental science is only half the journey. The real magic happens when world-changing research successfully leaves the academic lab to hit the commercial market. Few people have bridged this gap like Professor James Rothman, Ph.D. Originally trained in physics at Yale before pivoting to biochemistry at Harvard, Professor Rothman looks at biology through the lens of fundamental mechanics. Today, he is the Sterling Professor of Cell Biology & the Director & Founder of the Yale Nanobiology Institute, where researchers merge the physical sciences with engineering to study living systems at the nanoscale. Beyond academia, Professor Rothman is a veteran biotech founder, life science industry executive, & venture advisor. From founding ARIAD Pharmaceuticals to guiding deep-tech bio platforms like Prellis Biologics & advising firms like Celesta Capital & Arsenal, his career represents the ultimate "bench-to-boardroom" trajectory. In this exclusive fireside chat with SOSV Managing Partner Sean O'Sullivan, Professor Rothman will explore: The Cellular Supply Chain: What his Nobel-winning discovery of SNARE proteins teaches us about the ultimate "machinery" of life-and how understanding these pathways allows us to block viral entry & combat infectious diseases. The Nanobiology Era: Why human health tech is shifting away from incremental chemistry toward engineering & programming life at the molecular scale. The Translation Chasm: The raw realities of moving breakthroughs from elite university benches to commercial boardrooms. Platform vs. Product: Lessons from building scalable biotherapeutics platforms (like Prellis's bioprinted human immune systems) versus single-drug assets. The Future of Investment: What the next generation of venture capitalists & founders must understand to accurately de-risk deep tech biology. Seats are limited. Register early to save your spot! This is an in-person event. Location will be shared after you register & are approved.  Broadcast live from our SOSV NY event space, this is the next installment of SOSV Deep Tech LIVE, our video podcast series exploring the frontiers of deep tech with leading founders, researchers, & technologists.

events.name: Enterprise Security In Age Of AI
events.description: In July an OpenAI model escaped its evaluation sandbox & compromised Hugging Face's production infrastructure in a weekend. The model responsible was not publicly available. Frontier cyber capability now sits inside a handful of labs, & a gap is opening between those with access & everyone defending without it. When attacks move at machine speed & the attacker might be an AI, what does real protection even look like? Join us for a conversation with senior security & AI leaders who live these questions daily. Nick Muy: Nicholas Muy is the VP of Engineering, Platform & Security / CISO at Scrut Automation, where he leads platform engineering, security, AI governance, & agentic AI product strategy for a GRC platform serving 1,700+ customers. He's also a Venture Partner at Tidal Ventures & co-leads the Angel Syndicate at Venture in Security. He started as a childhood hacker who couldn't leave well enough alone, which led to the Department of Homeland Security, securing billions in travel transactions at Expedia, contributing to the first NIST Cybersecurity Framework v1.0, & eventually building security & product programs at high-growth startups. He reads Hobbes & Anthropic model reports with equal enthusiasm, fights engineers on architecture & marketing teams on unit economics, & doesn't discriminate against interesting problems. Mariya Vasileva: Mariya Vasileva is a Senior Research Scientist at Meta, where she studies multimodal model behavior, safety & alignment, & the scalable evaluation of frontier AI systems. Her research focuses on understanding how models behave under complex constraints & developing rigorous methods for evaluating the reliability & security of increasingly agentic systems. Previously, she developed auditing methodologies for high-impact machine-learning & computer-vision systems at AWS. She holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. John Kitaoka: John Kitaoka is a research fellow at MATS Research working on dangerous capability evaluations & scalable oversight for multi-agent systems with UK AISI & US CAISI. Prior to MATS, John worked with scientists at Harvard & Lawrence Livermore National Labs on automated red-teaming & verification techniques for dangerous knowledge elicitation by frontier models. He spent four years at Amazon Web Services as an AI Architect, & led AI product development for government technology sectors. His work spans scalable LLM evaluation for enterprises, multi-agent systems for critical sectors, & advising AI adoption across the public sector, & John has a background in mathematics & computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Moderated By: Yash Tulsani: Yash is a serial cybersecurity & AI founder & operator. He is currently building a new company that is creating the Intelligence Layer for Enterprise Security. Previously, he built CalypsoAI, which pioneered AI Runtime Security & AI Redteaming & was acquired by F5 Networks. Prior to CalypsoAI, Yash got his start building technology companies at UiPath, where he was lucky to see all sides of business building from early stage to public company. He started his career researching public technology companies at Credit Suisse & trading High Yield Bonds at BlackRock. Yash is just as comfortable talking about product architectures as he is about breaking down merger models. Thank you to Asymptote Labs for their partnership on this event! About South Park Commons (SPC)SPC is a technical community & venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, & technologists figure out what to work on next-what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible. Apply to SPC here.

events.name: Future Of Financial Services w/ Microsoft AI
events.description: Join Microsoft's Uzo Acholonu to discover how financial institutions deploy secure Microsoft Copilot agents to automate back-office workflows, streamline IT/HR support, & scale workforce productivity within regulated environments. In this immersive, expert-led demo event, you'll discover how to unlock organizational efficiency in financial services using Microsoft's agentic ecosystem. Watch a step-by-step build as we transition from designing context-aware personal assistants to automating high-volume internal support in Copilot Studio, demonstrating the strict governance required for safe deployment in banking & finance. Uzo Acholonu is a Senior Cloud Solutions Architect at Microsoft who specializes in designing & implementing scalable, secure, & resilient cloud architectures. He focuses on partnering with enterprise clients to align complex technical requirements with strategic business objectives, driving digital transformation & optimizing cloud infrastructure across the Microsoft Azure ecosystem. Discover how to scale workforce productivity & securely automate internal workflows within financial services through a live demonstration of Microsoft Copilot. 01Personal AI Coworkers for Financial Professionals Discover how to design context-aware AI agents tailored precisely to the daily workflows of analysts, advisors, & operations teams. Learn to leverage Copilot's capabilities to manage complex, multi-step financial tasks autonomously & radically boost individual productivity. 02Automating Internal FinServ Support Explore how to build custom agents in Copilot Studio that replace manual IT, compliance, & HR intake processes. See how streamlining high-volume support workflows reduces resolution times & successfully scales secure employee self-service across your institution. 03Architecting for Compliance & Security Watch a live, step-by-step build of intelligent agents within the Microsoft Copilot ecosystem. Learn essential best practices for data privacy, strict governance, & seamlessly deploying these automated solutions securely across your heavily regulated organization.

Those events are intentionally curated & sponsored around targeted audiences to provide a more focused networking experience.

events.name: Claude For Life Sciences
events.description: Predicting a structure takes seconds now. Deciding which binding pocket is worth a program still takes months. We are spending an evening in that gap. This one is hands-on & anchored in oncology. Early on, a computational biologist from a leading New York research institute opens a blank screen & works through a live analysis in front of the room: protein mutation analysis first, then scanning drug candidates. None of it is rehearsed. You will watch it get stuck in places, & honestly that is usually where you learn the most. Then it is your turn. We break into groups by sub-field, so you end up sitting next to people who understand your problem before you finish describing it. We close with an open floor for anyone who wants to show what they have been building. Who this is for:Computational biologists & bioinformaticians, medicinal & computational chemists, translational researchers, & the engineers & product people building tools for all of them. Never touched Claude before? Come anyway. Bringing a real problem from your work matters far more than experience with the tool. Agenda:5:00 - 5:30  Arrive, get settled, get your laptop set up 5:30 - 6:00  Kickoff: how research teams are using Claude right now, including where it falls short 6:00 - 6:30  The live analysis, built from a blank screen 6:30 - 7:15  Breakout working sessions by sub-field 7:15 - 7:45  Open demos, for anyone who wants to show what they built 7:45 - 8:00  Closing remarks, & time to keep talking What to bringA laptop A real problem from your own work, even a half-formed one Your host:Brandon Slicklein is the Claude Community Ambassador for New York City & co-founder of AuraPath AI, an AI-native enablement agency. His product & engineering work runs across fintech, legal, private equity, & education, & Claude sits inside nearly everything he builds. He started the New York community because the best conversations about this work happen in a room, not a thread. Come say hi when you arrive, he means it. LinkedIn Instagram The detailsFree, like everything we host. Space is limited. Hosted by the Claude Community in New York City. Thank you to Twilio for your support for this event!

events.name: The Scope 3 Paradox
events.description: Are you responsible for emissions you don't control? Join us for Summit in the Sky, a private panel & networking event held during Climate Week NYC 2026 at One World Trade Center. This invitation-only event brings together senior sustainability, procurement, & supply chain leaders from large corporates actively managing Scope 3 programs, to tackle the defining challenge of corporate decarbonization: being fully accountable for emissions that sit entirely outside your direct operations. Nearly 80% of sustainability leaders cite supplier data availability as their biggest barrier. Companies that actively engage suppliers are nine times more likely to hit their Scope 3 targets, yet only one in three currently do so. This panel gets into what leading companies are actually doing about it. This is a closed event held under Chatham House rules. If you're a senior sustainability, procurement, or supply chain leader interested in joining the conversation, please request to attend above. Program Timeline 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM : Welcome Refreshments & Networking 12:00 PM - 1:00 PM: Panel Discussion: The Scope 3 Paradox: Accountable without Control 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM: Networking Lunch 2:00 PM - 3:00 PM: Panel Discussion: Beyond the Trilemma, The Four Forces Shaping Data Center Energy 3:00 PM - 4:00 PM: Networking Our PanelistsSpeaker information coming soon. About GO2 Markets GO2 Markets is a Berlin-headquartered firm dedicated to helping companies achieve measurable environmental progress. With an operational presence in 65+ countries, our team combines in-house advisory & markets expertise to support clients worldwide in shaping & reaching their sustainability goals.

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: Building Unified AI Workspace Across Enterprise Data
events.description: ODSC AI Skills Accelerator x Snowflake | New York City We meet at: 6:00 PM ET Location: Nomadworks, 240 West 40th Street, New York, NY 10018 Speaker: Joyce Avila, Chief Innovation Officer, DataWorthy.ai This event is part of the ODSC AI Skills Accelerator, bringing together AI & data professionals for practical sessions focused on real-world AI. Join ODSC AI & Snowflake in NYC to explore how Snowflake CoWork & CoCo can bring enterprise data together into a unified, no-code AI workspace. About the Session Organizations are rapidly enabling their teams to operational AI using governed data from multiple sources. However, most knowledge workers & business analysts can't afford the friction of protracted engineering projects or complex orchestration frameworks. This session demonstrates how Snowflake CowWork, powered by the no-code Snowflake CoCo experience, can become a unified "front door" to enterprise data spanning Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake Marketplace listings, native Snowflake tables, & staged unstructured files. We will walk through the design of a CoWork workspace that brings together customer profiles & engagement signals from Salesforce Data 360, third-party enrichment data from Marketplace, & internal fact tables in Snowflake, while also incorporating uploaded documents & other unstructured assets. Attendees will see how to declaratively describe data sources, define guardrails, & expose AI-driven workflows without writing traditional application code. By the end of the session, participants will have a concrete blueprint for delivering a no-code, agentic workspace where business users can ask complex questions, trigger guided actions, & collaborate on decisions across Salesforce Data 360, Marketplace data, internal Snowflake assets, & unstructured content. And, importantly, we'll learn how all of this can be achieved without sacrificing governance, performance, or architectural integrity. Come for the hands-on insights & stay to connect with NYC's AI & data community over complimentary food & drinks.  Space is limited, register to save your spot!

events.name: Betting On Open Source - Post-Training Models In Production
events.description: Join EliseAI & Baseten for an evening exploring how teams can adapt open-source models for specific use cases, deploy them reliably in production, & keep pace with a rapidly evolving ecosystem. Engineers from both teams will compare strategies for adapting & improving open-source models: when fine-tuning & other post-training techniques are worthwhile, when harness engineering is the better approach, how to build accurate benchmarks & reliable ground-truth datasets, & how to hill-climb on evals without optimizing for the wrong signals. They'll also discuss the performance, infrastructure, & reliability challenges that emerge at scale. We'll kick things off with a short technical discussion, followed by an open Q&A & networking with engineers, researchers, & builders from across the AI ecosystem. Come for the technical deep dive, stay for drinks & conversation with others building at the frontier of AI. What to expect: 6:00 PM: Doors open, Pizza & Drinks  6:45 PM: Panel: Post-Training Models in Production 7:15 PM: Open Q&A & Technical Deep Dive 7:45 PM: Networking & Community 9:00 PM: Doors Close   About us: EliseAI builds AI automation for the housing & healthcare industries, which together make up 40% of American household spending. Our AI powers operations across the full customer & resident lifecycle-from initial inquiry & leasing through ongoing resident engagement, renewals, & other critical workflows. Today, one in six leasing apartments in the U.S. runs on EliseAI. Baseten is the training & inference platform behind some of the most demanding AI workloads in production for companies like Abridge, Cursor, Notion, & OpenEvidence.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. Learn more & apply before Wednesday, September 17, at 12:00 PM; apply here. Do you work for a Government agency/department?If you work for a government agency/department & want to purchase a general admission ticket by check or purchase order (PO), government ticket opportunities close on Wednesday, September 17, by 5:00 PM. Please email us at citycamp@beta.nyc. Sponsors, want to support the conference?We're looking for mission-aligned sponsors to help cover conference costs, including meals, coffee, childcare, & ASL interpretation. Learn more about our opportunities to support by filling out this form. Press & Media: Interested in covering the event?Media credentials are available to reporters, editors working as reporters, producers, video camera operators, & still photographers who present valid press identification. If you want to attend to cover a session or the event, email us your valid press identification to citycamp@beta.nyc. We will follow up. General Event Information:What is included in my ticket? All tickets include access to a full day of conference sessions, lunch, snacks, & coffee. We offer free, professional on-site childcare. Space is limited. Please register if you are interested. Childcare We have contracted on-site childcare for children under the age of 18. In order to use this service, you MUST be a ticket-holder, & you MUST register your child(ren) before September 11th by acquiring a Childcare Ticket. Each child you register requires a ticket registration. There are limited spots available, so please sign up sooner rather than later! If you have any questions, please email us at citycamp+childcare@beta.nyc. Accessibility & Accommodations We want CityCamp to be usable by everyone who wants to take part. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available upon request. Service animals are always welcome. The conference is delivered in English & uses technical terms. If you need ASL interpretation, or have any other accessibility question or request, email us at citycamp@beta.nyc by Friday, September 4. Requests after that date are welcome, & we will do what we can, but we cannot promise to fill them. Code of Conduct BetaNYC is committed to hosting safe & open spaces for all. By participating in this space, you are committing yourself to BetaNYC's Code of Conduct & Anti-Harassment Policy. Health Policy If you're not feeling well, PLEASE stay home. We strive to create a safe environment for everyone. (Please see our refund policy for questions.) We encourage everyone to wear a high-quality mask at all times (except when eating & drinking). We will have ample KF-94 masks in various sizes for you to wear. Masks keep our staff, volunteers, & attendees safe. Masking helps prevent the spread of viruses - this is science, based on data! Refund Policy Contact us to request a refund. We will try to honor all of your refund requests at citycamp+refund@beta.nyc. Please note that some ticketing fees are nonrefundable.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: WorkOS & You.com Agenda 5:30 pm - 5:35 pmWelcome & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  5:35 pm - 5:50 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  5:50 pm - 6:05 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from WorkOS TBA Outline:TBA  6:05 pm - 6:20 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from You.com TBA Outline:TBA  6:20 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:30 pm - 6:40 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:40 pm - 6:50 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:50 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. events.name: From Lab To Scale - Building Northeast's Climate Innovation Pipeline
events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. Over Greentown's 15-year history, the organization has supported 700+ startups that have gone on to raise $15B+ & create 16,000+ jobs. Greentown has hubs in Somerville & Houston, so while most of our members are based in Massachusetts or Texas, our membership is growing beyond these two states, & we intend to double down on that growth. New York's climate & energy ecosystem, with some of the country's most ambitious climate policy, deepest capital markets, & strongest research institutions, is a critical part of where we see Greentown's impact growing next, & this event is one step toward building deeper roots here. Please join the Greentown leadership team to discuss how we can collectively shape the future of climate & energy innovation in New York & Massachusetts - we want to hear from you! You'll be joined by climate & energy leaders from the investment community, large corporates, government, foundations, academia, & the startup community itself, from the Northeast & beyond. Space is limited to keep the conversation intimate, so we hope you'll RSVP soon. Potential topics of discussion include: Seeding & sourcing innovation: How Massachusetts' & New York's university & research ecosystems can learn from each other to build a stronger, more connected pipeline from lab to startup Bridging the Second Valley of Death: How public dollars (through NYSERDA & MassCEC) & private capital across both states can help the most promising climate & energy companies scale from prototype to commercial pilot Keeping manufacturing in the Northeast: How Massachusetts & New York can work together, through shared infrastructure or incentives, to keep growing manufacturers here instead of losing them to other regions Lunch will be provided. Once our discussion wraps up, we invite you to stay for the Greentown Startup Showcase from 1:30 to 3:30 PM to see climate innovation in action. Big thanks to our venue sponsor, SOSV! Agenda (times in ET) 12:30 PM - 12:40 PM: Welcome & mingling 12:40 PM - 12:50 PM: Welcome remarks / presentation from Greentown CEO Georgina Campbell Flatter 12:50 PM - 1:20 PM: VIP discussion on cross-border climate & energy collaboration 1:20 PM - 1:30 PM: Wrap up & establish next steps to increase collaboration between Massachusetts & New York 1:30 PM: Beginning of Startup Showcase event About Greentown As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Greentown enables entrepreneurs to bring their technologies into the world through world-class incubation support, programs for collaborative innovation, & a global ecosystem of corporates, investors, researchers, governments, & philanthropists dedicated to scaling transformational technologies. Greentown Labs, the world's largest climatetech incubator network, provides entrepreneurs mission-critical access to labs, equipment, customers, capital, talent, community, & resources for business growth at its flagship incubators in Somerville, MA & Houston, TX. Please note: By registering for this event, you consent to your name, title, & company/organization being shared with other event attendees. You consent to your image or likeness being used in content associated with the event. You release Greentown Labs & all partners from any & all liability stemming from any event-related incident.

events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

Expect good conversation, good energy, & a few surprises. Voice AI should be easy, & we're excited to prove it.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). GP returning for 2026 Invited Founders & Fund Managers  Nicholas Flanders - Co-Founder & CEO, Twelve (turning CO into jet fuel, backed by TPG Rise Climate)  Martijn Lopes Cardozo - Partner, Regeneration.VC (Leonardo DiCaprio-backed circular economy fund)  Brian Riordan - Co-Founder & COO, Avalanche Energy (compact fusion systems advancing next-generation clean energy)  Daria Saharova - General Partner, World Fund (350M European climate VC. Joining SF 2026)  Mira Inbar - Partner, ArcTern Ventures ($500M+ deployed into climate tech across 40+ companies. Joining SF 2026)  Jocelyn Matyas - Cisco Foundation (supporting climate innovation & early-stage impact ventures)  More speakers to be announced $110 BILLION in committed capital represented in this room. This is an 150-person event. Reach out to us at : team@wetheatlas.com WHAT HAPPENED AFTER OUR LAST SUMMITS This is not a talking shop. Capital moves in this room. $15M Raised - Twelve (SAF Carbon Transformation). An introduction made through our summit network connected Twelve - the company turning CO into jet fuel & chemicals for Mercedes-Benz, P&G, & British Airways - with the CMA CGM Saad family office. Result: $15M raised to scale the technology that's replacing fossil fuels with air & water. $37M+ in Funds LPs Investments Value Facilitated in 2025. Across our summits & coalition network, Atlas team facilitated more than $37M in transaction value between LPs & GPs of frontier & climate tech funds in a single year. 500+ Investor-Innovators Connections Made. Our events don't end when the panels do. Through structured 1:1 matching, post-event introductions, & the WeTheAtlas platform, our summits have generated over 500 qualified LP-GPs connections since 2024. Every number on this page is real. We don't count badge scans. We count capital deployed. THE FORMAT: BUILT FOR DEALS, NOT PANELS This is not a 3,000-person conference with a lanyard & a prayer. Here's exactly how the day works: 150 attendees. That's it. We cap attendance & curate every seat. Ratio target: 50% LPs & family offices, 30% GPs & fund managers, 20% frontier tech founders. Everyone in the room is either writing checks or building companies worth funding. Structured 1:1 Investor-Founder Matching. Every sponsors is matched with up to 10 relevant connections before the event through our WeTheAtlas matching system. You'll arrive knowing exactly who to meet, what time & which table number - no cold intros, no wasted conversations. 3 Deep-Dive Panels (Not TED Talks) Moderated discussions with founders & investors who are in the trenches - not keynotes from people selling you a vision. Topics this year:  Energy Abundance: Nuclear Power, SAF & the New Economics of the Energy Renaissance  From Bits to Atoms: Physical AI, Robotics & the Climate Resilient Infrastructure Revolution  LP & GP Perspectives: Deploying Capital in Vital, Frontier Tech, Resilience & the Rise of Secondaries  Old Money, New Frontiers: Foundations, Endowments & Corporates Are Funding Existential Resilience  The 2026 Portfolio: How Family Offices Are Navigating War, Tariffs, Reshoring & the New World Order About WeTheAtlas WeTheAtlas is the capital mobilization platform for frontier & climate tech. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. events.name: Product Leaders Breakfast - AI Graveyards
events.description: Every team has an AI graveyard by now: the copilot nobody opens anymore, the agent workflow that quietly got abandoned, the AI role we invented & then un-invented, the model policy we were completely sure about eighteen months ago. But everyone also has a short list: the AI that stuck so well it's just how we work now. At this breakfast, we'll dig into both: what died, what survived, & what evolved into something nobody predicted. And what all of it says about how AI actually takes hold inside an organization. Come ready to name one thing you buried & one thing that stuck. The burials are usually the better story. If you've never been to our breakfast before:We bring together curated groups of PM leaders to connect & share learnings & insights over casual breakfast. We carefully & thoughtfully curate discussion groups. Please fill out the "Request to Join" form & we'll send invitations out if you're selected. Please note that spots are limited & depending on demand, we may not be able to get back to you if you're not selected. If you are selected & are unable to make it, please do your best to RSVP "no" within at least 3 business days of the event so that we can offer your seat to someone on the waitlist. For nearly three decades, ITX has helped mid- to large-sized companies solve complex business challenges through custom digital product development that drives growth, operational efficiency, & customer loyalty. As a remote-first, globally distributed company, ITX pairs a big-picture focus on outcomes with a responsive, easy-to-work-with approach that keeps every engagement smooth, collaborative, & productive.

events.name: Product Evenings - AI PM Playbook
events.description: Join us for an evening with Sebastian Misiurek, Senior Product Manager - Omniverse at NVIDIA, as he explores the new playbook for building advanced AI products. Sebastian will share how to navigate the intersection of physical AI, digital twins, & agentic workflows to drive scalable innovation. As AI expands into physical environments & autonomous systems, product managers need a new playbook. Sebastian Misiurek will unpack how to design digital twin architectures, automate pipelines with agentic workflows, & maintain human oversight. Expect practical insights on managing advanced AI systems, balancing autonomy with governance, & building safe, scalable products. Sebastian Misiurek is a Computational Designer & Design Leader who specializes in the intersection of advanced computational methodologies, digital fabrication, & architectural innovation. He focuses on leveraging parametric design & emerging 3D technologies to translate complex spatial concepts into functional, scalable, & highly immersive physical & digital experiences. Building next-generation AI products demands new frameworks for architecture & oversight. Sebastian Misiurek shares how product managers can leverage digital twins, deploy agentic workflows, & implement strategic governance to ensure safe & scalable AI solutions. 01Physical AI & Digital Twin Architecture Explore how to bridge the gap between physical environments & digital spaces by leveraging digital twin architecture to build robust, spatial AI products. 02Agentic Workflows & Pipeline Automation Discover how to design & implement agentic workflows that automate complex pipelines, enabling AI systems to efficiently execute multi-step tasks. 03Strategic Governance & Human-in-the-Loop Control Learn how to establish critical oversight mechanisms, balancing autonomous AI capabilities with human-in-the-loop control to mitigate risk & ensure reliable outcomes.

events.name: Building Slack's Simplified Layout Mode
events.description: This event will be online on YouTube & in-person (New York City). The speaker & live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page & someone will come down ASAP. DescriptionSlack is a powerful hub for work & communication, but its dense & complex interface can be a barrier for users with motor, vision, & cognitive disabilities. To help more people use Slack effectively, we introduced Simplified Layout Mode on desktop & web. This preference transforms Slack into a single-column layout that is easier to navigate & has fewer distractions. In this session, we will demo Simplified Layout Mode & discuss its evolution from an accommodation request by an ALS advocacy group to a feature that benefits multiple audiences. Along the way, we'll share specific examples of how its design was shaped by our partnerships with disabled & neurodivergent users. Attendees will learn ... How to collect & synthesize feedback from different groups of users with disabilities over the course of a feature's developmentHow to collaborate with internal employee disability groups to get feedback & build momentum around a featurePresenter biosChris Xu is a director of product management of Slack looking after accessibility & design systems. Outside of product management, they have had a wide-ranging career focused on how technology & communities shape each other. They live in Brooklyn, NY & hold strong opinions about fruit. Lena Wang is a frontend software engineer at Slack working on accessibility & design systems. Outside of engineering, she's usually mid-side-quest - whether that's walking the entire length of Manhattan on a whim, running a Taco Bell 5k, or competing in a city-wide scavenger hunt. She lives in Manhattan, NY. Kaili Liang is a Software Engineer at Slack, working on accessibility & design systems. In her free time, she loves chasing new eats, diving into books, trying various arts & crafts, & traveling. AccessibilityThe presentation will have human captions [CC], not automatic captions. For ASL preferred speakers, learn about the Aira ASL App, & download it before the event. For the Blind & Low Vision community, learn about the Aira Explorer App & download it before the event. To access the online webinar for audio description, use the A11yNYC Access Offer to call, or simply inform your Visual Interpreter that you'd like that offer applied when you connect. For additional accessibility requirements, please email meryl@equalentry.com two weeks before the event. LivestreamYouTube Provided by Internet Society Accessibility SIG. Location detailsThe event is at 72 Spring street on the 4th floor. Everyone must be accompanied to the event on the 4th floor. Because everyone needs to be escorted, please arrive early or on time. When you enter the ground floor, a representative from A11yNYC will be there to provide elevator access. TransitThe building 72 Spring street is near several transit stops: 6 train Spring Street (non-accessible stop): 100 feetCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.4 milesB/D/F/M trains Broadway-Lafayette Street (accessible stop), 0.2 milesN/Q/R/W trains Prince Street (non-accessible stop): 0.2 milesCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.3 milesM1 / M55 Bus lines Broadway/Spring Street stop: 500 feetCabs & rideshares can let passengers out right near the building entrance. Finding the buildingIn Google Maps, find 72 Spring street. It shows the correct location of the entrance: on Spring Street, halfway between Crosby & Lafayette.It's also between the Glossier store & the Krewe Eyewear store.Inside & over the reception desk in our building 72 Spring st, it says Marc Jacobs. Traveling to the event?We recommend Hotel on Rivington or Crosby Street Hotel. AccreditationAll A11yNYC meetups are pre-approved for IAAP Continuing Accessibility Education Credits (CAEC). SponsorsThanks to Aira, AKQA, Deque, Evinced, Equal Entry, & Fable for sponsoring. Want to be a sponsor? Contact meryl@equalentry.com

events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.name: Leaders In Fintech - Evolution Of Agentic Commerce
events.description: Join leading AI & product executives as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. Drawing on experience scaling complex transactional infrastructure, the panel will unpack practical models for deploying autonomous agents, securing machine-to-machine payments, & capturing enterprise value in agent-driven markets. Andr Kerr is the Director, Applied AI Lab at American Express, leading the strategy & execution of AI-driven product development. With a strong engineering background, he focuses on integrating generative AI technologies to enhance customer experiences & drive innovation within the financial services sector. Sailaja is a Director, Product Management - Agent Pay at Mastercard, where she launches innovative payment products across North America. She partners with major tech platforms & issuers to scale tokenized solutions that secure & simplify transactions, & brings 10+ years of experience across fintech, banking, & regulation driving innovation in complex, highly regulated environments. Join our panel of fintech leaders as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. They will unpack practical models for scaling autonomous execution across complex financial ecosystems while prioritizing security & customer trust. 01From Recommendations to Transactions Explore how AI systems are evolving from advisory roles to autonomous decision-makers capable of completing complex financial transactions. Learn how teams are designing products that seamlessly bridge conversational interactions with real-world execution. 02Trust, Security, & Payment Infrastructure Discover how leading institutions build secure, scalable payment rails designed specifically for autonomous agents. We'll examine how leaders manage risk, balance authorization with autonomy, & ensure ironclad trust across machine-driven financial interactions. 03The Machine-to-Machine Product Playbook Examine the strategies & frameworks product leaders use to build, launch, & scale machine-to-machine financial products. Learn how to adapt traditional product management playbooks to meet the demands of an increasingly agentic commerce ecosystem. What's IncludedGourmet Light Refreshments - Enjoy a curated selection of artisanal bites & small plates, perfect for connecting with colleagues.Settle in for easy conversation & good company in a warm, welcoming space. With a thoughtful selection of beer & wine on hand, it's the perfect backdrop for winding down or catching up.Have dietary restrictions? To ensure we can accommodate your dietary needs, please inform us at least 48 hours before the workshop start date.
