events.name: HealthTech Launchathon & ClawCamp
events.description: Note: we are postponing & redesigning this event for September. This was a new event type & let's just say, it wasn't as popular as we thought it would be so, in true crowd-validator style, we are going back to the drawing board. Please contact us if you have constructive feedback. Thanks & Stay tuned!Alex Fair Original write up - subject to change. Presented by MedStartr in Partnership with ClawCamp You bring the vision. We'll help you launch a company - in a weekend. Healthcare is broken in a hundred ways we all see daily. You've felt it as a patient. diagnosed it as a clinician. doded around it as a builder, & hated it as a person who came into healthcare to help people. The things you see that could be better are hard to fix, & it bothers you that they seem incorrigible. But then you got an idea of something that could help, if you could just build it & get it in the hands of people like you to help patients get better care & the system & caregivers to give better care. We know, we have met thousands of you & ARE you too. That's why we have run this group for almost 18 years & done so many events. But now, with the help of AI & the new MedStartr.ai platform, we can help even more. So we created what we are calling a "Launchathon" to help with all that & this is the first one! The NYC HealthTech Launchathon is your chance to do something about it. No startup experience required. No coding background needed. Just bring your problem, your perspective, & your curiosity - & we'll bring the AI tools, expert faculty, mentors, investors, & community to help you build something real. The Program: 3 Phases, 8 Weeks  Phase I  HealthTech ClawCamp  August 1-2 **Day 1 - August 1 | Stack AI HQ, One World Trade Center**Learn. Ideate. Validate with Experts on hand & Build or add to your team from other folks like yourself. Meet amazing people. Pitch problems. Learn from expert AI faculty, upskill. Present or Find a problem worth solving - & the team to solve it with. No startup idea or coding required, but bring your passion to build solutions to the problems in healthcare. Day 2 - August 2 | Arya Health HQ, NYC**Build Something Real. Build prototypes. Validate ideas. Design workflows. Interview users. Use AI, code, & creativity. Leave Day 2 with something real - a working prototype posted to MedStartr.ai Qualifies you for Phase II (Also Awards of tokens & other great stuff from Day 2 Winners)  Phase II  MedStartr Crowd Challenge  August 2 - October 6 Your Build goes live on MedStartr.ai where 250,000+ credentialed healthcare stakeholders - patients, clinicians, investors, partners - can review, comment, follow, pilot, & share. More eyes. More feedback. More signal on what actually matters. Teams keep building & iterating based on what the crowd says.  Phase III  Launchathon Finals  October 6Health Impact Forum  Microsoft  Times Square, NYC The top crowd-validated teams take the stage at one of NYC's biggest healthcare innovation gatherings. Compete for **over $1 million** in investment, accelerator spots, pilots, partnerships, software credits, & everything a startup needs to succeed. Keynote SpeakersDay 1: Khan Siddiqui, MDCEO & Co-Founder, HOPPR  2025 SIIM Imaging Informatics Innovator"From Hacking to Scale" Brian Yarnell3x Exited HealthTech Founder Day 2: Grace Cordovano, PhDBoard Certified Patient Advocate  CancerX*"Designing for the Patient Experience"* 15 other MedStartr Mentors & 7 AI expert trainers to help you validate, plan & build your ideas out better & faster## Who Should Attend? This is for **everyone who touches healthcare** - not just developers: -  **Clinicians** - physicians, nurses, NPs, PAs who see broken workflows daily-  **Patients & caregivers** - living the gaps in care & navigation firsthand-  **Admins & billers** - revenue cycle, coding, & operations insiders-  **Researchers** - with data, insights, & unmet needs to solve-  **Tech co-founders** - developers & AI builders seeking high-impact problems (apply for discounted tickets)-  **Early founders** - ideas at any stage, ready to validate fast MedStartr Challenge Winners are 22 more likely to succeed. --- There are many more ticket Types available on MedStartr.ai/launchathon: | Type | Price | Details ||------|-------|---------|| General Admission | $50| Open enrollment || Two Pack | $80| Everything is better with friends || VIP | $100 | Dedicated mentor time + Health Impact Forum ticket || Early Bird | $0-25 | Apply to attend - going fast || Tech Co-Founder | $50 | Apply - discounted for technical builders || Mentor | Free | Apply via MedStartr.ai || Volunteer | Free | Help us run the event || Demo Table | $1,000 | Table for laptop, monitor + 1 rollup banner | Register & buy tickets here or for more options [visit the MedStartr.ai Healthcare Innovation platform with more details!](http://medstartr.ai/launchathon) Confirmed Sponsors Arya Health  Stack.ai  Health Impact Forum Interested in sponsoring?Five tiers from $2,500 Community to $50,000 Title. About MedStartr 17 years building the global healthcare innovation community. 9,000+ innovations reviewed. 250,000+ credentialed stakeholders. 1,200+ events in 41 cities. The team behind over 120 contests & crowdchallenges for over 200 sponsors since 2010. We also run the investment funds & accelerators, also named MedStartr where we invest in & accelerate the teams that win challenges like this one. Check out the new [MedStartr.ai](http://medstartr.ai) alpha Just Launched 7/14/2026! About ClawCamp ClawCamp is a global community advancing mastery of AI agents - from first personal agent to advanced multi-agent workflows. 1,400+ events  120+ cities  100,000+ attendees trained. The AI training backbone of the Launchathon build weekend. Visit them at clawcamp.us Khan Siddiqui, MDDr. Khan Siddiqui is a physician-entrepreneur, technologist, & radiologist at the forefront of the medical AI revolution. As CEO & Co-Founder of HOPPR, he leads the development of advanced multimodal foundation models designed to democratize AI training & accelerate medical imaging development for healthcare systems worldwide.He previously served as Chief Medical Officer & Chief Strategy Officer of Hyperfine, where he helped take the company public & deploy Swoop - the world's first FDA-cleared, portable bedside MRI system. In 2012 he founded higi, a consumer health network of thousands of biometric screening kiosks across North American pharmacies, culminating in a multi-billion-dollar acquisition. Earlier, as a principal program manager & AI architect at Microsoft, he designed the deep-learning image infrastructure used to train the Xbox Kinect. A recognized pioneer in imaging informatics, Dr. Siddiqui received the 2025 Imaging Informatics Innovator Award from the Society for Imaging Informatics in Medicine (SIIM) & holds dozens of patents across medical image processing, machine learning, & healthcare analytics.

events.name: GTM Leaders, Vol. 1 - Breaking Through The AI Slop
events.description: NYC GTM Leaders, Vol. 1: Breaking Through the AI Slop Every channel is flooded with machine-generated outreach, & your buyers have stopped paying attention to any of it. So what still breaks through? Join us Thursday, August 27th in Midtown (address shared upon approval) for an off-the-record evening with GTM leaders who are figuring it out in real time. Capped at 50 so the conversations stay focused & real. The agenda: 6:30 pm: Doors open. Drinks, light bites, & an icebreaker to get the room talking. 7:00 pm: GTM Insight Talks. Three quick-hit talks from operators actually running these plays: using AI for lead gen without sounding like AI, thought leadership as a channel buyers still trust, & a head-to-head teardown of real GTM stacks. Q&A after. 7:30 pm: Working session. Small groups, hands-on. Apply the plays to your own pipeline. 8:00 pm: Round two networking. Now that everyone has shared context, conversations go deeper. 8:30 pm: Close & a first look at Vol. 2. Who should request an invite: GTM leaders at Series A+ startups Founders (Series A+, 2+ years in) Heads of Growth at scaling companies Seats are limited & approved individually. Request your invite now. Your hosts: Tanny Kang is Co-founder & COO at Vibranium Labs, an a16z-backed startup building AI-native incident management. A former Big Law tech attorney who traded redlines for pipeline, he now runs GTM end to end & has closed enterprise customers like Shutterstock, where Vibe OnCall cut manual incident work by 70% across 300+ engineers. He also writes Incidents.World, a newsletter on all things on-call. Josh Kim is Chief of Staff, GTM & Growth at Remy by MindStudio, an AI agent that builds enterprise-grade apps from a plain-language spec doc. A former Fortune 500 data & analytics consultant at Kantar, he's since helped drive 1.5x revenue growth & grown a community of 10,000+ builders, execs, & investors. Eric Fleshman is a GTM Engineer who has built go-to-market functions from the ground up, including founding GTME roles. His focus is what still breaks through when every inbox is machine-generated noise: technical depth, human-first outreach, & intent-driven systems. Signal first, intent after. He's an AlphaForge Architect Award winner from his Clay cohort & loves coffee, climbing & traveling! About Vibranium Labs: At vibraniumlabs.ai, we build Vibe OnCall, the #1 AI incident commander that proactively hunts down issues in your eng org before engineers ever get paged. We help engineering teams stay ahead of incidents, cut down on 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence. Our mission is straightforward: Prevent Incidents, Not Just Respond: Equip engineering orgs with an AI incident commander that proactively surfaces issues before they page anyone. Reduce On-Call Burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build Lasting Reliability: Offer ongoing tuning & partnership so Vibe OnCall keeps learning your systems & gets sharper the longer it runs.

events.name: Building Slack's Simplified Layout Mode
events.description: This event will be online on YouTube & in-person (New York City). The speaker & live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page & someone will come down ASAP. DescriptionSlack is a powerful hub for work & communication, but its dense & complex interface can be a barrier for users with motor, vision, & cognitive disabilities. To help more people use Slack effectively, we introduced Simplified Layout Mode on desktop & web. This preference transforms Slack into a single-column layout that is easier to navigate & has fewer distractions. In this session, we will demo Simplified Layout Mode & discuss its evolution from an accommodation request by an ALS advocacy group to a feature that benefits multiple audiences. Along the way, we'll share specific examples of how its design was shaped by our partnerships with disabled & neurodivergent users. Attendees will learn ... How to collect & synthesize feedback from different groups of users with disabilities over the course of a feature's developmentHow to collaborate with internal employee disability groups to get feedback & build momentum around a featurePresenter biosChris Xu is a director of product management of Slack looking after accessibility & design systems. Outside of product management, they have had a wide-ranging career focused on how technology & communities shape each other. They live in Brooklyn, NY & hold strong opinions about fruit. Lena Wang is a frontend software engineer at Slack working on accessibility & design systems. Outside of engineering, she's usually mid-side-quest - whether that's walking the entire length of Manhattan on a whim, running a Taco Bell 5k, or competing in a city-wide scavenger hunt. She lives in Manhattan, NY. Kaili Liang is a Software Engineer at Slack, working on accessibility & design systems. In her free time, she loves chasing new eats, diving into books, trying various arts & crafts, & traveling. AccessibilityThe presentation will have human captions [CC], not automatic captions. For ASL preferred speakers, learn about the Aira ASL App, & download it before the event. For the Blind & Low Vision community, learn about the Aira Explorer App & download it before the event. To access the online webinar for audio description, use the A11yNYC Access Offer to call, or simply inform your Visual Interpreter that you'd like that offer applied when you connect. For additional accessibility requirements, please email meryl@equalentry.com two weeks before the event. LivestreamYouTube Provided by Internet Society Accessibility SIG. Location detailsThe event is at 72 Spring street on the 4th floor. Everyone must be accompanied to the event on the 4th floor. Because everyone needs to be escorted, please arrive early or on time. When you enter the ground floor, a representative from A11yNYC will be there to provide elevator access. TransitThe building 72 Spring street is near several transit stops: 6 train Spring Street (non-accessible stop): 100 feetCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.4 milesB/D/F/M trains Broadway-Lafayette Street (accessible stop), 0.2 milesN/Q/R/W trains Prince Street (non-accessible stop): 0.2 milesCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.3 milesM1 / M55 Bus lines Broadway/Spring Street stop: 500 feetCabs & rideshares can let passengers out right near the building entrance. Finding the buildingIn Google Maps, find 72 Spring street. It shows the correct location of the entrance: on Spring Street, halfway between Crosby & Lafayette.It's also between the Glossier store & the Krewe Eyewear store.Inside & over the reception desk in our building 72 Spring st, it says Marc Jacobs. Traveling to the event?We recommend Hotel on Rivington or Crosby Street Hotel. AccreditationAll A11yNYC meetups are pre-approved for IAAP Continuing Accessibility Education Credits (CAEC). SponsorsThanks to Aira, AKQA, Deque, Evinced, Equal Entry, & Fable for sponsoring. Want to be a sponsor? Contact meryl@equalentry.com

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. Her experience is specialized in the digital health space, & she enjoys building community & connecting people in the space. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: Leaders In Fintech - Evolution Of Agentic Commerce
events.description: Join leading AI & product executives as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. Drawing on experience scaling complex transactional infrastructure, the panel will unpack practical models for deploying autonomous agents, securing machine-to-machine payments, & capturing enterprise value in agent-driven markets. Andr Kerr is the Director, Applied AI Lab at American Express, leading the strategy & execution of AI-driven product development. With a strong engineering background, he focuses on integrating generative AI technologies to enhance customer experiences & drive innovation within the financial services sector. Sailaja is a Director, Product Management - Agent Pay at Mastercard, where she launches innovative payment products across North America. She partners with major tech platforms & issuers to scale tokenized solutions that secure & simplify transactions, & brings 10+ years of experience across fintech, banking, & regulation driving innovation in complex, highly regulated environments. Join our panel of fintech leaders as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. They will unpack practical models for scaling autonomous execution across complex financial ecosystems while prioritizing security & customer trust. 01From Recommendations to Transactions Explore how AI systems are evolving from advisory roles to autonomous decision-makers capable of completing complex financial transactions. Learn how teams are designing products that seamlessly bridge conversational interactions with real-world execution. 02Trust, Security, & Payment Infrastructure Discover how leading institutions build secure, scalable payment rails designed specifically for autonomous agents. We'll examine how leaders manage risk, balance authorization with autonomy, & ensure ironclad trust across machine-driven financial interactions. 03The Machine-to-Machine Product Playbook Examine the strategies & frameworks product leaders use to build, launch, & scale machine-to-machine financial products. Learn how to adapt traditional product management playbooks to meet the demands of an increasingly agentic commerce ecosystem. What's IncludedGourmet Light Refreshments - Enjoy a curated selection of artisanal bites & small plates, perfect for connecting with colleagues.Settle in for easy conversation & good company in a warm, welcoming space. With a thoughtful selection of beer & wine on hand, it's the perfect backdrop for winding down or catching up.Have dietary restrictions? To ensure we can accommodate your dietary needs, please inform us at least 48 hours before the workshop start date.

events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. Learn more & apply before Wednesday, September 17, at 12:00 PM; apply here. Do you work for a Government agency/department?If you work for a government agency/department & want to purchase a general admission ticket by check or purchase order (PO), government ticket opportunities close on Wednesday, September 17, by 5:00 PM. Please email us at citycamp@beta.nyc. Sponsors, want to support the conference?We're looking for mission-aligned sponsors to help cover conference costs, including meals, coffee, childcare, & ASL interpretation. Learn more about our opportunities to support by filling out this form. Press & Media: Interested in covering the event?Media credentials are available to reporters, editors working as reporters, producers, video camera operators, & still photographers who present valid press identification. If you want to attend to cover a session or the event, email us your valid press identification to citycamp@beta.nyc. We will follow up. General Event Information:What is included in my ticket? All tickets include access to a full day of conference sessions, lunch, snacks, & coffee. We offer free, professional on-site childcare. Space is limited. Please register if you are interested. Childcare We have contracted on-site childcare for children under the age of 18. events.name: Product Leaders Breakfast - AI Graveyards
events.description: Every team has an AI graveyard by now: the copilot nobody opens anymore, the agent workflow that quietly got abandoned, the AI role we invented & then un-invented, the model policy we were completely sure about eighteen months ago. But everyone also has a short list: the AI that stuck so well it's just how we work now. At this breakfast, we'll dig into both: what died, what survived, & what evolved into something nobody predicted. And what all of it says about how AI actually takes hold inside an organization. Come ready to name one thing you buried & one thing that stuck. The burials are usually the better story. If you've never been to our breakfast before:We bring together curated groups of PM leaders to connect & share learnings & insights over casual breakfast. We carefully & thoughtfully curate discussion groups. Please fill out the "Request to Join" form & we'll send invitations out if you're selected. Please note that spots are limited & depending on demand, we may not be able to get back to you if you're not selected. If you are selected & are unable to make it, please do your best to RSVP "no" within at least 3 business days of the event so that we can offer your seat to someone on the waitlist. For nearly three decades, ITX has helped mid- to large-sized companies solve complex business challenges through custom digital product development that drives growth, operational efficiency, & customer loyalty. As a remote-first, globally distributed company, ITX pairs a big-picture focus on outcomes with a responsive, easy-to-work-with approach that keeps every engagement smooth, collaborative, & productive.

events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.name: From Concept To Conviction - AI In The Designer's Toolkit
events.description: Join us for an evening with Mareike Carolin Keller, Product Designer at Spotify, as she explores how to move AI from an experimental tool to a core part of your design workflow. Mareike will share how to leverage AI-assisted prototyping & code generation to accelerate execution & earn rapid stakeholder buy-in. As AI tools mature, the challenge for design teams is moving from informal experimentation to practical, daily utility. Mareike Carolin Keller will unpack how to embed AI directly into sprint cycles, validate complex ideas through real-time prototyping, & replace static mockups with interactive deliverables. Expect practical insights on using AI to bridge the gap between ideation & execution, ultimately driving faster cross-functional consensus. Mareike Carolin Keller (she/her) is a Product Designer at Spotify, where she focuses on creating cohesive, human-centered experiences across Spotify's growing multi-format platform. Her work spans across discovery & systemized distribution of content, as well as social experiences - helping millions of listeners seamlessly explore music, podcasts, & audiobooks. With a background in interaction design & experimental psychology, Mareike is passionate about crafting intuitive digital experiences that connect people to culture & creativity. Integrating AI into the design process transforms individual speed into team-wide capability. Mareike Carolin Keller shares how product designers can deploy AI tools in active production, build high-fidelity prototypes, & secure stakeholder alignment before committing heavy engineering resources. 01Evolving Design Workflows at Scale Learn how to establish clear frameworks that integrate AI capability directly into daily practice, transforming individual experimentation into institutional-grade capability. 02AI-Assisted Prototyping in Production Discover how to embed AI coding tools & custom generators directly into sprint cycles to validate complex ideas & test practical mechanics in real time. 03Accelerating Stakeholder Conviction Explore how to replace static mockups with high-fidelity, interactive prototypes that demonstrate actual product behavior, reduce decision friction, & secure immediate cross-functional buy-in.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Claude For Life Sciences
events.description: Predicting a structure takes seconds now. Deciding which binding pocket is worth a program still takes months. We are spending an evening in that gap. This one is hands-on & anchored in oncology. Early on, a computational biologist from a leading New York research institute opens a blank screen & works through a live analysis in front of the room: protein mutation analysis first, then scanning drug candidates. None of it is rehearsed. You will watch it get stuck in places, & honestly that is usually where you learn the most. Then it is your turn. We break into groups by sub-field, so you end up sitting next to people who understand your problem before you finish describing it. We close with an open floor for anyone who wants to show what they have been building. Who this is for:Computational biologists & bioinformaticians, medicinal & computational chemists, translational researchers, & the engineers & product people building tools for all of them. Never touched Claude before? Come anyway. Bringing a real problem from your work matters far more than experience with the tool. Agenda:5:00 - 5:30  Arrive, get settled, get your laptop set up 5:30 - 6:00  Kickoff: how research teams are using Claude right now, including where it falls short 6:00 - 6:30  The live analysis, built from a blank screen 6:30 - 7:15  Breakout working sessions by sub-field 7:15 - 7:45  Open demos, for anyone who wants to show what they built 7:45 - 8:00  Closing remarks, & time to keep talking What to bringA laptop A real problem from your own work, even a half-formed one Your host:Brandon Slicklein is the Claude Community Ambassador for New York City & co-founder of AuraPath AI, an AI-native enablement agency. His product & engineering work runs across fintech, legal, private equity, & education, & Claude sits inside nearly everything he builds. He started the New York community because the best conversations about this work happen in a room, not a thread. Come say hi when you arrive, he means it. LinkedIn Instagram The detailsFree, like everything we host. events.name: Building Unified AI Workspace Across Enterprise Data
events.description: ODSC AI Skills Accelerator x Snowflake | New York City We meet at: 6:00 PM ET Location: Nomadworks, 240 West 40th Street, New York, NY 10018 Speaker: Joyce Avila, Chief Innovation Officer, DataWorthy.ai This event is part of the ODSC AI Skills Accelerator, bringing together AI & data professionals for practical sessions focused on real-world AI. Join ODSC AI & Snowflake in NYC to explore how Snowflake CoWork & CoCo can bring enterprise data together into a unified, no-code AI workspace. About the Session Organizations are rapidly enabling their teams to operational AI using governed data from multiple sources. However, most knowledge workers & business analysts can't afford the friction of protracted engineering projects or complex orchestration frameworks. This session demonstrates how Snowflake CowWork, powered by the no-code Snowflake CoCo experience, can become a unified "front door" to enterprise data spanning Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake Marketplace listings, native Snowflake tables, & staged unstructured files. We will walk through the design of a CoWork workspace that brings together customer profiles & engagement signals from Salesforce Data 360, third-party enrichment data from Marketplace, & internal fact tables in Snowflake, while also incorporating uploaded documents & other unstructured assets. Attendees will see how to declaratively describe data sources, define guardrails, & expose AI-driven workflows without writing traditional application code. By the end of the session, participants will have a concrete blueprint for delivering a no-code, agentic workspace where business users can ask complex questions, trigger guided actions, & collaborate on decisions across Salesforce Data 360, Marketplace data, internal Snowflake assets, & unstructured content. And, importantly, we'll learn how all of this can be achieved without sacrificing governance, performance, or architectural integrity. Come for the hands-on insights & stay to connect with NYC's AI & data community over complimentary food & drinks.  Space is limited, register to save your spot!

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: The Builders Table
events.description: The Builder's Table is a weekly meetup for building out ideas with AI agents. Every month follows a rhythm. Every meeting has a focus. Must bring a laptop! Week 1 - Ideation & collaboration We'll have 1.5 hours to talk to one another, exchange ideas, ask questions, & refine what you'll be working on for the rest of the month. In the final 30 minutes, we'll start up our agents & have them create a step-by-step plan for building out your idea. Weeks 2 & 3 - Vibecoding Both meetups will be 2 full hours of straight vibecoding your project alongside everyone else. The idea is to take the plan you made at the end of week one & start building it out. Week 4 - Demo day The goal by the end of the month is to have a working project you can demo. Don't worry - it doesn't have to be polished or anywhere near perfect. As long as you have the bare bones of your idea & can show how it works, that's all that matters. We're focused on shipping, not perfection.   -Arrive at 4:45 -This meetup is intended for anyone looking to make more time for vibecoding. No need to commit to all the meetings in order to get something out of it. The intent is to form a community that is constantly building together. So you get out what you want to put in. Meetings will happen every week of every month, so we invite you to join us for food, drinks, good vibes, & vibecoding.

events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business To 7-Figures Without Raising Venture Capital
events.description: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business to 7-Figures Without Raising Venture CapitalI built Fibe to millions of dollars in profit without raising a dollar of venture capital, without a co-founder, & without a board. I still own the whole thing. Since then I've started The Shortlist, which has just begun to hit profitability, & cofounded Outliers Summit, which runs independently as a profitable events & media company that will cross seven figures soon. We run over a hundred events a year with a tiny team. On September 3 I'm walking through exactly how, in one session. What you'll leave with: How to pick the game you're playing before you start, so the advice you take actually applies to the business you're building Why one marketing channel is enough to reach a million dollars in revenue, & how to find yours How to build distribution before you have a product. I spent years building an audience before I had a business idea, & it is the single biggest reason bootstrapping worked How to find customers who will write a $50,000 check without blinking instead of ones who argue over $20 a month Then live Q&A for the rest of the session. Come with the specific question about your business, not the general one. That is where these earn their keep. Who this is for: anyone building something they would rather own outright than raise against. If you're going after a winner-take-all market & need capital to reach escape velocity, raising is the right call & this isn't for you.at. Mine wasn't.

events.name: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. About Farzad, the host Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C.   About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: WorkOS & You.com Agenda 5:30 pm - 5:35 pmWelcome & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  5:35 pm - 5:50 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. events.name: Product Evenings - AI PM Playbook
events.description: Join us for an evening with Sebastian Misiurek, Senior Product Manager - Omniverse at NVIDIA, as he explores the new playbook for building advanced AI products. Sebastian will share how to navigate the intersection of physical AI, digital twins, & agentic workflows to drive scalable innovation. As AI expands into physical environments & autonomous systems, product managers need a new playbook. Sebastian Misiurek will unpack how to design digital twin architectures, automate pipelines with agentic workflows, & maintain human oversight. Expect practical insights on managing advanced AI systems, balancing autonomy with governance, & building safe, scalable products. Sebastian Misiurek is a Computational Designer & Design Leader who specializes in the intersection of advanced computational methodologies, digital fabrication, & architectural innovation. He focuses on leveraging parametric design & emerging 3D technologies to translate complex spatial concepts into functional, scalable, & highly immersive physical & digital experiences. Building next-generation AI products demands new frameworks for architecture & oversight. Sebastian Misiurek shares how product managers can leverage digital twins, deploy agentic workflows, & implement strategic governance to ensure safe & scalable AI solutions. 01Physical AI & Digital Twin Architecture Explore how to bridge the gap between physical environments & digital spaces by leveraging digital twin architecture to build robust, spatial AI products. 02Agentic Workflows & Pipeline Automation Discover how to design & implement agentic workflows that automate complex pipelines, enabling AI systems to efficiently execute multi-step tasks. 03Strategic Governance & Human-in-the-Loop Control Learn how to establish critical oversight mechanisms, balancing autonomous AI capabilities with human-in-the-loop control to mitigate risk & ensure reliable outcomes.

events.name: Founder Lab: NYC
events.description:
Founder Lab is a weekly build day for early-stage founders. Bring what you're stuck on — check in on what you're testing and what you learned, then get to work: office hours with investors and operators, and open build time with founders at your stage. Same day, every week.

​Who is this for?

​Founders building venture-scale startups, pre-seed to Series A — AI, deep tech, frontier, or any technical or science vertical. Connected through a common thread of relentless honesty and proof arc: something built to scale, tested and iterated on weekly.

​The System

​Every check-in runs through FounderOS, the proof engine that turns weekly work into a track record with venture visibility.

​Review Reps: How are you stuck, what did you learn, and what needs to change.

​Pressure-Test Logic: Use adversarial feedback to identify flaws in current hypotheses.

​Anchor the Roadmap: Align on near-term technical unlocks and business milestones.

​Design the Next Interval: Lock the specific success gates for the upcoming build cycle.

events.name: How to Turn Trains Into Music
events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "How to Turn Trains Into Music" 🎤 Lecturer: Joshua Wolk 📆 Date: Friday, September 4th  ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Tribeca, Manhattan
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
Every dot is a real subway train. Eight hundred of them, give or take, form a small jazz combo (walking bass, piano, sax, vibes, brushes) that has been playing without pause for over a hundred years. On the platforms they are hot, screaming, full of complaint. This is the music inside the noise.  The harmony moves through a slow chorus. A note is placed precisely where the train happens to be along its route. Rush hour fills the band with held tones; at 3 a.m. the silences grow longer. Whatever is playing now has not played before and will not play again.  Share your location and the trains nearest you grow louder. The piece rearranges itself around your body. You are listening to a portrait of where you stand, played by the city you are standing in.
Joshua Wolk is a designer and engineer who leverages data to make art.
We'll explore:
* The music all around us in every day life.
* The science of sound design.
* Basic music theory as applied to locomotives.
This might be for you if you...
* Are a music enthusiast or have interest in sound design
* Are curious about music theory in a bite sized setting
* Are intrigued by the idea of finding the art in the ordinary
* Enjoy lecture-based and conversation-focused events of any kind — think Ted Talks in bars, Lectures on Tap, or micro learning meets dinner party
* Want to switch up your usual weeknight. Why not make it interesting? 🤓

events.name: Building Unified AI Workspace Across Enterprise Data
events.description: ODSC AI Skills Accelerator x Snowflake | New York City We meet at: 6:00 PM ET Location: Nomadworks, 240 West 40th Street, New York, NY 10018 Speaker: Joyce Avila, Chief Innovation Officer, DataWorthy.ai This event is part of the ODSC AI Skills Accelerator, bringing together AI & data professionals for practical sessions focused on real-world AI. Join ODSC AI & Snowflake in NYC to explore how Snowflake CoWork & CoCo can bring enterprise data together into a unified, no-code AI workspace. About the Session Organizations are rapidly enabling their teams to operational AI using governed data from multiple sources. However, most knowledge workers & business analysts can't afford the friction of protracted engineering projects or complex orchestration frameworks. This session demonstrates how Snowflake CowWork, powered by the no-code Snowflake CoCo experience, can become a unified "front door" to enterprise data spanning Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake Marketplace listings, native Snowflake tables, & staged unstructured files. We will walk through the design of a CoWork workspace that brings together customer profiles & engagement signals from Salesforce Data 360, third-party enrichment data from Marketplace, & internal fact tables in Snowflake, while also incorporating uploaded documents & other unstructured assets. Attendees will see how to declaratively describe data sources, define guardrails, & expose AI-driven workflows without writing traditional application code. By the end of the session, participants will have a concrete blueprint for delivering a no-code, agentic workspace where business users can ask complex questions, trigger guided actions, & collaborate on decisions across Salesforce Data 360, Marketplace data, internal Snowflake assets, & unstructured content. And, importantly, we'll learn how all of this can be achieved without sacrificing governance, performance, or architectural integrity. Come for the hands-on insights & stay to connect with NYC's AI & data community over complimentary food & drinks.  Space is limited, register to save your spot!

events.name: Leaders In Fintech - Evolution Of Agentic Commerce
events.description: Join leading AI & product executives as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. Drawing on experience scaling complex transactional infrastructure, the panel will unpack practical models for deploying autonomous agents, securing machine-to-machine payments, & capturing enterprise value in agent-driven markets. Andr Kerr is the Director, Applied AI Lab at American Express, leading the strategy & execution of AI-driven product development. With a strong engineering background, he focuses on integrating generative AI technologies to enhance customer experiences & drive innovation within the financial services sector. Sailaja is a Director, Product Management - Agent Pay at Mastercard, where she launches innovative payment products across North America. She partners with major tech platforms & issuers to scale tokenized solutions that secure & simplify transactions, & brings 10+ years of experience across fintech, banking, & regulation driving innovation in complex, highly regulated environments. Join our panel of fintech leaders as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. They will unpack practical models for scaling autonomous execution across complex financial ecosystems while prioritizing security & customer trust. 01From Recommendations to Transactions Explore how AI systems are evolving from advisory roles to autonomous decision-makers capable of completing complex financial transactions. Learn how teams are designing products that seamlessly bridge conversational interactions with real-world execution. 02Trust, Security, & Payment Infrastructure Discover how leading institutions build secure, scalable payment rails designed specifically for autonomous agents. We'll examine how leaders manage risk, balance authorization with autonomy, & ensure ironclad trust across machine-driven financial interactions. 03The Machine-to-Machine Product Playbook Examine the strategies & frameworks product leaders use to build, launch, & scale machine-to-machine financial products. Learn how to adapt traditional product management playbooks to meet the demands of an increasingly agentic commerce ecosystem. What's IncludedGourmet Light Refreshments - Enjoy a curated selection of artisanal bites & small plates, perfect for connecting with colleagues.Settle in for easy conversation & good company in a warm, welcoming space. With a thoughtful selection of beer & wine on hand, it's the perfect backdrop for winding down or catching up.Have dietary restrictions? To ensure we can accommodate your dietary needs, please inform us at least 48 hours before the workshop start date.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. Her experience is specialized in the digital health space, & she enjoys building community & connecting people in the space. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: WorkOS & You.com Agenda 5:30 pm - 5:35 pmWelcome & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  5:35 pm - 5:50 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  5:50 pm - 6:05 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from WorkOS TBA Outline:TBA  6:05 pm - 6:20 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from You.com TBA Outline:TBA  6:20 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:30 pm - 6:40 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:40 pm - 6:50 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:50 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. events.name: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business To 7-Figures Without Raising Venture Capital
events.description: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business to 7-Figures Without Raising Venture CapitalI built Fibe to millions of dollars in profit without raising a dollar of venture capital, without a co-founder, & without a board. I still own the whole thing. Since then I've started The Shortlist, which has just begun to hit profitability, & cofounded Outliers Summit, which runs independently as a profitable events & media company that will cross seven figures soon. We run over a hundred events a year with a tiny team. On September 3 I'm walking through exactly how, in one session. What you'll leave with: How to pick the game you're playing before you start, so the advice you take actually applies to the business you're building Why one marketing channel is enough to reach a million dollars in revenue, & how to find yours How to build distribution before you have a product. I spent years building an audience before I had a business idea, & it is the single biggest reason bootstrapping worked How to find customers who will write a $50,000 check without blinking instead of ones who argue over $20 a month Then live Q&A for the rest of the session. Come with the specific question about your business, not the general one. That is where these earn their keep. Who this is for: anyone building something they would rather own outright than raise against. If you're going after a winner-take-all market & need capital to reach escape velocity, raising is the right call & this isn't for you.at. Mine wasn't.

Regroup at a bar nearby First Talk Description: Taming Dependency Graphs: Lessons from a 14-Year-Old iOS Codebaseby Victoria Ono As iOS apps grow over the years, managing dependencies becomes just as important as building new features. Understanding what depends on what, how new changes affect the codebase, & how to maintain architectural boundaries are challenges that every large engineering team eventually faces.In this talk, Victoria will share how Snapchat iOS codebase has evolved through the lens of their dependency injection frameworks. She'll cover what dependency graphs are, how they help reason about relationships across a large codebase, & how their approach to dependency injection has evolved to address the challenges that come with scale. Along the way, she'll talk about the architectural decisions behind that evolution & the lessons they have learned about managing complexity as applications grow. Victoria is an iOS engineer at Snap on the Maps team. Her recent work has focused on modernizing dependency injection within Maps & across the iOS codebase. Second Talk Description: The Soft Skills Nobody Taught Youby Mani Ramezan There's a lot of advice out there on how to prep for interviews & land your dream job. events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

We'll feature a presentation from Michael Guarino (Plural) & Eric Mustin (Elastic) followed by networking, refreshments, & pizza with the New York City tech community.  Date: Tuesday, August 25th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup? events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week's topic - Anthropic's IPO)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.
