events.name: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. About Farzad, the host Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C.   About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Acelab x Structured AI Hackathon
events.description: Join Acelab & Structured AI for an evening of building, food, & drinks. On any project the drawings, specs, & material library all disagree with each other in small ways. events.name: Building Slack's Simplified Layout Mode
events.description: This event will be online on YouTube & in-person (New York City). The speaker & live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page & someone will come down ASAP. DescriptionSlack is a powerful hub for work & communication, but its dense & complex interface can be a barrier for users with motor, vision, & cognitive disabilities. To help more people use Slack effectively, we introduced Simplified Layout Mode on desktop & web. This preference transforms Slack into a single-column layout that is easier to navigate & has fewer distractions. In this session, we will demo Simplified Layout Mode & discuss its evolution from an accommodation request by an ALS advocacy group to a feature that benefits multiple audiences. Along the way, we'll share specific examples of how its design was shaped by our partnerships with disabled & neurodivergent users. Attendees will learn ... How to collect & synthesize feedback from different groups of users with disabilities over the course of a feature's developmentHow to collaborate with internal employee disability groups to get feedback & build momentum around a featurePresenter biosChris Xu is a director of product management of Slack looking after accessibility & design systems. Outside of product management, they have had a wide-ranging career focused on how technology & communities shape each other. They live in Brooklyn, NY & hold strong opinions about fruit. Lena Wang is a frontend software engineer at Slack working on accessibility & design systems. Outside of engineering, she's usually mid-side-quest - whether that's walking the entire length of Manhattan on a whim, running a Taco Bell 5k, or competing in a city-wide scavenger hunt. She lives in Manhattan, NY. Kaili Liang is a Software Engineer at Slack, working on accessibility & design systems. In her free time, she loves chasing new eats, diving into books, trying various arts & crafts, & traveling. AccessibilityThe presentation will have human captions [CC], not automatic captions. For ASL preferred speakers, learn about the Aira ASL App, & download it before the event. For the Blind & Low Vision community, learn about the Aira Explorer App & download it before the event. To access the online webinar for audio description, use the A11yNYC Access Offer to call, or simply inform your Visual Interpreter that you'd like that offer applied when you connect. For additional accessibility requirements, please email meryl@equalentry.com two weeks before the event. LivestreamYouTube Provided by Internet Society Accessibility SIG. Location detailsThe event is at 72 Spring street on the 4th floor. Everyone must be accompanied to the event on the 4th floor. Because everyone needs to be escorted, please arrive early or on time. When you enter the ground floor, a representative from A11yNYC will be there to provide elevator access. TransitThe building 72 Spring street is near several transit stops: 6 train Spring Street (non-accessible stop): 100 feetCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.4 milesB/D/F/M trains Broadway-Lafayette Street (accessible stop), 0.2 milesN/Q/R/W trains Prince Street (non-accessible stop): 0.2 milesCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.3 milesM1 / M55 Bus lines Broadway/Spring Street stop: 500 feetCabs & rideshares can let passengers out right near the building entrance. Finding the buildingIn Google Maps, find 72 Spring street. It shows the correct location of the entrance: on Spring Street, halfway between Crosby & Lafayette.It's also between the Glossier store & the Krewe Eyewear store.Inside & over the reception desk in our building 72 Spring st, it says Marc Jacobs. Traveling to the event?We recommend Hotel on Rivington or Crosby Street Hotel. AccreditationAll A11yNYC meetups are pre-approved for IAAP Continuing Accessibility Education Credits (CAEC). SponsorsThanks to Aira, AKQA, Deque, Evinced, Equal Entry, & Fable for sponsoring. Want to be a sponsor? Contact meryl@equalentry.com

events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Bets Over Baghdad
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket. Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business To 7-Figures Without Raising Venture Capital
events.description: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business to 7-Figures Without Raising Venture CapitalI built Fibe to millions of dollars in profit without raising a dollar of venture capital, without a co-founder, & without a board. I still own the whole thing. Since then I've started The Shortlist, which has just begun to hit profitability, & cofounded Outliers Summit, which runs independently as a profitable events & media company that will cross seven figures soon. We run over a hundred events a year with a tiny team. On September 3 I'm walking through exactly how, in one session. What you'll leave with: How to pick the game you're playing before you start, so the advice you take actually applies to the business you're building Why one marketing channel is enough to reach a million dollars in revenue, & how to find yours How to build distribution before you have a product. I spent years building an audience before I had a business idea, & it is the single biggest reason bootstrapping worked How to find customers who will write a $50,000 check without blinking instead of ones who argue over $20 a month Then live Q&A for the rest of the session. Come with the specific question about your business, not the general one. That is where these earn their keep. Who this is for: anyone building something they would rather own outright than raise against. If you're going after a winner-take-all market & need capital to reach escape velocity, raising is the right call & this isn't for you.at. Mine wasn't.

events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 TBA 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner HealthTechQuity is a community spotlighting tech-for-good in Healthcare & Life Sciences: uniting mission-driven professionals to do well by doing good' & reduce the health equity gap. About the organisers Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Perrin Joel is the Founder of HealthTechQuity & Client Solutions Director at BioTalent, a global Life Science staffing firm. Her experience is specialized in the digital health space, & she enjoys building community & connecting people in the space. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: The Builders Table
events.description: The Builder's Table is a weekly meetup for building out ideas with AI agents. Every month follows a rhythm. Every meeting has a focus. Must bring a laptop! Week 1 - Ideation & collaboration We'll have 1.5 hours to talk to one another, exchange ideas, ask questions, & refine what you'll be working on for the rest of the month. In the final 30 minutes, we'll start up our agents & have them create a step-by-step plan for building out your idea. Weeks 2 & 3 - Vibecoding Both meetups will be 2 full hours of straight vibecoding your project alongside everyone else. The idea is to take the plan you made at the end of week one & start building it out. Week 4 - Demo day The goal by the end of the month is to have a working project you can demo. Don't worry - it doesn't have to be polished or anywhere near perfect. As long as you have the bare bones of your idea & can show how it works, that's all that matters. We're focused on shipping, not perfection.   -Arrive at 4:45 -This meetup is intended for anyone looking to make more time for vibecoding. No need to commit to all the meetings in order to get something out of it. The intent is to form a community that is constantly building together. So you get out what you want to put in. Meetings will happen every week of every month, so we invite you to join us for food, drinks, good vibes, & vibecoding.

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

Don't forget your ID! 6:30 PM - Welcome 6:35 PM - First Talk: Taming Dependency Graphs: Lessons from a 14-Year-Old iOS Codebase 7:05 PM - Community Announcements 7:15 PM - Second Talk: The Soft Skills Nobody Taught You 7:45 PM - Networking 8:30 PM - Doors close. Regroup at a bar nearby First Talk Description: Taming Dependency Graphs: Lessons from a 14-Year-Old iOS Codebaseby Victoria Ono As iOS apps grow over the years, managing dependencies becomes just as important as building new features. Understanding what depends on what, how new changes affect the codebase, & how to maintain architectural boundaries are challenges that every large engineering team eventually faces.In this talk, Victoria will share how Snapchat iOS codebase has evolved through the lens of their dependency injection frameworks. She'll cover what dependency graphs are, how they help reason about relationships across a large codebase, & how their approach to dependency injection has evolved to address the challenges that come with scale. Along the way, she'll talk about the architectural decisions behind that evolution & the lessons they have learned about managing complexity as applications grow. Victoria is an iOS engineer at Snap on the Maps team. Her recent work has focused on modernizing dependency injection within Maps & across the iOS codebase. Second Talk Description: The Soft Skills Nobody Taught Youby Mani Ramezan There's a lot of advice out there on how to prep for interviews & land your dream job. But there's far less on how to actually succeed once you're in it-how to navigate promotions & annual reviews. Mani remembers the days that Interface Builder was a separate app than Xcode. events.description: 2026 is the year of enterprise AI deployment. The window for experimentation has closed; the time for ROI is fast approaching. events.name: Stronger Together - Find Your Co-Founder
events.description: Stronger Together: Find Your Co-FounderBuilding an AI startup is hard. Building it with the right co-founder changes everything. Whether you're a technical builder looking for a commercial partner, a product leader searching for an AI engineer, or an operator with a big vision looking for someone equally obsessed with bringing it to life, this event is designed to help you meet the right people through structured, high-quality conversations. Goodbye to headless networking! Unlike traditional meetups where everyone drifts from conversation to conversation, this evening is designed around intentional matching, giving you multiple opportunities to connect with people who complement your skills, ambitions, & interests. What to expect  Opening KeynoteA short talk on what makes exceptional founding teams, common mistakes when choosing co-founders, & how to evaluate long-term fit beyond technical skills.  60-Second Founder IntroductionsEvery attendee will have the opportunity to introduce themselves in one minute (subject to capacity). Tell the room: Who you are What you're building (or want to build) What you're looking for What you can bring to a founding team Each attendee will also receive a name tag highlighting their background, interests, & expertise to make conversations easier.  Facilitated Co-Founder MatchingInstead of random networking, attendees will rotate between themed discussion tables based on startup stage, industry, technologies, or interests. These small-group conversations are designed to help you quickly discover complementary skills, shared vision, & potential collaboration opportunities.  Community MixerContinue conversations & meet other founders, investors, operators, & builders in the community. Who should attend AI founders looking for a co-founder Engineers interested in starting a company Product managers & designers passionate about AI GTM, sales, & growth leaders looking to join an early-stage startup Researchers & technical builders exploring startup ideas Experienced operators interested in becoming founding team members Who this event is forWe're curating for ambitious, execution-oriented people who are serious about building companies. You don't need to have a startup today, but you should have the skills, experience, or commitment to become part of a founding team. Whether you already have an idea or are looking for the right person to build one with, you'll leave having met people who could become your future co-founder. Space is limited, & applications may be reviewed to maintain a high-quality mix of attendees. The Yard:The Yard is a coworking space at the intersection of creativity, design, & play with locations in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Philly, Washington DC, & Chicago, with a variety of shared & private workspace options to meet your team's needs. Built to inspire & cultivate success, The Yard is here to help you win! Learn more at theyard.com. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

We'll feature a presentation from Michael Guarino (Plural) & Eric Mustin (Elastic) followed by networking, refreshments, & pizza with the New York City tech community.  Date: Tuesday, August 25th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup? Along the way, we'll discuss resiliency, duplication, architectural tradeoffs, & how to avoid getting lost at sea in an increasingly complex observability ecosystem.

events.name: AI & What Makes Us Human
events.description: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.

Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Bets Over Baghdad
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket. Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week's topic - Anthropic's IPO)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. events.name: GTM Leaders, Vol. 1 - Breaking Through The AI Slop
events.description: NYC GTM Leaders, Vol. 1: Breaking Through the AI Slop Every channel is flooded with machine-generated outreach, & your buyers have stopped paying attention to any of it. So what still breaks through? Join us Thursday, August 27th in Midtown (address shared upon approval) for an off-the-record evening with GTM leaders who are figuring it out in real time. Capped at 50 so the conversations stay focused & real. The agenda: 6:30 pm: Doors open. Drinks, light bites, & an icebreaker to get the room talking. 7:00 pm: GTM Insight Talks. Three quick-hit talks from operators actually running these plays: using AI for lead gen without sounding like AI, thought leadership as a channel buyers still trust, & a head-to-head teardown of real GTM stacks. Q&A after. 7:30 pm: Working session. Small groups, hands-on. Apply the plays to your own pipeline. 8:00 pm: Round two networking. Now that everyone has shared context, conversations go deeper. 8:30 pm: Close & a first look at Vol. 2. Who should request an invite: GTM leaders at Series A+ startups Founders (Series A+, 2+ years in) Heads of Growth at scaling companies Seats are limited & approved individually. Request your invite now. Your hosts: Tanny Kang is Co-founder & COO at Vibranium Labs, an a16z-backed startup building AI-native incident management. A former Big Law tech attorney who traded redlines for pipeline, he now runs GTM end to end & has closed enterprise customers like Shutterstock, where Vibe OnCall cut manual incident work by 70% across 300+ engineers. He also writes Incidents.World, a newsletter on all things on-call. Josh Kim is Chief of Staff, GTM & Growth at Remy by MindStudio, an AI agent that builds enterprise-grade apps from a plain-language spec doc. A former Fortune 500 data & analytics consultant at Kantar, he's since helped drive 1.5x revenue growth & grown a community of 10,000+ builders, execs, & investors. Eric Fleshman is a GTM Engineer who has built go-to-market functions from the ground up, including founding GTME roles. His focus is what still breaks through when every inbox is machine-generated noise: technical depth, human-first outreach, & intent-driven systems. Signal first, intent after. He's an AlphaForge Architect Award winner from his Clay cohort & loves coffee, climbing & traveling! About Vibranium Labs: At vibraniumlabs.ai, we build Vibe OnCall, the #1 AI incident commander that proactively hunts down issues in your eng org before engineers ever get paged. We help engineering teams stay ahead of incidents, cut down on 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence. Our mission is straightforward: Prevent Incidents, Not Just Respond: Equip engineering orgs with an AI incident commander that proactively surfaces issues before they page anyone. Reduce On-Call Burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build Lasting Reliability: Offer ongoing tuning & partnership so Vibe OnCall keeps learning your systems & gets sharper the longer it runs.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: October Nexus Networking Meet Up
events.description: A casual, pay-your-own-way networking event designed for professionals to connect, share ideas, and build lasting relationships across the broader business and technology ecosystem. Meet fellow professionals, expand your network, and enjoy a relaxed evening together. Food and beverages are available for individual purchase. Who Attends: Founders & startups PR & Agency teams Venture Capitalists Consultants Finance professionals Content & social media marketers Marketing technology professionals Attendance is limited to help keep conversations meaningful, so please apply for a spot. We look forward to meeting you! About Our Meet Ups: Our Meet Ups are relaxed, industry-agnostic gatherings built for professionals who want to unplug from the standard corporate routine and connect on a human level. Whether you are looking to exchange fresh perspectives, brainstorm new concepts, or simply meet peers navigating similar spaces, this environment is designed for open-ended conversation and organic relationship-building. What It Is: An open, welcoming community space to meet new connections. An opportunity to exchange industry perspectives and uncover unexpected collaborations. A low-pressure, welcoming atmosphere with no formal agenda or mandatory pitches. What It Isn't: RTM Nexus Meet Up is not a curated buyer/seller event and is not structured around guaranteed access to a specific target audience, vertical, company type, or decision-maker profile (ICP). Looking for something more targeted? If you need to connect with a specific niche-such as retail, fashion, beauty, CPG, or enterprise brand leaders-check out our "Retail Leaders Receptions" and "Nexus Mixers" instead. Those events are intentionally curated and sponsored around targeted audiences to provide a more focused networking experience.

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: Investors For A Better America
events.description: A nonpartisan conference for family offices & other investors strengthening our capitalist constitutional democracy.   Our speakers are senior investors from Millennium, Apogem, Rothschild Asset Management, Harvard Management Company, Goldman Sachs, B Capital, First Round, Renaissance Technologies, District of Columbia Retirement, International Finance Corporation, Cantor Fitzgerald, & TIAA-CREF. We believe a free & fair democracy is foundational to a strong investment climate. Free enterprise depends on civic conditions that markets cannot create on their own, including: - Representative & accountable democracy without over-centralization & with anti-corruption safeguards- Social trust- A responsive, fiscally responsible, & effective government with         an independent Federal Reserve - The ability to recruit the best people globally, and- Strong alliances, especially with other capitalist democracies. Who: investors, philanthropists, nonprofits, senior executives, founders Cost: Admission is complimentary for investing principals of family offices, foundations, endowments, & other institutional investors with at least $100m AUM, who do not manage outside capital.   All others: $2,026. Use 10% discount code: IBA_Cal_2026.  All revenues go to Mediators Foundation, a 501(c)3 nonprofit focused on bridging divides.

events.name: Idea To MVP Workshop - Build Night w/ Lovable
events.description: Idea to MVP Workshop: Build Night with Lovable Bring an idea & a phone/laptop, leave with something you built. This is a hands-on workshop for non-technical builders who want to ship real products using Lovable. No engineering background required. Spend the evening learning the future of vibe coding: prompts, harnesses, & the workflows that turn an idea into a working app in a single night. Whether you're in big tech, at a startup, or just looking to level up your technical skills, this is a night to make new ideas come to life.  Who's this for?Non-technical builders, operators, & the founder-curious. If you've ever wanted to build but thought you couldn't code, this room is for you. First-timers & seasoned builders both welcome.  What we'll do Arrival, light bites, & drinks Demo & onboarding with Lovable Build on your own or in teams of up to 4 Lightning pitches of what you made Celebrate, connect, & keep the conversations going  Everyone gets 100 free Lovable credits to build with.  August 26th, 6:00 to 9:00 PM Williamsburg, Brooklyn (exact location shared with confirmed registrants)More sponsors to be announced soon. About the hosts & sponsors  Lovable is the AI platform that lets anyone build full web apps through natural-language prompts, no coding required. He is active in NYC's & Silicon Valley's tech communities, having hosted 180+ community mixers & brand activations since 2020.

events.name: UN Blockchain Week 2026 | Main Conference
events.description: September 16-17  New York City  During UNGA 81  The Most Important Blockchain Event of the Year - Where Global Leaders, Policymakers & Visionaries Shape the Future About the EventIn an increasingly unpredictable world, one gathering rises above the noise as the single most strategic opportunity of 2026: UN Blockchain Week. The centerpiece of the 10-day UN Blockchain Week (Sept 10-19) is this exclusive two-day conference - perfectly timed with the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA 81) & New York Fashion Week. This is not another blockchain conference. This is where senior policymakers, institutional investors, government officials, energy executives, & the world's top builders converge for high-signal dialogue on real-world adoption, nation-state strategy, & the future of finance, AI, energy, & the space economy. The world's leaders will be in New York. The most important conversations in blockchain will happen here. Why This Is the Most Important Event of the Year Unmatched Access - Direct proximity to the global governance class during the one week they are all physically in New York.  High-Signal Programming - Focused, curated content at the true intersection of policy & innovation.  Elite Audience - Institutional investors, heads of state advisors, energy leaders, & technologists already in Manhattan for UNGA.  Real Impact - These are the conversations that influence actual policy outcomes & strategic national positioning. This is the week serious players show up. What to Expect - The Two-Day Conference Day 1 - September 16 Bitcoin, Policy & Institutional Infrastructure Opening Keynote: Blockchain's Role in Global Governance Nation-State Bitcoin Adoption Regulatory Outlook Post-UNGA Season Tokenization of Real-World Assets Day 2 - September 17 AI, Energy, Space & Real-World Impact Keynote: The Convergence of AI & Blockchain AI Agents & Decentralized Systems Blockchain for the Energy Transition The Space Economy & Blockchain Each day delivers 18 hours of world-class content, panels, keynotes, & high-level networking - from morning strategy sessions through late-night discussions. Plus the full 10-day UN Blockchain Week experience (Sept 10-19) featuring 100+ events, panels, workshops, NYFW  Blockchain Runway moments, & side programming across Bitcoin, AI, Energy, Space, & Fashion-Tech. Official After Party - BitcoinPalooza Evening of September 17 (immediately following Day 2 close) The official celebration of UN Blockchain Week. BitcoinPalooza brings together the community for an unforgettable night of music, networking, & Bitcoin culture in the heart of New York City. events.description: Join RTM Nexus and ESW for an intimate evening at Raines Law Room, bringing together a select group of senior retail and brand leaders for an open conversation around the future of international commerce. Expanding globally has never been simple - and AI is adding an entirely new dimension. From entering and scaling in new markets to localization, customer experience, payments, fulfillment and the rise of AI-powered shopping, the way brands approach international growth is quickly changing. Over dinner, we'll explore how leaders are navigating that shift, where AI is creating real opportunities, and what retailers and brands should be thinking about now as commerce becomes increasingly global, intelligent and interconnected. No presentations or sales pitches - just great food, thoughtful conversation and candid discussion with peers tackling many of the same challenges. September 15 | 6:00 PMRaines Law Room | New York City Attendance is limited and reserved for senior leaders from retailers and brands. Apply on Luma: https://luma.com/rtmnexus-kd2i

events.name: Dell x NVIDIA Hackathon
events.description: Dell x NVIDIA's Local AI on Dell Pro Max with GB10 is a oneday build sprint where you ship an alwayson business agent running locally on the Dell Pro Max with GB10. A one-day hackathon. Real hardware on the line.40 teams. 40 Dell Pro Max with GB10 units. One day to build an AI agent that runs locally on the box (no cloud API) & helps businesses or corporates. You get the hardware. You get the stack. You get a day to ship something real. Prizes- 1st place takes home a Dell Pro Max with GB10p per team.- 2nd & 3rd win a Dell laptop per team. ----  Your AI model on a drive. Venue Wi-Fi won't be fast enough for everyone to download models on the day, so load anything you want to use onto a USB or external drive ahead of time.  A laptop for development. You'll get a Dell Pro Max with GB10 for the day, but bring your own laptop to code on. Your demo has to run locally on the box.  A power strip or extension. We won't have one outlet per person, so if your battery's weak, a splitter or extension cord is a smart backup. Sign up here or sign up at the main event page & hackathon platform - BuilderBasehttps://builderbase.com/event/dell-x-nvidia-ai-hackathon-nyc   How it works01 Apply Fill out the application form on this page. We review on a rolling basis & confirm your spot by email. 02 Team formation Teams of 2-4 builders. If you register alone, use the BuilderBase dashboard to find teammates or we'll pair you before the event. 03 Build Show up on August 22th. You get a Dell Pro Max with GB10 for the day. Build an AI agent that runs locally on the box. Business or corporate use cases, required stack: OpenClaw + NVIDIA NemoClaw + OpenShell. 04 Submit Submit your working demo through the BuilderBase portal before the deadline. Demo must run on the Dell Pro Max with GB10. 05 Live pitch Top 8 teams are selected from all submissions & deliver a short live pitch to the judges the same evening. 06 Win 07 Mingle/Networking 1st place takes home a Dell Pro Max with GB10p per team.2nd & 3rd win a Dell laptop per team. Sign up here!

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works:15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Situational Awareness. Are we in an AI bubble? Circular financing between AI labs & infrastructure players, record market concentration, & capex spending that's outpacing monetization. We're decoding the real risk signals versus the noise, & what it means for how you invest from here. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time. Disclaimer By registering for this event, you'll be added to the Innovest newsletter (innovest.substack.com). You can unsubscribe at any time.

events.name: Agentics - Use Agents Effectively
events.description: Join Nori Agentic & Modal (featuring Warp, Opus, Goose, Librechat, & Subconscious) in New York on August 19 for our second flagship Agentics speaker series - a full evening of presentations from teams at the cutting edge of agentic development. Whether you're just getting started with AI coding agents (beginner friendly!) or you've been shipping with them for months, you'll walk away with practical techniques you can use the next day. Dinner will be provided! A recap of our last event: agenticsnyc.com/events/may-2026-speaker-series.html Huge thanks to our sponsors, MongoDB & Clickhouse! MongoDB is the leading modern database platform empowering developers to build flexible, scalable, data-driven applications. Check-out the MongoDB for Startups for Atlas credits & Voyage AI tokens, technical expertise, & dedicated support on the world's best modern, AI-ready data platform. ClickHouse is one of the fastest & most resource-efficient real-time databases & data warehouses, optimized for diverse data-intensive & large-scale workloads. Applications range from interactive & user-facing to ad-hoc historical analyses. Planned Schedule: 6 PM: Doors Open 6:30 PM - 9 PM: Presentations 9 PM - 10 PM: Networking Each presentation will be ~10 minutes with a ~5 minute Q&A, 7 presentations total. We don't expect to use the full 2.5 hours for presentations, but we're estimating conservatively. Speakers: Aloke Desai is the head of product engineering & first engineering hire at Warp. He's been building agents for 5 years at Warp, helping scale it to millions of active users. Prior to Warp, he was a senior engineer & tech lead at Google Docs. Aloke's talk will focus on how a software factory can self-improve over time. Amol Kapoor is the CEO of Nori, the lead organizer of Agentics, & the author of 12 Grams of Carbon. He's been in the AI world for 12 years, including a 4-year stint at Google Research. Nori uses background agents to do just about everything - an army of agents respond to errors, manage the CRM, keep data clean, & more. In his talk, Amol will walk through what a "software factory" is, how to build one, & what pitfalls to avoid. Danny Avila is the founder & core maintainer of LibreChat. He was early to recognize the need for cross-provider dev tools, & started LibreChat 3 years ago to create a chat UI experience separated from the big labs. Danny will be speaking about how LibreChat solved multiplayer agent/human sandboxes. Jack Amadeo is a software engineer on the Goose team at Block & one of the most prolific contributors to Goose, Block's open-source AI agent. He joined Block via the acquisition of Neptyne, the YC-backed Python spreadsheet startup he co-founded, & was previously an engineer at Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs. His Goose work spans the multi-provider LLM architecture, MCP integration, & the Goose SDK. Jack will speak about unbundling the Goose harness into an SDK & the uses that emerge from treating agents as SDKs. Jack O'Brien is a two-time founder & ex-Googler, & the current CEO of subconscious.dev. LLMs are incredible tools with one massive limitation: the context window. They are fundamentally limited in what they can remember. Jack has spent the last two years thinking about how to make this problem better. He'll be speaking about context compression & long-horizon tasks in modern LLMs. Jeffrey Silver is the CTO & cofounder of Opus. Over the last 6 years, Jeff has spent a lot of time thinking about how to build tools that benefit everyone at Opus, including non-technical team members. That focus led him to build one of the first cloud agent stacks. Jeff will be speaking about how Opus uses their cloud agent army to manage their on-call burden. Qijia (Joy) Liu is an early Member of Technical Staff at Modal & a Penn M&T grad. She came up through Penn Labs before joining Modal, where she's focused on making serverless GPU infrastructure accessible to ML engineers. Joy will show you how to vibe train a model on Modal Training Gym, an RL library that lets users post-train on Modal in under 100 lines of code. Agentics is a community of 1000+ people building with coding agents. We meet in New York City to share what actually works, what doesn't, & what's next. We're reinventing best practices every day (without having to be glued to Twitter). Learn more here: https://agenticsnyc.com/ Sign up for the newsletter: https://noriagentic.com/newsletter.html#agentics And join our community slack: https://join.slack.com/t/nori-7sp2119/shared_invite/zt-3nvw8xlw2-hxppg~NXeawHVvopmbMCFw

The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Bets Over Baghdad
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket. Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: AI & What Makes Us Human
events.description: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.
