events.name: Health2Tech NYC
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events. Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in.6:00 - 6:45 TBA6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology. About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape.Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders.Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for. Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey.Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation.Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces. Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers).Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors.Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.

events.name: AI Tinkerers Demo Day
events.description: Join us for the next AI Tinkerers meetup in NYC! Showcase your latest AI demos, connect with fellow practitioners, & dive deep into the world of LLMs & generative AI with the best technical community in NYC. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQSome slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? This is your moment to share with like-minded AI tinkerers! A demo is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress, followed by Q\&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!)  FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE  Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy! Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI Tinkerers Please note that capacity is limited, so we'll prioritize those who are able to present a demo. Demo vibes  Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:00 Networking & pizzas9:00 Doors Close

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: AI Comes To The Museum
events.description: Join Aboard for a conversation with Hlne Alonso of WonderWay, Spencer Kiser of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, & Danny Reynolds of the Museum of Modern Art as they discuss how museums & other cultural institutions are beginning to use artificial intelligence in both public-facing experiences & behind-the-scenes operations. From visitor engagement & collections to governance, infrastructure, & organizational change, they'll explore where AI is already proving useful, how organizations can design around its limitations, & what thoughtful adoption looks like in institutions built around knowledge, creativity, & public trust. Aboard president Paul Ford will moderate the discussion, followed by an audience Q&A. Afterward, stay for food, drinks, & conversation with the speakers & fellow attendees. About the speakers: Hlne Alonso is the founder of WonderWay, a conversational AI platform that transforms curated cultural knowledge into personalized conversations with visitors. WonderWay is currently being piloted at the MIT Museum as part of a research study with MIT Sloan. Hlne also teaches at NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program, where she explores AI, spatial experiences, & new forms of human-computer interaction. Her career has spanned both cultural institutions-including the American Museum of Natural History, the Wildlife Conservation Society, & Liberty Science Center-and the tech industry, where she served as Chief Design Officer at two Series B startups. Spencer Kiser is Senior Manager of Application Development at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, where he leads the team behind the Met's web platform & APIs, including the new semantic search experience. With over 20 years in cultural institutions, including MoMA & the American Museum of Natural History, his work has spanned in-gallery experiences, mobile development, API architecture, & the Met's Open Access initiative. His path winds through sound: field recording & sound design alongside a coding practice, shaped by NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program & its culture of experimentation & collaboration. Outside work, he enjoys archiving physical media & hacking on hardware & local AI tooling. He lives in New York with his family. Danny Reynolds is an AI enablement leader at The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), where he helps deploy practical AI systems & enterprise technology that support one of the world's leading cultural institutions. Drawing on a background that spans a library & information science degree focusing on archives & records management to more than a decade at Apple, he focuses on the real-world challenges of AI adoption, governance, & organizational change.

events.name: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business To 7-Figures Without Raising Venture Capital
events.description: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business to 7-Figures Without Raising Venture CapitalI built Fibe to millions of dollars in profit without raising a dollar of venture capital, without a co-founder, & without a board. I still own the whole thing. Since then I've started The Shortlist, which has just begun to hit profitability, & cofounded Outliers Summit, which runs independently as a profitable events & media company that will cross seven figures soon. We run over a hundred events a year with a tiny team. On September 3 I'm walking through exactly how, in one session. What you'll leave with: How to pick the game you're playing before you start, so the advice you take actually applies to the business you're building Why one marketing channel is enough to reach a million dollars in revenue, & how to find yours How to build distribution before you have a product. I spent years building an audience before I had a business idea, & it is the single biggest reason bootstrapping worked How to find customers who will write a $50,000 check without blinking instead of ones who argue over $20 a month Then live Q&A for the rest of the session. Come with the specific question about your business, not the general one. That is where these earn their keep. Who this is for: anyone building something they would rather own outright than raise against. If you're going after a winner-take-all market & need capital to reach escape velocity, raising is the right call & this isn't for you.at. Mine wasn't.

So what still breaks through? Join us Thursday, August 27th in Midtown (address shared upon approval) for an off-the-record evening with GTM leaders who are figuring it out in real time. Capped at 50 so the conversations stay focused & real. The agenda: 6:30 pm: Doors open. Drinks, light bites, & an icebreaker to get the room talking. 7:00 pm: GTM Insight Talks. Three quick-hit talks from operators actually running these plays: using AI for lead gen without sounding like AI, thought leadership as a channel buyers still trust, & a head-to-head teardown of real GTM stacks. Q&A after. 7:30 pm: Working session. Small groups, hands-on. Apply the plays to your own pipeline. 8:00 pm: Round two networking. events.name: Stronger Together - Find Your Co-Founder
events.description: Stronger Together: Find Your Co-FounderBuilding an AI startup is hard. Building it with the right co-founder changes everything. Whether you're a technical builder looking for a commercial partner, a product leader searching for an AI engineer, or an operator with a big vision looking for someone equally obsessed with bringing it to life, this event is designed to help you meet the right people through structured, high-quality conversations. Goodbye to headless networking! Unlike traditional meetups where everyone drifts from conversation to conversation, this evening is designed around intentional matching, giving you multiple opportunities to connect with people who complement your skills, ambitions, & interests. What to expect  Opening KeynoteA short talk on what makes exceptional founding teams, common mistakes when choosing co-founders, & how to evaluate long-term fit beyond technical skills.  60-Second Founder IntroductionsEvery attendee will have the opportunity to introduce themselves in one minute (subject to capacity). Tell the room: Who you are What you're building (or want to build) What you're looking for What you can bring to a founding team Each attendee will also receive a name tag highlighting their background, interests, & expertise to make conversations easier.  Facilitated Co-Founder MatchingInstead of random networking, attendees will rotate between themed discussion tables based on startup stage, industry, technologies, or interests. These small-group conversations are designed to help you quickly discover complementary skills, shared vision, & potential collaboration opportunities.  Community MixerContinue conversations & meet other founders, investors, operators, & builders in the community. Who should attend AI founders looking for a co-founder Engineers interested in starting a company Product managers & designers passionate about AI GTM, sales, & growth leaders looking to join an early-stage startup Researchers & technical builders exploring startup ideas Experienced operators interested in becoming founding team members Who this event is forWe're curating for ambitious, execution-oriented people who are serious about building companies. You don't need to have a startup today, but you should have the skills, experience, or commitment to become part of a founding team. Whether you already have an idea or are looking for the right person to build one with, you'll leave having met people who could become your future co-founder. Space is limited, & applications may be reviewed to maintain a high-quality mix of attendees. The Yard:The Yard is a coworking space at the intersection of creativity, design, & play with locations in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Philly, Washington DC, & Chicago, with a variety of shared & private workspace options to meet your team's needs. Built to inspire & cultivate success, The Yard is here to help you win! Learn more at theyard.com. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Mindsets Of $1B Founders
events.description: Join Andrew Yeung & Ankur Nagpal, for a live conversation on how outlier founders actually think, & where that thinking breaks from the advice everyone repeats. Ankur built Teachable from an idea to $60M ARR & sold it for $250M. He also founded & sold Carry & is now the General Partner at USVC he backs the next generation of founders. He has seen the pattern from all three seats: building it, selling it, & writing the checks. Andrew is the founder of Fibe, the media & events platform behind Outliers Summit, Junto & Tech Breakfast Club. You can learn more about my A Chief of Staff New York events here. About Colliers:Sheena & Jen from Colliers work alongside tech companies to help make strategic decisions about office, lab/R&D, and/or warehouse/distribution space-whether that's in New York, San Francisco, or across the globe. events.name: Innovation In Public Mixer 2.0
events.description: Innovation in Public 2.0. Edition two of our monthly mixer series. Come & you are guaranteed one relevant intro. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access. Limited release, & it goes fast.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. The August cohort is underway right now, building in public. Come see them present at Demo Day, our public showcase in front of 35+ investors. Applications for the next cohort open after Demo Day  Get on the list 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders On camera: Nik Michael, host of the Pivot Point podcast, is shooting photography, video, & follow up interviews with select attendees. Nik is a licensed clinician with more than thirty years in counseling & decades in business, education, & investing, & his show explores the moments where transformation begins. Watch the show on YouTube  Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts  More at counselingtherapy.com/pivotpoint. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. The current cohort presents at Demo Day, open to the network. You can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Register here The Private Network, the thread through all of it. Every vertical above runs on the same engine. You tell us what you need, we find the person, we make the introduction in writing. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. Join here Want to sponsor a room? One sponsor per event so it never feels crowded. Email stephen@propel.earth Media ConsentPhotography & Video Acknowledgement. You grant the Organizer a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, & distribute any such recordings or photographs for promotional, educational, or commercial purposes. You waive any right to inspect or approve the finished product & understand that no compensation will be provided for your appearance in these materials. events.name: Dell x NVIDIA Hackathon
events.description: Dell x NVIDIA's Local AI on Dell Pro Max with GB10 is a oneday build sprint where you ship an alwayson business agent running locally on the Dell Pro Max with GB10. A one-day hackathon. Real hardware on the line.40 teams. 40 Dell Pro Max with GB10 units. One day to build an AI agent that runs locally on the box (no cloud API) & helps businesses or corporates. You get the hardware. You get the stack. You get a day to ship something real. Prizes- 1st place takes home a Dell Pro Max with GB10p per team.- 2nd & 3rd win a Dell laptop per team. ----  Your AI model on a drive. Venue Wi-Fi won't be fast enough for everyone to download models on the day, so load anything you want to use onto a USB or external drive ahead of time.  A laptop for development. You'll get a Dell Pro Max with GB10 for the day, but bring your own laptop to code on. Your demo has to run locally on the box.  A power strip or extension. We won't have one outlet per person, so if your battery's weak, a splitter or extension cord is a smart backup. Sign up here or sign up at the main event page & hackathon platform - BuilderBasehttps://builderbase.com/event/dell-x-nvidia-ai-hackathon-nyc   How it works01 Apply Fill out the application form on this page. We review on a rolling basis & confirm your spot by email. 02 Team formation Teams of 2-4 builders. If you register alone, use the BuilderBase dashboard to find teammates or we'll pair you before the event. 03 Build Show up on August 22th. You get a Dell Pro Max with GB10 for the day. Build an AI agent that runs locally on the box. Business or corporate use cases, required stack: OpenClaw + NVIDIA NemoClaw + OpenShell. 04 Submit Submit your working demo through the BuilderBase portal before the deadline. Demo must run on the Dell Pro Max with GB10. 05 Live pitch Top 8 teams are selected from all submissions & deliver a short live pitch to the judges the same evening. 06 Win 07 Mingle/Networking 1st place takes home a Dell Pro Max with GB10p per team.2nd & 3rd win a Dell laptop per team. Sign up here!

events.name: Kubernetes Developers Meetup
events.description: Join the Elastic NYC User Group & Plural Kubernetes Developers on Tuesday, August 25th for an exciting meetup. We'll feature a presentation from Michael Guarino (Plural) & Eric Mustin (Elastic) followed by networking, refreshments, & pizza with the New York City tech community.  Date: Tuesday, August 25th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup? Email us at [meetups@elastic.co](mailto:meetups@elastic.co)Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food6:00 pm: Talk # 1 - Details coming soon - Michael Guarino (Plural)7:00 pm: Telemetry's Long Way Home: A Kubernetes Odyssey with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic - Eric Mustin (Elastic)7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up Talk Details:Telemetry's Long Way Home: A Kubernetes Odyssey with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic Eric Mustin (Elastic)Like Odysseus trying to find his way home, Kubernetes telemetry must navigate a difficult journey through dynamic workloads, short-lived infrastructure, overlapping tools, dropped signals, & unexpected operational monsters. This talk explores how Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic can work together to give Kubernetes metrics, logs, & traces a reliable path home. We'll look at practical collection architectures, Prometheus-native metrics, OpenTelemetry processing & routing, & how Elastic can bring the resulting signals together. Along the way, we'll discuss resiliency, duplication, architectural tradeoffs, & how to avoid getting lost at sea in an increasingly complex observability ecosystem.

events.name: Brains In Sync - Neuroscience Of Music, Drugs & Shared Experience
events.description: This is not a dry academic talk. Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. When a room full of strangers moves to the same beat, their brains start to move together too. This talk explores the neuroscience of interbrain synchrony, such as how music, rhythm, & altered states pull separate nervous systems into a shared rhythm, from ritual dance to the modern rave. We'll trace the math underneath the music (fractal structure, wave dynamics) up through the psychology of the dance floor, & into the clinic, where music is increasingly used as a deliberate tool in psychedelic-assisted therapy. Drawing on years inside the cannabis industry & hands-on psychedelic pharmacology research, this talk breaks down what's actually happening in the brain on psychoactive substances: shifts in perception, cognition, & the neurochemistry behind altered states, plus what's driving their growing clinical use in therapy.   Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. Agenda: Doors Open: 6:30 PM Lecture + Q&A: 6:45 PM - 8 PM Open-form networking: 8 PM & onwards Whether you're a parent, student, educator, or just someone fascinated by neuroscience, this is the perfect first night for PhDs & Pints. Smart people. Cold drinks. Big conversations.

We'll feature a presentation from Michael Guarino (Plural) & Eric Mustin (Elastic) followed by networking, refreshments, & pizza with the New York City tech community.  Date: Tuesday, August 25th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup? Along the way, we'll discuss resiliency, duplication, architectural tradeoffs, & how to avoid getting lost at sea in an increasingly complex observability ecosystem.

Applications range from interactive & user-facing to ad-hoc historical analyses. Planned Schedule: 6 PM: Doors Open 6:30 PM - 9 PM: Presentations 9 PM - 10 PM: Networking Each presentation will be ~10 minutes with a ~5 minute Q&A, 7 presentations total. We don't expect to use the full 2.5 hours for presentations, but we're estimating conservatively. Speakers: Aloke Desai is the head of product engineering & first engineering hire at Warp. He's been building agents for 5 years at Warp, helping scale it to millions of active users. Prior to Warp, he was a senior engineer & tech lead at Google Docs. Aloke's talk will focus on how a software factory can self-improve over time. Amol Kapoor is the CEO of Nori, the lead organizer of Agentics, & the author of 12 Grams of Carbon. He's been in the AI world for 12 years, including a 4-year stint at Google Research. Nori uses background agents to do just about everything - an army of agents respond to errors, manage the CRM, keep data clean, & more. In his talk, Amol will walk through what a "software factory" is, how to build one, & what pitfalls to avoid. Danny Avila is the founder & core maintainer of LibreChat. He was early to recognize the need for cross-provider dev tools, & started LibreChat 3 years ago to create a chat UI experience separated from the big labs. Danny will be speaking about how LibreChat solved multiplayer agent/human sandboxes. Jack Amadeo is a software engineer on the Goose team at Block & one of the most prolific contributors to Goose, Block's open-source AI agent. He joined Block via the acquisition of Neptyne, the YC-backed Python spreadsheet startup he co-founded, & was previously an engineer at Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs. His Goose work spans the multi-provider LLM architecture, MCP integration, & the Goose SDK. Jack will speak about unbundling the Goose harness into an SDK & the uses that emerge from treating agents as SDKs. Jack O'Brien is a two-time founder & ex-Googler, & the current CEO of subconscious.dev. LLMs are incredible tools with one massive limitation: the context window. They are fundamentally limited in what they can remember. Jack has spent the last two years thinking about how to make this problem better. He'll be speaking about context compression & long-horizon tasks in modern LLMs. Jeffrey Silver is the CTO & cofounder of Opus. Over the last 6 years, Jeff has spent a lot of time thinking about how to build tools that benefit everyone at Opus, including non-technical team members. That focus led him to build one of the first cloud agent stacks. Jeff will be speaking about how Opus uses their cloud agent army to manage their on-call burden. Qijia (Joy) Liu is an early Member of Technical Staff at Modal & a Penn M&T grad. She came up through Penn Labs before joining Modal, where she's focused on making serverless GPU infrastructure accessible to ML engineers. Joy will show you how to vibe train a model on Modal Training Gym, an RL library that lets users post-train on Modal in under 100 lines of code. Agentics is a community of 1000+ people building with coding agents. We meet in New York City to share what actually works, what doesn't, & what's next. We're reinventing best practices every day (without having to be glued to Twitter). Learn more here: https://agenticsnyc.com/ Sign up for the newsletter: https://noriagentic.com/newsletter.html#agentics And join our community slack: https://join.slack.com/t/nori-7sp2119/shared_invite/zt-3nvw8xlw2-hxppg~NXeawHVvopmbMCFw

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: GTM Leaders, Vol. 1 - Breaking Through The AI Slop
events.description: NYC GTM Leaders, Vol. 1: Breaking Through the AI Slop Every channel is flooded with machine-generated outreach, & your buyers have stopped paying attention to any of it. So what still breaks through? Join us Thursday, August 27th in Midtown (address shared upon approval) for an off-the-record evening with GTM leaders who are figuring it out in real time. Capped at 50 so the conversations stay focused & real. The agenda: 6:30 pm: Doors open. Drinks, light bites, & an icebreaker to get the room talking. 7:00 pm: GTM Insight Talks. Three quick-hit talks from operators actually running these plays: using AI for lead gen without sounding like AI, thought leadership as a channel buyers still trust, & a head-to-head teardown of real GTM stacks. Q&A after. 7:30 pm: Working session. Small groups, hands-on. Apply the plays to your own pipeline. 8:00 pm: Round two networking. Now that everyone has shared context, conversations go deeper. 8:30 pm: Close & a first look at Vol. 2. Who should request an invite: GTM leaders at Series A+ startups Founders (Series A+, 2+ years in) Heads of Growth at scaling companies Seats are limited & approved individually. Request your invite now. Your hosts: Tanny Kang is Co-founder & COO at Vibranium Labs, an a16z-backed startup building AI-native incident management. A former Big Law tech attorney who traded redlines for pipeline, he now runs GTM end to end & has closed enterprise customers like Shutterstock, where Vibe OnCall cut manual incident work by 70% across 300+ engineers. He also writes Incidents.World, a newsletter on all things on-call. Josh Kim is Chief of Staff, GTM & Growth at Remy by MindStudio, an AI agent that builds enterprise-grade apps from a plain-language spec doc. A former Fortune 500 data & analytics consultant at Kantar, he's since helped drive 1.5x revenue growth & grown a community of 10,000+ builders, execs, & investors. Eric Fleshman is a GTM Engineer who has built go-to-market functions from the ground up, including founding GTME roles. His focus is what still breaks through when every inbox is machine-generated noise: technical depth, human-first outreach, & intent-driven systems. Signal first, intent after. He's an AlphaForge Architect Award winner from his Clay cohort & loves coffee, climbing & traveling! About Vibranium Labs: At vibraniumlabs.ai, we build Vibe OnCall, the #1 AI incident commander that proactively hunts down issues in your eng org before engineers ever get paged. We help engineering teams stay ahead of incidents, cut down on 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence. Our mission is straightforward: Prevent Incidents, Not Just Respond: Equip engineering orgs with an AI incident commander that proactively surfaces issues before they page anyone. Reduce On-Call Burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build Lasting Reliability: Offer ongoing tuning & partnership so Vibe OnCall keeps learning your systems & gets sharper the longer it runs.

events.description: Back by popular demand  Build your first app with Replit! Hosted by the Prompt Engineers Society in collaboration with Replit & Veris AI, we're bringing together a curated group of ambitious students, recent graduates & founders in NYC. All attendees will receive access to exclusive credits & promotions to get started with building your first app with Replit & Veris. The Schedule: 6pm - doors open, networking with food/drinks 6:30pm - Replit & Veris platform walk-throughs 6:50pm - panel talk to spark app ideas 7:10pm - live build time with support from the Replit team 8pm - project demos & showcase About the Hosts:Prompt Engineers Society is a community of AI engineers & AI consultants advancing the field of AI deployment. Follow us to get notified of future events & join us on this journey!  Replit is the AI-powered platform where anyone can build, ship & run software - straight from a prompt, right in the browser. From first-time builders to seasoned engineers, millions of people use Replit to turn ideas into real, working apps in minutes. Veris AI is a stateful dependency sandbox for coding agents. Think of it as staging for agents: one disposable copy of your stack per agent instead of one shared environment everyone queues for. Integration bugs get caught & fixed inside the agent's own loop, at the cheapest point to fix them, rather than surfacing in review or after the merge.

events.name: Tech Council Summit
events.description: 2026 is the year of enterprise AI deployment. The window for experimentation has closed; the time for ROI is fast approaching. At the WSJ Technology Council Summit, the world's leading enterprise technology executives will debate the accelerated journey from experimentation to value. Key themes include: Balancing CEO demand for rapid AI rollout against the need for modernization of legacy systems, employee adoption & enterprise-wide change managementHow technology leaders can control cost, value, productivity & ROI when the economics of AI are still evolvingMitigating the cybersecurity risks associated with the latest frontier models & operationalizing agentic defenseEvaluating build versus buy, centralized versus decentralized AI governance & striking a balance between horizontal & vertical AI deployment - all at a time when the enterprise software sector is facing significant disruptionReviewing the Trump administration's technology policies & debating their impact on enterprise technology leaders todayHow geopolitical uncertainty can increase the risk of cyber attacksHow technology leadership is evolving to drive business strategyThe summit is built with extensive input from WSJ Technology Council members, & will balance the timeliness & newsworthiness of WSJ live events with the relevance & exclusivity of our peer community. Expect news, peer discussions, real-time polling & unrivaled networking.

events.name: AI & What Makes Us Human
events.description: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.

Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.

events.description: Join 51 Alpha in New York City for an evening exploring prediction markets as the new financial asset class & their growing role across finance, politics, & decision-making. The evening will bring together leaders with deep experience across prediction markets & institutional finance to discuss how the industry is evolving & what greater institutional participation could mean for the future of prediction markets. Following the panel & audience Q&A, join founders, traders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders for a networking mixer. Schedule 4:00-4:30 PM - Networking4:30-4:35 PM - VERIFACT: Investor-backed startup out-of-stealth reveal4:35-5:05 PM - Prediction Markets Panel5:05-5:20 PM - Audience Q&A5:20-6:00 PM - Networking Mixer Presenting Sponsor: Verifact Markets - a platform where people can trade True or False on disputed facts. Think prediction markets, but instead of asking what will happen, we ask what has actually happened. Markets are resolved based on evidence, which anyone can review & contribute. Combining evidence analysis & market signals using a purpose-built AI system (patent-pending) to examine disputed claims at scale. Panelists John Aristotle Phillips - CEO of Aristotle & PredictIt. Phillips is one of the pioneers of modern prediction markets & founded PredictIt, one of the first widely used political prediction markets in the U.S. He has spent decades advancing forecasting markets as tools for better decision-making, public policy, & democratic transparency. A Princeton University graduate, he holds a B.S. in Aerospace Engineering. Dan M. Berkovitz - Vice Chairman for External & Regulatory Affairs at Millennium. Previously, Berkovitz served as General Counsel of the U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission, Commissioner of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, & General Counsel of the CFTC. While serving as CFTC General Counsel, he played a significant role in the formulation & implementation of the Dodd-Frank Act, including the development & implementation of the special rule governing event contracts. He is also a Lecturer in Law at Columbia Law School, where he teaches derivatives regulation. Moderator: Gina Antoniello - is Academic Director & Clinical Assistant Professor at the Tisch Institute for Global Sport at New York University-a leader working at the edge of sport, culture, & social impact. events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works:15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Situational Awareness. Are we in an AI bubble? Circular financing between AI labs & infrastructure players, record market concentration, & capex spending that's outpacing monetization. We're decoding the real risk signals versus the noise, & what it means for how you invest from here. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time. Disclaimer By registering for this event, you'll be added to the Innovest newsletter (innovest.substack.com). You can unsubscribe at any time.

We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works:15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Situational Awareness. Are we in an AI bubble? Circular financing between AI labs & infrastructure players, record market concentration, & capex spending that's outpacing monetization. We're decoding the real risk signals versus the noise, & what it means for how you invest from here. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time. Disclaimer By registering for this event, you'll be added to the Innovest newsletter (innovest.substack.com). You can unsubscribe at any time.

events.name: AI Comes To The Museum
events.description: Join Aboard for a conversation with Hlne Alonso of WonderWay, Spencer Kiser of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, & Danny Reynolds of the Museum of Modern Art as they discuss how museums & other cultural institutions are beginning to use artificial intelligence in both public-facing experiences & behind-the-scenes operations. From visitor engagement & collections to governance, infrastructure, & organizational change, they'll explore where AI is already proving useful, how organizations can design around its limitations, & what thoughtful adoption looks like in institutions built around knowledge, creativity, & public trust. Aboard president Paul Ford will moderate the discussion, followed by an audience Q&A. Afterward, stay for food, drinks, & conversation with the speakers & fellow attendees. About the speakers: Hlne Alonso is the founder of WonderWay, a conversational AI platform that transforms curated cultural knowledge into personalized conversations with visitors. WonderWay is currently being piloted at the MIT Museum as part of a research study with MIT Sloan. Hlne also teaches at NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program, where she explores AI, spatial experiences, & new forms of human-computer interaction. Her career has spanned both cultural institutions-including the American Museum of Natural History, the Wildlife Conservation Society, & Liberty Science Center-and the tech industry, where she served as Chief Design Officer at two Series B startups. Spencer Kiser is Senior Manager of Application Development at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, where he leads the team behind the Met's web platform & APIs, including the new semantic search experience. With over 20 years in cultural institutions, including MoMA & the American Museum of Natural History, his work has spanned in-gallery experiences, mobile development, API architecture, & the Met's Open Access initiative. His path winds through sound: field recording & sound design alongside a coding practice, shaped by NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program & its culture of experimentation & collaboration. Outside work, he enjoys archiving physical media & hacking on hardware & local AI tooling. He lives in New York with his family. Danny Reynolds is an AI enablement leader at The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), where he helps deploy practical AI systems & enterprise technology that support one of the world's leading cultural institutions. Drawing on a background that spans a library & information science degree focusing on archives & records management to more than a decade at Apple, he focuses on the real-world challenges of AI adoption, governance, & organizational change.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Brains In Sync - Neuroscience Of Music, Drugs & Shared Experience
events.description: This is not a dry academic talk. Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. When a room full of strangers moves to the same beat, their brains start to move together too. This talk explores the neuroscience of interbrain synchrony, such as how music, rhythm, & altered states pull separate nervous systems into a shared rhythm, from ritual dance to the modern rave. We'll trace the math underneath the music (fractal structure, wave dynamics) up through the psychology of the dance floor, & into the clinic, where music is increasingly used as a deliberate tool in psychedelic-assisted therapy. Drawing on years inside the cannabis industry & hands-on psychedelic pharmacology research, this talk breaks down what's actually happening in the brain on psychoactive substances: shifts in perception, cognition, & the neurochemistry behind altered states, plus what's driving their growing clinical use in therapy.   Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. Agenda: Doors Open: 6:30 PM Lecture + Q&A: 6:45 PM - 8 PM Open-form networking: 8 PM & onwards Whether you're a parent, student, educator, or just someone fascinated by neuroscience, this is the perfect first night for PhDs & Pints. Smart people. Cold drinks. Big conversations.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week's topic - Anthropic's IPO)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events. Join us on September 10th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Perrin Joel & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in.6:00 - 6:45 TBA6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology. About our Guest Speakers: Margaret Davidson Margaret is a Principal at Company Ventures, where she works with Terrarium's entrepreneurs-in-residence to ideate, validate, & build new health tech companies. She backs founders with a track record of execution who are obsessed with solving hard problems in markets where innovation has lagged. She began her career in global public health as a Peace Corps volunteer in Senegal, later leading digital transformation & workforce programs for the Colorado Community Health Network & founding a nationally distributed retail brand. Margaret has an MBA from Columbia Business School & a BA from Johns Hopkins University. Michelle Wang Michelle is a healthcare investor at Wavemaker 360. Previously, she was an operator across seed to growth & late-stage venture-backed startups, where she helped launch new businesses & grow existing business lines while navigating hypergrowth. She began her career in healthcare banking, where she's supported dozens of transactions raising over $10bn in aggregate funding. Michelle has an MBA from Harvard Business School & a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago. Jessie (Laurash) Gentil Jessie is a Principal at Health Enterprise Partners, a healthcare IT & services focused growth equity firm whose investors include leading hospital systems & health plans across the country. She joined HEP in 2017 while completing her MBA at Columbia Business School. Previously, Jessie was Director of Operations at MediQuire, a venture-backed healthcare data analytics company, & before that was with Evolent Health, where she helped delivery systems build population health management infrastructure. She began her career as a consultant at Booz Allen Hamilton focusing on healthcare policy & reform. Jessie is on the faculty at Columbia Business School & holds a BS in Biology of Global Health from Georgetown University.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape.Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders.Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for. Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey.Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation.Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces. Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers).Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors.Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Bets Over Baghdad
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket. Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: UN Blockchain Week 2026 | Main Conference
events.description: September 16-17  New York City  During UNGA 81  The Most Important Blockchain Event of the Year - Where Global Leaders, Policymakers & Visionaries Shape the Future About the EventIn an increasingly unpredictable world, one gathering rises above the noise as the single most strategic opportunity of 2026: UN Blockchain Week. The centerpiece of the 10-day UN Blockchain Week (Sept 10-19) is this exclusive two-day conference - perfectly timed with the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA 81) & New York Fashion Week. This is not another blockchain conference. This is where senior policymakers, institutional investors, government officials, energy executives, & the world's top builders converge for high-signal dialogue on real-world adoption, nation-state strategy, & the future of finance, AI, energy, & the space economy. The world's leaders will be in New York. The most important conversations in blockchain will happen here. Why This Is the Most Important Event of the Year Unmatched Access - Direct proximity to the global governance class during the one week they are all physically in New York.  High-Signal Programming - Focused, curated content at the true intersection of policy & innovation.  Elite Audience - Institutional investors, heads of state advisors, energy leaders, & technologists already in Manhattan for UNGA.  Real Impact - These are the conversations that influence actual policy outcomes & strategic national positioning. This is the week serious players show up. What to Expect - The Two-Day Conference Day 1 - September 16 Bitcoin, Policy & Institutional Infrastructure Opening Keynote: Blockchain's Role in Global Governance Nation-State Bitcoin Adoption Regulatory Outlook Post-UNGA Season Tokenization of Real-World Assets Day 2 - September 17 AI, Energy, Space & Real-World Impact Keynote: The Convergence of AI & Blockchain AI Agents & Decentralized Systems Blockchain for the Energy Transition The Space Economy & Blockchain Each day delivers 18 hours of world-class content, panels, keynotes, & high-level networking - from morning strategy sessions through late-night discussions. Plus the full 10-day UN Blockchain Week experience (Sept 10-19) featuring 100+ events, panels, workshops, NYFW  Blockchain Runway moments, & side programming across Bitcoin, AI, Energy, Space, & Fashion-Tech. Official After Party - BitcoinPalooza Evening of September 17 (immediately following Day 2 close) The official celebration of UN Blockchain Week. BitcoinPalooza brings together the community for an unforgettable night of music, networking, & Bitcoin culture in the heart of New York City. Open to all conference attendees. Who AttendsCurated audience of 1,000+ visionaries including:  Senior policymakers & government officials  Institutional investors & family offices  Energy executives & sustainability leaders  Blockchain builders, founders & protocol teams  AI & space economy pioneers  Fashion-Tech & creative industry leaders This is where the highest-signal conversations & connections happen. Tickets - Current Advanced Pricing (Ends August 1st at midnight EST) Prices increase on August 1st. This is your last chance to get tickets at current Advanced Pricing rates. events.name: AI & What Makes Us Human
events.description: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.

events.description: How enterprises balance cost, performance, & efficiency as GenAI scales. As enterprises push more GenAI into production, the pressure to control cost & improve performance is intensifying.
